The attackers gained temporary access to the company's internal systems and stole hundreds of sensitive files, including details of eight Royal Air Force (RAF) and Royal Navy bases, such as RAF Lakenheath, Portreath, and Predannack, as well as names, email addresses, phone numbers, car registrations, and other personal data of Ministry of Defence staff members and contractors with some documents labeled “Controlled” or “Official Sensitive.” The stolen data was published on the dark web. A Dodd Group spokesman confirmed the data breach, stating that only limited data had been stolen, and the company had secured and recovered its systems. A Ministry of Defence spokesperson said that they were investigating the alleged leak.

The Shelbyville Police Department in Tennessee, United States, experienced a cyber incident on 15 October 2025 that disrupted its computer systems. An investigation was initiated to determine the cause and scope of the incident. While systems for filing accident and incident reports remained functional, the department informed the public of potential delays as restoration efforts progressed.

The town hall of Ville-Elne in France and a company in Perpignan were targeted by the Qilin ransomware group on 4 and 5 October 2025. The threat actors, claimed responsibility for the incident, which disrupted the internal computer systems of the Ville-Elne municipality, including essential software.  Mayor Nicolas Garcia stated that municipal services were disrupted for a week but were nearly back to normal by 15 October, with no major data loss due to existing backups.

On 2 September 2025, unknown threat actors breached the systems of financial services company Prosper, a peer-to-peer lending marketplace, stealing personal information Social Security numbers, names, government-issued IDs, employment status, credit status, income levels, dates of birth, physical addresses, IP addresses. On 16 October, 'Have I Been Pwned' revealed that at least 17.6 million unique email addresses were affected, which has been confirmed by Prosper.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Between January and July 2025, China-linked APT group Jewelbug (aka REF7707, CL-STA-0049, Earth Alux) targeted a Russian IT service provider, as well as a South American government agency, a Taiwanese software firm, and an IT service provider in South Asia. The group remained in the network of the Russian IT service provider for five months, showing a prolonged, stealthy operation. During the attacks, the threat actor accessed code repositories and build systems, potentially enabling supply chain attacks, and exfiltrated data to Yandex Cloud to evade detection. The attackers performed credential dumping, established persistence via scheduled tasks, and cleared Windows Event Logs to hide traces. Symantec researchers reported the attack on 15 October 2025.

In August 2025, North Korean state-affiliated threat actor Famous Chollima were observed targeting a Sri Lankan organization, published in a report by Cisco Thalos on 16 October 2025. The organization was not deliberately targeted by the attackers, but it had one of the systems on the network infected, because a user was deceived by a fake job offer and installed a trojanized Node.js application called "Chessfi".  Typically, the Famous Chollima uses evasive techniques to steal data and cryptocurrency by duping jobseekers into installing malicious code on their devices. In the attack on the organization, the threat actor utilised BeaverTail and OtterCookie malware strains, which were observed to have merged and displayed new functionality in recent campaigns, including a previously undocumented keylogging and screenshotting module.
Techniques Used: Exploit Public-Facing Application, Phishing, Supply Chain Compromise

Title (Company): Kelowna International Airport - Not available - Not available - Harrisburg International Airport
Description: On 14 October 2025, four airports in the United States and Canada were compromised by an unknown group, including the Harrisburg International Airport in Pennsylvania and Kelowna International Airport in Canada. The attackers breached a third-party software to access the PA system the loudspeaker systems and information screens, broadcasting pro-Hamas messages and insults against US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The attack caused confusion among passengers, with some flights delayed as airport staff struggled to regain control of their systems. Authorities, including the Royal Canadian Mounted Police and the FBI, were informed about the incident and started investigating.

On 9 August 2025, F5 was breached by a nation-state threat actor who gained long-term access to its internal systems, stealing valuable technical data, including parts of its BIG-IP source code, internal vulnerability research, and configuration details for some customers. The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) confirmed the incident compromised parts of F5's internal network and involved advanced, persistent techniques consistent with nation-state operations. The breach was detected in August 2025, and F5 engaged external experts, including CrowdStrike, Mandiant, NCC Group, and IOActive, to assist with the investigation. The company found no evidence that its software build systems or update mechanisms were tampered with, and normal operations remained unaffected. Government agencies and enterprise customers using F5's BIG-IP and related products were urged to apply all recent patches and review access controls. The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned that hackers were using F5 devices to target government networks, presenting an imminent threat to federal networks using F5 products. CISA's Executive Assistant Director for Cybersecurity Nick Andersen encouraged others to identify F5's devices on their network and apply urgent updates, noting that the risk of this vulnerability extends to every organization and sector that's using this product. British authorities also issued an alert urging F5 users to update their software. The incident was publicly disclosed by F5 on 15 October 2025, and reported by various sources, including the US Securities and Exchange Commission, the NCSC, and CISA. Some media reports attributed the attack to the Chinese state-sponsored actor UNC5221 (aka Emissary Panda/APT27).

The Vegetable Marketing Organization (VMO) in Hong Kong detected a ransomware incident affecting parts of its computer systems, including the Cheung Sha Wan Vegetable Wholesale Markets gate and accounting systems, which stored information on approximately 7,000 market users on 13 October 2025. The VMO suspended network operations and disconnected affected servers to contain the intrusion, engaging an external contractor to assist with restoration and investigation. The incident was reported to the Hong Kong Police Force, the Computer Emergency Response Team Coordination Centre, and the Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data on the same day. The VMO announced the incident publicly, stating it would conduct a comprehensive review and enhance its information and network security measures. Market operations continued, with invoicing and payments temporarily handled manually.

Pro-Russian hackers NoName057(16) targeted the German public procurement portal Deutsches Vergabeportal and other public administration websites, causing temporary service disruptions in October 2025. The Federal Office for Information Security (BSI) confirmed the incident, which briefly rendered the affected sites unavailable. The disruption was subsequently resolved, and the BSI informed the public about the incident.

On 23 September 2025, a ransomware attack was carried out by the Obscura ransomware gang against Michigan City, Indiana, affecting a portion of the city's data and impacting municipal employees' online and telephone access. The city was forced to take many systems offline and initially referred to it as a network disruption. Mayor Angie Nelson Deuitch informed the public about the incident on 14 October 2025, stating that the city's focus is on safely restoring systems. A forensic investigation, led by an external incident response team comprising IT professionals from Michigan City and outside agencies, was underway to determine the full scope and impact of the event, with law enforcement involved. The Obscura ransomware gang claimed responsibility for the attack on 14 October 2025, stating they stole 450 gigabytes of data, which they subsequently posted online after their ransom deadline expired.

Since 2024, hackers from a Chinese state-backed espionage group, known as Flax Typhoon, infiltrated a popular software mapping tool, ArcGIS, by turning one of its own features into a webshell. The attackers compromised a portal administrator account for the backend server and deployed a malicious extension, creating a hidden directory to serve as their private workspace. They maintained backdoor access to the system by structuring their requests to appear as routine system operations, evading detection tools, and locking off access to others with a hardcoded key. The attack was discovered by ReliaQuest, who reported it to the public on 14 October 2025. The targeted sector was the software mapping industry, specifically organizations using ArcGIS.

On 5 September 2024, Doctors Imaging Group, a Florida-based radiology practice, was hacked by an unknown entity, who breached the computer networks and had access to nearly 172,000 individuals' sensitive information, including names, addresses, dates of birth, financial account numbers, medical record numbers, health insurance information, and Social Security numbers. The incident was reported to federal regulators on 24 September. On 29 August 2025, they completed the review of the attack and notified individuals.

On 26 September 2025, Avnet, an electronics giant, was breached by a threat actor who accessed a database hosted on an external service in the EMEA region, stealing 1.3TB of compressed data, which included details about the company's operations. The threat actor claimed responsibility for the breach and set up a leak site on the dark web to pressure Avnet into paying a ransom. BleepingComputer reported the incident on 07 October 2025, after being informed by both Avnet and the threat actor. BleepingComputer saw some samples in plaintext form, containing data such as personally identifiable information (PII), which Avnet confirmed, but said that none of them are sensitive information as defined under GDPR. Avnet further stated that most of the stolen data was unreadable without proprietary tools and consisted mainly of historical point-of-sale records, potential sales opportunities, and customer contact details. Avnet informed authorities about the cyberattack and contacted impacted customers and suppliers directly.

On 10 October 2025, a cyberattack was carried out by unknown attackers against the city of Sugar Land, Texas, impacting several online services, including bill pay. The city's internal network infrastructure was breached, but critical infrastructure systems remained operational. Police, fire, and medical services were still available through 911, with an alternative number provided for non-emergency issues. The city worked with state and federal law enforcement to investigate the breach.

On 10 October 2025, a ransomware attack affected 80% of public secondary schools in the Hauts-de-France region with Qilin ransomware, disrupting access to information systems, networks and the internet at the institutions. Despite the incident, classes continued, with only a few digital features remaining inaccessible. The Hauts-de-France Region filed a complaint and implemented corrective and preventive measures to strengthen system resilience.

The Hohen Neuendorf Town Hall in Germany was targeted by unknown threat actors around 7 October 2025, disrupting administrative operations and preventing staff from working properly. The State Criminal Police Office (LKA) launched an investigation into suspected extortion and computer sabotage. Town Hall spokesman Daniel Dinse stated that efforts were underway to restore email services and gradually reactivate individual administrative functions, including the registry and residents’ registration offices. According to local media reports, data collected from citizens over several decades may have been exfiltrated, potentially exposing personal and financial information, although the administration stated it was unaware of any confirmed data leak.

The Paziente Consapevole platform, a private system used by general practitioners in Lombardy, Italy, for issuing patient prescriptions, was compromised around 10 October 2025. Threat actors, reportedly based in Eastern Europe, infiltrated the servers of operator Murex Software, stealing thousands of sensitive medical records. The stolen information was used in a phishing campaign in which citizens received fraudulent emails demanding payment for fabricated healthcare services from a fake Monza-based company, CreditLex Srl. The messages contained genuine personal data and details of medical tests and prescriptions, increasing their credibility. The Milan Prosecutor’s Office opened an investigation into fraud, led by public prosecutor Enrico Pavone and the Postal Police, who took steps to block malicious links and trace the perpetrators. The Lombardy Region stated that no breach had occurred in its central or local healthcare systems, confirming that the compromise was limited to the private platform. The Paziente Consapevole website was subsequently suspended.

On 13 September 2025, a supplier of Dolomiti Energia was breached, which resulted in the loss of confidentiality of some personal data, including names, surnames, supply addresses, tax codes, emails, telephone numbers, meter codes, contract information, and IBANs, belonging to Dolomiti Energia customers. In October 2025, the company, Dolomiti Energia, started to inform its customers about the incident via an email, after initial investigations were carried out. The company stated after an analysis that identity documents (such as identity card or passport) or access credentials to the services are not affected. Dolomiti Energia notified the Authority for the Protection of Personal Data.

Since March 2025, a cybercrime gang tracked by Microsoft as Storm-2657 targeted a range of US-based organizations, particularly employees in sectors like higher education, to gain access to third-party human resources (HR) software as a service (SaaS) platforms like Workday since March 2025. The attackers compromised Workday accounts and other third-party human resources SaaS platforms by using sophisticated social engineering tactics and exploiting the lack of multifactor authentication (MFA) according to a report published by Microsoft Threat Intelligence on 9 October 2025. They found that 11 accounts at three universities were successfully compromised, and then used to send phishing emails to nearly 6,000 email accounts across 25 universities. The criminals used custom-tailored themes in phishing emails, including warnings of illnesses or outbreaks on campus, suggesting that recipients might have been exposed, to trick recipients into clicking phishing links. After gaining access to compromised employee accounts, the threat actor created inbox rules to delete incoming warning notification emails from Workday, hiding the actor’s changes to the HR profiles. Storm-2657 then stealthily moved on to modify the employee’s salary payment configuration in their HR profile, thereby redirecting future salary payments to accounts under the actor’s control, causing financial harm to their victims. Microsoft identified affected customers and reached out to assist with mitigation efforts, sharing guidance for investigating these attacks and implementing phishing-resistant MFA to help block them.

Title (Company): Washington Post - LKQ Corporation - Not available - Cox Enterprises, Inc. - Allianz UK - Barts Health NHS Trust - Oracle - Envoy Air - University of Pennsylvania - Logitech - Dartmouth College - Wits University - Harvard University - University of Phoenix
Description: The CL0P ransomware group initiated an extortion campaign against Oracle’s E-Business Suite (EBS) on 11 July 2025. From 9 August, the threat actor employed CVE-2025-61882 as a zero-day vulnerability to target Oracle EBS customers and successfully exfiltrated significant volumes of data from some organisations, according to a joint report by Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant. On 29 September, CL0P launched a high-volume extortion email campaign directed at affected entities. Oracle subsequently confirmed exploitation of vulnerabilities in its EBS platform and released an emergency patch on 4 October. Confirmed victims include the University of Phoenix (United States), Cox Enterprises (a major US communications and automotive services conglomerate), The Washington Post (US news organisation), Allianz UK (subsidiary of German insurer Allianz), Barts Health NHS (one of England’s largest hospital trusts), Envoy Air (a US regional carrier owned by American Airlines), Harvard University (United States), Wits University (South Africa),  Logitech (Swiss multinational manufacturer of computer peripherals) and LKQ Corporation (American automotive parts manufacturer). CL0P has named additional organisations on its leak site, but many alleged victims have not publicly confirmed whether they were affected.

In September 2025, unknown threat actors stole firewall configuration backups from SonicWall’s cloud service, impacting all users of its MySonicWall cloud backup platform. The stolen data contains configuration data and credentials, albeit the latter are protected by strong encryption. The company notified all impacted customers, released tools to assist with threat detection and remediation, and encouraged customers to check for potential exposure. The incident was made public by SonicWALL on 17 September 2025. Mandiant aided in the investigation, which confirmed that an unauthorized party accessed firewall configuration backup files for all customers who used SonicWall's cloud backup service. In a report published on 10 October 2025, Huntress observed widespread compromise of SonicWall SSLVPN devices across multiple customer environments since 4 October. Over 100 SonicWall SSLVPN accounts across 16 customer accounts have been impacted and, in some cases, there was evidence of post-exploitation activity, with the actors conducting network scanning activity and attempting to access numerous local Windows accounts. On 4 November, the company published a statement that the investigation conducted by Mandiant has been completed and revealed that the malicious activity was carried out by a state-sponsored threat actor and could be isolated to the unauthorized access of cloud backup files from a specific cloud environment using an API call.

Title (Company): Thai Diamond Zebra Electric Co., Ltd.
Description: On 8 September 2025, Thai Diamond Zebra Electric Co., Ltd., a subsidiary of Diamond Electric Holdings, Inc., was hit by a ransomware attack when an unauthorised third-party accessed its network system at around 11:00 a.m. JST, resulting in the encryption of data on local servers and some computers. The company severed its network connections with external networks, stopped using affected servers and computers, and began recovery work. From 9 September 2025 onwards, Thai Diamond Zebra Electric collaborated with a local security specialist firm to investigate the situation and strengthened its system monitoring framework. The incident was made public by Diamond Electric Holdings on 26 September 2025.

On 7 October 2025, an unknown threat actor targeted the security operation centre of Mexico City, the Command, Control, Computing, Communications and Contact Center (C5), which belongs to the Secretariat of Citizen Security of Mexico City (CDMX), and is responsible for critical services including the ambulance office, systems related to the seismic alert and real-time monitoring of thousands of video surveillance cameras.  The attackers targeted the servers, which hosted its content management platform (CMS). The head of the General Coordination of C5, Jos Salvador Guerrero Chiprés, reported that the intrusion was immediately contained without affecting sensitive information or emergency services in the capital.

Unidentified hackers leveraged WhatsApp to target Brazilian government institutions and businesses with a new malware strain called SORVEPOTEL. The malware spread through phishing messages containing a zip file disguised as a legitimate document and was designed to deliver additional payloads collecting banking information. The infection began when users received a WhatsApp message from a compromised contact, after which the malware hijacked their WhatsApp web session and automatically sent the same file to all contacts and group chats. Trend Micro reported the incident on 03 October 2025, identifying 477 infections, 457 of which occurred in Brazil, mainly across government, public service, manufacturing, education, banking, technology and construction sectors.

Suspected Chinese state-linked hackers targeted the Serbian aviation agency and other European institutions in an espionage campaign that began in late September 2025. The operation used phishing emails sent to a Serbian government office, redirecting recipients to fake Cloudflare verification pages before deploying malware. Decoy documents were themed around European government affairs. The attackers employed the Sogu, PlugX and Korplug malware families, tools commonly associated with Chinese state-sponsored actors.
Techniques Used: Content Injection, Phishing, Replication Through Removable Media

Description: Suspected Chinese state-linked hackers breached the computer systems of US law firm Williams & Connolly, which represents several prominent political clients. The intrusion, part of a broader espionage campaign against multiple law firms, exploited a previously unknown software vulnerability to access the firm’s network and target the email accounts of selected attorneys. The operation was assessed to be espionage-motivated.

In mid-September 2025, the Crimson Collective hacking group breached Red Hat's GitLab instance, stealing approximately 570GB of compressed data across 28,000 internal development repositories, including around 800 Customer Engagement Reports (CERs) containing sensitive customer information. The threat actors attempted to extort Red Hat into paying a ransom but received no response. Later, the Crimson Collective partnered with Scattered Lapsus Hunters and ShinyHunters to continue extortion attempts against Red Hat. They released samples of stolen CERs for companies such as Walmart, HSBC, Bank of Canada, Atos Group, American Express, Department of Defence, and Société Française du Radiotéléphone. ShinyHunters announced that they would publicly leak the data on 10 October 2025 if a ransom demand was not negotiated. BleepingComputer reported the incident, and Red Hat confirmed the breach.

On 24 September 2025, the blockchain analysts ZachXBT reported suspicious outflows from SBI Crypto-linked crypto assets denominated in bitcoin (BTC), ethereum (ETH), litecoin (LTC), dogecoin (DOGE), and bitcoin cash (BCH) addresses, in total around $21 million, during the previous week. According to these observations, the stolen funds were transferred to five instant exchanges and deposited into the Tornado Cash crypto mixer. SBI Crypto, a crypto mining platform, confirmed an unauthorized outflow of assets that the company owns, but has been no impact on customers who use their services and that all mining pool functionality is operating as normal. North Korean hackers are suspected to be responsible for the attack.

Title (Company): Legal Practice Board of Western Australia
Description: The Dire Wolf ransomware gang compromised the systems of the Legal Practice Board of Western Australia and exfiltrated sensitive data including health, financial, and personal information of legal practitioners in 21 May 2025. The ransomware gang claimed to have stolen 300 gigabytes of data and published samples on 26 May. The Legal Practice Board of Western Australia, a public sector, independent statutory authority that issues practising certificates and assists the Supreme Court of Western Australia, confirmed the incident.

On 3 October 2025, the messaging platform Discord was breached, which resulted in the personal data of 200 million users being accessed by hackers, including their name, Discord username, email, limited billing information and messages with customer service agents. Credit card information or user communications were not affected. Discord stated on their website that an unauthorized party targeted their third-party customer support services to access user data, with a view to extort a financial ransom from Discord. On 9 October, Discord confirmed that the government-ID photos of approximately 70,000 users were stolen, which their vendor used to review age-related appeals.

On or before 1 October 2025, the J Group ransomware gang breached the systems of Dimensional Control Systems (DCS) Software Solutions, a third-party software supplier used by major companies such as Airbus, Boeing, Nissan, Samsung, and Volkswagen, and claimed to have exfiltrated 11 gigabytes of sensitive data, including legal documents, client-side metadata, config files, and internal procedures, alongside internal documents from Sandvik, DCS’s parent company. J Group posted a compressed folder and a list of allegedly stolen PDF files on their dark web leak site on 3 October to back up their claims.

On 11 September 2025, the Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization (CIRO) discovered that unknown treat actors had comprised internal systems. CIRO proactively shut down some of its systems and immediately started an investigation. Throughout this time, critical functions remained available. The investigation found that registration information for member firms and registered individuals had been exposed, including names, addresses, personal financial information required at the time of registration as well as notes from regulatory investigations, and civil or criminal disclosures. In September 2025, media reported that the data from the hack is circulating on the dark web.

On 18 May 2025, a ransomware attack occurred on Union County in Ohio, impacting over 45,000 residents and employees. The attackers stole information, including Social Security numbers, financial information, driver’s license numbers, fingerprint data, medical information, and passport numbers. The county government detected the ransomware on their network and subsequently hired cybersecurity experts and notified federal law enforcement agencies. The incident was first disclosed publicly via Union County’s data breach notification on 24 September 2025.

On 24 September 2025, Moldova's Central Electoral Commission was breached by Russian state-sponsored hackers, according to Moldova’s Deputy Prime Minister Doina Nistor. The attack occurred just days ahead of a parliamentary election and was part of a wider hybrid campaign by Russia to destabilize Moldova's democracy. By hijacking Wi-Fi routers, attackers directed a flood of network traffic toward the Central Electoral Commission’s infrastructure, attempting a distributed denial-of-service attack. The police chief, Viorel Cernauteanu, informed local media about the attack on 25 September 2025. Doina Nistor reported that the vulnerability had been identified and fixed, securing the electoral commission. The attack occurred just days ahead of a parliamentary election and is believed to be a part of a wider hybrid campaign by Russia to destabilize Moldova's democracy.

Sometime before 3 October 2024, the Banco Hipotecario del Uruguay (BHU -- "Mortgage Bank of Uruguay") was targeted by a ransomware attack, allegedly carried out by the Crypto24 group, who compromised approximately 700 GB of data, including personal client information, accounting records, and legal contracts. The attackers encrypted the stolen data, rendering it inaccessible to the bank, and demanded a ransom, with a nine-day deadline for payment. If the ransom was not paid, they threatened to publicly disclose the information. The attack was reported by BCA LTD to Telemundo, and BHU confirmed the incident, which resulted in their institutional network being taken out of service, affecting online payments and deposits.

Title (Company): Broad River Physicians Group LLC - Passaic Hospitalist Services LLC - Lorain Emergency Physicians LLC - Methodist University Emergency Physicians PLLC - Pensacola Hospitalist Physicians LLC - Aurora Emergency Physicians LLC - Olive Branch Emergency Physicians LLC - Pennsylvania Hospitalist Group LLC - ApolloMD - Trinity Emergency Physicians LLC - The Bortolazzo Group LLC - Passaic River Physicians LLC
Description: On 12 June 2025, the ransomware group Qilin added ApolloMD to their darkweb leak site, claiming to hold 238 GB of files, which were allegedly obtained during a compromise that occurred between 22 May and 23 May 2025. ApolloMD, a business associate to hospitals and health systems, notified patients of 11 physician practices affected by the incident, including Passaic Hospitalist Services LLC, Pensacola Hospitalist Physicians LLC, Broad River Physicians Group LLC, Olive Branch Emergency Physicians LLC, Aurora Emergency Physicians LLC, Passaic River Physicians LLC, The Bortolazzo Group LLC, Methodist University Emergency Physicians PLLC, Trinity Emergency Physicians LLC, Lorain Emergency Physicians LLC, and Pennsylvania Hospitalist Group LLC. The affected data included patient names, dates of birth, addresses, diagnosis information, provider names, dates of service, treatment information, and/or health insurance information, as well as Social Security numbers for some individuals. ApolloMD posted a substitute notice on its website on 15 September 2025 and sent notification letters to affected patients on 17 September 2025. In February 2026, ApolloMD confirmed that over 626,000 individuals were impacted.

On 23 September 2025, the municipality of Forli in Italy experienced an intrusion of its computer systems. No evidence of personal data leakage was found at that time. The municipality activated safety procedures and conducted technical checks, resulting in some digital systems and services being temporarily taken offline.

On 29 September 2025, hacktivists calling themselves 'Cyber Islam' defaced the website of Turkish news provider OdaTV, manipulated the content to show propaganda on the main page, including images of Sheikh Said and organisational militants. They also posted photos of Abu Ubeyde, commander of the Kassam brigades.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Phantom Taurus, a previously undocumented China-aligned nation-state actor, breached ministries of foreign affairs, embassies, diplomatic, and telecom networks in the Middle East, Africa, and Asia since late 2022. The group used specific tactics and extreme stealth to avoid detection, including the use of custom-developed tools and techniques such as the NETSTAR malware suite, which consists of three distinct web-based backdoors. Phantom Taurus targeted political and diplomatic institutions and telecom networks to steal sensitive and timely data around major summits between government leaders or political and economic events. The group's modus operandi also involved exploiting vulnerable on-premises Internet Information Services (IIS) and Microsoft Exchange servers, abusing flaws like ProxyLogon and ProxyShell, to infiltrate target networks.

The Ministry of Health (MINSA) was targeted between 19 and 21 September 2025 in a breach of the Monitoring and Evaluation System of the National Health Plan (SIMEPLANS), which contained public documentation such as regulations, policies and annual planning. The incident did not compromise systems containing patient personal data or health care platforms. MINSA's IT office detected unauthorized access and migrated the system to a new server environment. MINSA confirmed the incident on 25 September 2025 and announced that it would file a formal complaint with the Public Prosecutors Office to initiate investigations.

On 8 September 2025, a ransomware attack was carried out by an unknown treat actor on the municipal housing company in Senftenberg, in the German state of Brandenburg. The threat actor used malware to encrypt data and systems, demanding a ransom for their release. As a result, the IT network was deactivated, and email and telephone communication were restricted. The Landeskriminalamt (state criminal police) investigated the attack due to suspicion of extortion and computer sabotage. According to the housing company's statement, no contact was made with the attackers. Personal data is believed to have been compromised.

The Chinese state-sponsored threat actor UNC5174 exploited a high-severity privilege escalation vulnerability, identified as CVE-2025-41244, in VMware Aria Operations and VMware tools since mid-October 2024. The attackers staged a malicious binary within specific regular expression paths, such as tmphttpd, to escalate privileges on systems running vulnerable software, ultimately gaining root-level code execution on the VM. The vulnerability was reported by NVISO threat researcher Maxime Thiebaut in May and was patched by Broadcom. The attacks targeted various VMware products, including VMware Cloud Foundation, VMware vSphere Foundation, VMware Aria Operations, and VMware Tools. The incident was disclosed to the public by NVISO Labs on 30 September 2025.

On 29 September 2025, the Japanese brewing giant Asahi Group Holdings was breached by the Qilin ransomware group, which caused system failures affecting their shipping and customer service operations in Japan. The company stopped taking orders and suspended call centre operations due to disrupted access to corporate systems. The incident resulted in the temporary suspension of production at 30 factories throughout Japan. On 7 October 2025, Qilin claimed to have exfiltrated financial documents, budgets, contracts, employee personal data, and development plans. Later, the company confirmed that personal data of 1.5 million users belonging to customers, employees and former collaborators are affected.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Since 2022, a Chinese State-Sponsored threat actor, known as Lotus Panda, Naikon or APT30 carried out a cyberattack by distributing a new variant of the PlugX malware targeting telecommunications and manufacturing sectors in Central and South Asian countries including a telecommunications company in Kazakhstan. The campaign was disclosed in a report by Cisco Talos on 23 September 2025. The attackers utilised DLL sideloading, algorithms for payload encryption and decryption, and RC4 keys, similar to the RainyDay and Turian backdoors. The configuration associated with this new variant of PlugX differs significantly from the standard PlugX configuration format. Instead, it adopts the same structure as RainyDay, leading Cisco Talos to assess with medium confidence that this variant of PlugX can be attributed to Naikon.
Techniques Used: Exploit Public-Facing Application, Replication Through Removable Media

Description: On 21 September 2025, Circle K, a convenience store chain, reported a network disruption in Hong Kong, forcing nearly 400 outlets to suspend most electronic payment and loyalty services. Circle K acted quickly to secure customer, employee, and supplier data and worked with law enforcement and third-party forensics experts to determine the cause, scope, and extent of the breach.

On 28 September 2025, a group of hacktivists known as Deface Peru targeted the website of El Peruano, the official newspaper of Peru. The group replaced content with criticism of state authorities. El Peruano regained control of the website after two hours. Deface Peru claimed responsibility for the incident through their Telegram account.

Unknown threat actors infiltrated Healthcare Interactive Inc. (HCIactive), a provider of AI-powered software solutions for insurance enrolment and benefits administration, between 8 and 12 July 2025. The actors exfiltrated files containing protected health information, which included names, addresses, email addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, health insurance enrolment information, medical record numbers, diagnoses, lab results, prescriptions, treatment information, medical images, doctors’ names and health insurance claims information. Suspicious activity was identified within the company’s network around 22 July, prompting an internal investigation that confirmed unauthorised access and data exfiltration.

Title (Company): Directorate General of Taxes and Domains (DGID)
Description: On or before 29 September 2025, the ransomware group Black Shrantac carried out a ransomware attack against the Directorate General of Taxes and Domains (DGID), Senegal's tax administration, resulting in a massive 1TB theft and subsequent leak of sensitive data, including financial and tax information, network and system information, HR information, and legal and administrative information. As a result of the attack, workers within the DGID were warned to not turn on their computers to avoid further infections, and also led to a complete shutdown of the DGID's IT department. The compromised data was partially leaked on the darknet, with DGID confirming the incident, and journalist Bachir Fofana reporting that the incident caused daily losses in the amount of billions of CFA francs (millions of USD).

On 23 September 2025, the hacker group SBERISLAM carried out a DDoS attack on the websites of the major Turkish daily newspapers Milliyet and Hurriyet, resulting in short access problems for users. SBERISLAM claimed responsibility for the incident, stating that the attack was in response to the perceived persecution of Muslim people and the alleged bias of press organizations. The group posted a statement on Milliyet's website, which included photos of Sheikh Said, a leader of a Kurdish nationalist and Islamist rebellion against the early Turkish Republic, and Abu Ubeyde, the pseudonym of the spokesperson of the al-Qassam Brigades, the military wing of Hamas, who had been killed in an airstrike on Gaza City a month earlier. The incident was reported by Milliyet on its website.

On 25 September 2025, CISA issued an emergency directive regarding an ongoing and widespread attack spree involving two actively exploited zero-day vulnerabilities (CVE-2025-20333 and CVE-2025-20362) affecting Cisco firewalls devices, which are widely used across federal government agencies in the United States, at least since November 2024. Cisco assesses with high confidence that this campaign is connected to the ArcaneDoor activity identified in early 2024 carried out by the same Chinese state-sponsored threat group, tracked as UAT-4356 by Cisco and Storm-1849 by Microsoft. The attackers employed advanced evasion techniques, such as disabling logging and intercepting command-line interface commands, as well as manipulating read-only memory (ROM) to persist through reboot and system upgrade. Cisco began investigating the attacks in May 2025 together with the CISA to take immediate action, requiring them to hunt for evidence of compromise, report findings, and disconnect compromised devices immediately after disclosure.

Chinese State-Sponsored Threat Group UNC5221 deployed BRICKSTORM malware in a campaign, which is being used to maintain persistent access to victim organizations in the United States. The campaign started at least in March 2025 and was discovered by Mandiant and published in a report on 24 September 2025. The hackers targeted specialized operating systems like Linux and BSD, focusing on stealing valuable intellectual property and sensitive information related to national security and international trade from legal services, technology, SaaS, and Business Process Outsourcers (BPOs) sectors. In some cases, the attackers maintained access for over a year, exceeding log retention periods, complicating the analysis of initial access vectors. On 4 December 2025,  the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), National Security Agency (NSA) and Canadian Centre for Cyber Security published an advisory outlining the BRICKSTORM malware based off an analysis of eight samples taken from victim organizations and they are attributing the malware to People’s Republic of China (PRC) state-sponsored cyber actors.

On 7 January 2025, the BianLian Ransomware Group breached and stole data from Medical Associates of Brevard (MAB). The attackers subsequently added MAB to their dark web leak site on 23 January 2025 but did not provide any proof of their claims and suddenly went silent. Although the group itself published no proof to their claims, several months later, MAB confirmed the incident in a notification to the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), stating that 246,711 patients were affected by the incident.

On 22 September 2025, the Tacuara group announced that they breached the Electoral Court's online processing platform in Uruguay, allegedly accessing over 620,000 records, including identification data and civic credentials of Uruguayan citizens. The Electoral Court later confirmed the breach.

On 25 August 2025, an intrusion was detected at the Appalachian School Services Centre (CSSA), which paralysed its activities. The incident forced the organization to shut down its digital communications, including IP phones, computers, and Wi-Fi network, to limit the impact after a ransomware attack. Executive Director Jean Roberge informed the public about the attack through an interview with the Courier Frontenac on 27 August 2025. An investigation was underway, led by cybersecurity specialists, in collaboration with the Ministry of Cybersecurity and Digital Affairs, the Operational Centre for Cyberdefense (COCD), Prcicom, and the School Board's Computer Network Management Company.  On 3 September 2025, INC Ransom claimed responsibility for the attack on their dark net forum. On 10 September, personal information belonging to members of the school community was posted on the dark web.

Threat actors with ties to the North Korean threat actor Famous Chollima (aka Contagious Interview) were observed using ClickFix-style lures to deliver BeaverTail and InvisibleFerret malware in a campaign tracked as 'Contagious Interview'. Famous Chollima is suspected to operate as a subset of the umbrella group Lazarus. The latest attack wave was observed in late May 2025. The threat actors targeted marketing and trader roles in cryptocurrency and retail sector organisations. This activity was reported by GitLab Threat Intelligence researcher Oliver Smith on 17 September 2025. On 16 October 2025, Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) published additional details about coinciding Contagious Interview activity observed since February 2025. The TTPs documented for the infection chain by GTIG shares overlaps with the GitLab Threat Intelligence report, including the use of ClickFix techniques to compromise victim machines and the subsequent deployment of the BeaverTail stealer and InvisibleFerret backdoor. In addition, UNC5342, the threat actor GTIG associates with the Contagious Interview campaign, leveraged smart contracts to deposit malware on public blockchains, such as BNB Smart Chain and Ethereum. Known as EtherHiding, this technique takes advantage of the immutability of blockchains as a repository for malware and command and control infrastructure that is resilient to law enforcement takedowns. UNC5342 activity is the first time a nation-state actor has been detected to use this method. In a report published by NVISO Labs on 13 November 2025, identified a new technique for malware delivery leveraging legitimate JSON storage services like JSON Keeper, JSONsilo, and npoint.io.

Madrid-based gas distributor Madrileña Red de Gas suffered an intrusion that exposed customer identification data and Universal Supply Point Codes (CUPS), the unique reference numbers for individual gas meters on 12 September 2025.  Madrileña Red de Gas, which manages over one million supply points across the Community of Madrid, activated internal security protocols and launched a system-wide review. The incident was reported to the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD) and the National Cybersecurity Institute (INCIBE). Affected customers were notified beginning 20 September. The company confirmed that financial details and access credentials were not compromised. Public disclosure followed on 22 September 2025.

In early August 2025, the Russian-speaking ransomware group Qilin claimed to have targeted Welcome Financial Group, a South Korean savings bank, allegedly obtaining 1TB of data. Qilin released samples of the documents on their dark web site, including financial documents from affiliates such as Wellix Capital and Welcome Asset Management. The incident was disclosed by Qilin on 17 August 2025.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: According to a report published on 17 September 2025 by Swiss cybersecurity company PRODAFT, the Iranian state-sponsored hacking group known as UNC1549 has breached 34 devices in 11 telecom firms in an ongoing campaign since at least June 2022, with targets spanning Canada, France, the United Arab Emirates, the United Kingdom, and the United States. PRODAFT links this campaign to the group's use of LinkedIn job lures and MINIBIKE malware. The attackers used bespoke backdoors and tools such as BugSleep, LiteInject, StealthCache, Fooder, Phoenix, CannonRat, and UDGangster to compromise the networks.

On 16 September 2025, the Spanish city of Valencia discovered a breach that affected the irrigation system at the Turia Garden. This attack was carried out from a Russian IP address and exploited a security vulnerability in a device that had been installed for ten years. The municipality took action by isolating the affected equipment, which allowed them to resolve the incident and restore normal functioning of the irrigation system. According to the city of Valencia, the investigation revealed that no other municipal services' equipment was compromised. The incident was disclosed on 22 September 2025.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Since March 2025, a hacker group known as Warlock Group (aka GOLD SALEM, Storm-2603) has been observed by threat researchers to be operating an ongoing campaign utilizing ransomware to target nearly 20 organizations across multiple countries. According to Sophos, which first reported the campaign, victims include anywhere between "small commercial or government entities to large multinational corporations spread throughout North America, Europe, and South America." The group's origins and location are subject to further analysis, with Microsoft stating with moderate confidence that it is a China-based threat actor. Sophos noted that further evidence was necessary to corroborate information about the origin of the group. From 18 July 2025 onwards, Microsoft observed Warlock deploying ransomware, taking advantage of the SharePoint exploit chain ToolShell, initial exploitation of which had been linked to China nexus actors. Warlock's targets included at least one organization in Russia which provides engineering services and equipment to the electricity generation industry, suggesting that the group operates from outside of Russia.

The City of Yellowknife (Canada) had its computer systems breached by unknown actors on 13 September 2025, with the incident affecting access to the municipality's internal systems and several online services including Virtual City Hall, City View, and City Explorer services; the incident further rendered certain city services, such as city email systems, unavailable. The city confirmed the breach on 14 September 2025 in a Facebook post. The following day, the city confirmed that the incident was "ongoing" and that city officials were working with cybersecurity experts to understand the nature and extent of the incident.

On 22 September 2025, the medical biology group Inovie Labosud was compromised, potentially exposing sensitive data of over 3 million patients. The threat actors accessed personal data, including identity, social security, and medical information related to laboratory tests, but no banking coordinates or passwords were compromised. An investigation is ongoing, with no evidence yet on the use of the stolen data. Inovie Labosud notified 3.2 million people who could be affected by the intrusion. A criminal complaint has been filed.

On 2 October 2025, Renault and its subsidiary Dacia announced that they had been victims of data theft by unknown actors targeting a third-party data processing firm used by the companies. As a result, customer phone numbers and addresses of Renault UK customers and Dacia were stolen alongside further information, including names, addresses, emails, phone numbers, and vehicle registrations. Renault confirmed that the breach was an isolated incident and none of its own systems were infiltrated.

On 19 September 2025, a not further specified hack was carried out by unknown actors against the website of Pulkovo Airport in St. Petersburg, Russia, which resulted in temporarily disrupted access. The airport company announced the incident via its Telegram channel, noting that airport operations continued normally despite the incident.

Title (Company): Cork airport - London Heathrow Airport - Berlin Airport BER - Dublin Airport - Copenhagen Airport (CPH) - Münster Osnabrück Airport - Brussels Airport - Collins Aerospace
Description: On 10 September 2025, the Everest ransomware group breached Muse software of Collins Aerospace, an American defence and aviation system manufacturer which provides software services to many airports worldwide, and claimed to have exfiltrated 1,533,900 passenger records and other sensitive data from an insecure FTP server. On the night of 19 September 2025, the systems of multiple European major airports were disrupted. The attack was described as a “cyber-related disturbance” by Raytheon Technologies/RTX, the parent company of Collins Aerospace, which confirmed that it was working to resolve the incident as soon as possible. The incident targeted the aforementioned Muse software, which is used in passenger control (i.e., check-in) and baggage systems at several major European airports, including Brussels Airport, Berlin Airport, Dublin Airport, and Heathrow Airport. As a result, automated systems were completely disabled, forcing airports to conduct all operations manually by implementing emergency plans. This caused significant disruptions, including major setbacks in flight programs and extended passenger lines. The incident was reported by various sources, including the airports themselves, Collins Aerospace, and news agencies such as AFP and BBC. According to Brussels Airport, at least 10 flights were cancelled and 17 were delayed for more than an hour. London Heathrow Airport also reported delays, with over 140 flight delays until noon. Berlin Airport reported 62 delays, while other airports, such as Frankfurt and Zurich, were not affected. As of 22 September 2025, disruptions were still ongoing at certain European airports. On the same day, the EU's cybersecurity agency, ENISA, confirmed that the incident was a ransomware attack and stated that cybersecurity experts had identified the type of ransomware, without disclosing it to the public but stating to Deutsche Welle and Reuters that law enforcement was investigating. On 24 September 2025, the British National Crime Agency detained a 40-years-old man suspected to be involved in the ransomware attack.  While Everest claimed responsibility for targeting Collins Aerospace through their lake site on 17 October 2025, the group further specified its actions on 22 October. In the subsequent statement, Everest admitted to have exfiltrated data on 10 September but denied deploying ransomware or engaging in activities that could have resulted in the disruptions observed from 19 September onwards. To back up this timeline, the group shared screenshots allegedly showing conversations between Everest and representatives of RTX, Collins Aerospace's parent company. Initial statements by ENISA and the UK National Cyber Security Centre had noted that malware used in the intrusion had been identified, suggesting that ransomware may have been deployed, possibly by a separate actor in a colliding intrusion. The security company Hudson Rock noted that the credentials, which Everest claimed to have used for the intrusion, could be traced back to an infostealer infection of a Collins Aerospace employee in 2022.

On 23 September 2025, Mirae N Seohae Energy, a gas supplier in South Chungcheong, South Korea, was targeted in a ransomware attack by Gunra ransomware group, which resulted in the theft of customer information on 2 October 2025. The exposed information included customer names, dates of birth, contact numbers, email addresses, account numbers, and card numbers. Mirae N Seohae Energy reported the incident to the authorities after detecting the infiltration and subsequently confirmed the data breach during the investigation.

Russian state-sponsored hacking groups Gamaredon and Turla have been observed by ESET researchers to be collaborating to deploy the Kazuar backdoor against targets in Ukraine in what is described as an ongoing collaboration. According to ESET's report, published on 19 September 2025, Turla has compromised at least seven Ukrainian systems (of unnamed victims/sectors) since March 2024, while Gamaredon and Turla's collaboration in this ongoing campaign began in January 2025 with Gamaredon's compromise of four systems. While the exact method of infiltration is unknown, ESET describes in its report how several tools believed to be exclusive to Gamaredon, including PteroGraphin and PteroOdd, were used to execute Turla's Kazuar v3 backdoor on an endpoint in Ukraine in February 2025. The attack chain involved Gamaredon deploying PteroGraphin, which downloaded a PowerShell downloader dubbed PteroOdd, retrieving a payload from Telegraph to execute Kazuar. In separate instances in April and June 2025, ESET detected the deployment of Kazuar v2 through other Gamaredon malware families tracked as PteroOdd and PteroPaste. The attackers used the Kazuar backdoor to gather and exfiltrate the victim's computer name and system drives volume serial number to a Cloudflare Workers subdomain.

On 17 July 2025, Survival Flight, a US company providing air emergency medical transportation services, was allegedly breached by WorldLeaks, exposing the name, address, medical treatment information, and health insurance information of certain patients. This information was made public by the company on 12 August in a statement on their website. On 18 September 2025, WorldLeaks added Survival Flight to its breach list, claimed to have acquired 2.8 TB of files.

Between 30 September and 18 October 2023, Fairmont Federal Credit Union, a US-based financial cooperative, was breached by Black Basta ransomware gang, resulting in a data breach that impacted approximately 187,000 people. The incident was not detected until January 2024, which led to an investigation lasting until August 2025; the company disclosed on 17 August 2025 that impacted data included “personal information including, full name, date of birth, address, Social Security number, U.S. Alien registration number, passport number, driver’s license or state ID number, military ID number, Tax ID number, non-U.S. national identification number, financial account number, routing number, financial institution name, credit card/debit card number, security code/PIN number, credit card/debit card expiration date, IRS PIN number, treatment information/diagnosis, prescription information, provider name, MRN/patient ID, Medicare/Medicaid number, health insurance policy/subscriber number, other health insurance information, treatment cost information, full access credentials, security questions and answers, and digital signatures.”

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: On 5 September 2025, Check Point Research identified a new ransomware group named Yurei, which utilized a Go-based, open-source ransomware, Prince Ransomware, for a "fast-growing" campaign utilizing double extortion via file encryption and data theft. Check Point stated that malware samples from the group were uploaded from Morocco, leading the company to assess with low confidence that Yurei was based there.  The Check Point report on the incident from 12 September noted three victims since the group was first observed on 5 September. While Check Point did not elaborate on two of the victims beyond their locations (India and Nigeria), the company stated that the first victim was a Sri Lankan food manufacturing company which had its data stolen and leaked by Yurei.
On 30 May 2025, systems of the town hall of Ostercappeln were breached. The town hall remained paralysed for a week following the network intrusion by criminals.

On 12 September 2025, Qilin ransomware group breached the servers of the City of Waxhaw (North Carolina, US). Cybersecurity experts launched an investigation to secure the servers, and the city shut down its systems as a result of the attack to further limit damage; however, the city did confirm that systems had been breached, stating that local and state cybersecurity officials were investigating how far the attackers were able to get into the city's systems. On its leak site, Qilin claimed to have obtained 619GB of data, including internal documents related to municipal business and police reports.

On 15 September 2025, South Lyon Schools' computer systems were breached by an unknown entity, resulting in the suspension of classes for at least two days. The district's superintendent, Steve Archibald, informed the public about the incident and stated that they were investigating the network interruption with leading information technology experts.

Title (Company): Unspecified think tanks - United States government - US-China Business Council - Academic Organisations
Description: Between July and August 2025, China-linked APT41, also known as TA415, conducted spearphishing campaigns targeting United States government, think tank, and academic organizations focused on US-China economic relations. The group impersonated US Representative John Moolenaar, Chair of the Select Committee on Strategic Competition with China, and the US-China Business Council to deliver infection chains that established Visual Studio (VS) Code Remote Tunnels, enabling persistent remote access without conventional malware. The attackers used legitimate services for command and control, including Google Sheets and Calendar, as well as cloud sharing services like Dropbox and OpenDrive. The phishing emails contained links to password-protected archives, which, when opened, executed a batch script that ran the WhirlCoil Python loader, ultimately establishing a VS Code remote tunnel authenticated via GitHub. The attackers collected system information and user directory contents, sending this data to free request logging services.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: In a campaign originating in early 2025, Iranian hackers known as Nimbus Manticore breached major companies across Europe, targeting businesses in the defence, telecommunications, and aerospace sectors to steal sensitive information. The intrusions started with a fake email invitation to a job application, directing victims to a fraudulent website mimicking well-known companies like Boeing, Airbus, and flydubai. Once logged in, victims were tricked into downloading a malicious file, a compressed ZIP archive containing a legitimate looking program that secretly installed and ran other malicious files, including a backdoor. This was done to take control of the system and communicate with the attackers' servers. The downloaded file contained an evolved variant of the older malware called Minibike, also known as SlugResin, and new variants such as MiniJunk and MiniBrowse, designed to steal important data while avoiding detection. Check Point Research (CPR) reported technical details of the activity on 22 September 2025.

Starting in early January 2025, hackers exploited a zero-day flaw in Zimbra Collaboration Suite (CVE-2025-27915) to target a Brazilian military organisation by sending a malicious email spoofing the Libyan Navy's Office of Protocol, according to a report published on 30 September 2025 by StrikeReady. The email contained a 0KB iCalendar file with a JavaScript file obfuscated using Base64 encoding, which was used to deliver the zero-day exploit. The threat activity was reported on 5 October 2025.

Unattributed hackers compromised the Transparent Administration section of the Italian Municipality of Forio in September 2025. The incident resulted in the loss of published data, documents and information. The head of Sector III, Dr Gabriella Galasso, reported the incident and noted that internal expertise was insufficient to manage recovery.

North Korean Kimsuky group (aka APT43) exploited OpenAI’s ChatGPT to generate deepfake military ID cards for a phishing campaign targeting South Korean defence institutions. The attackers used ChatGPT to create sample images of government and military ID cards, which were embedded in phishing emails posing as official communications. These emails contained a fake ID card and malware used to steal data and enable remote access to victims' systems. Cybersecurity firm Genians reported the incident and confirmed in their report that metadata showed the images were created using ChatGPT.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Unknown threat actors have been observed by Trend Micro researchers to be using legitimate-looking AI tools and software to sneak malware into organizations worldwide, with Trend Micro saying that their telemetry first collected data on 29 August 2025 but that the campaign is ongoing and rapidly spreading. The campaign has been observed targeting hundreds of victims across manufacturing, government, healthcare, and other sectors in the US, India, the UK, the EU, Brazil, and beyond. The attackers used seemingly legitimate productivity and AI-enhanced apps with names like App Suite, Epi Browser, JustAskJacky, Manual Finder, and Tampered Chef to conceal malware. Trend Micro is tracking related malware, which is presented as functioning apps featuring professionally crafted user interfaces and real, working features, as EvilAI. The malware code itself appeared to have been AI-generated and contained little to attract the attention of antivirus and threat detection tools. The operators of EvilAI chose to conceal their malware in new apps with innocuous and generic-sounding titles to try and appear authentic. By combining believable functionality with stealthy payload delivery, AI was reviving classic threats like Trojans and giving them new evasion capabilities against modern antivirus defences. Eric Skinner, Trend Micro's VP of market strategy, commented that the malicious apps were likely being used to set the stage for future exploit activity.

On the evening of 14 September 2025, cybercriminals launched an attack meant to overload the server of the state of North Rhine-Westphalia used for presenting municipal election results. The targeted attack was quickly and successfully prevented by IT.NRW (the State Statistical Office), with the presentation of election results being disrupted for only a few minutes between 6 p.m. and 6:15 p.m. The state criminal office was informed, and an investigation was initiated. According to a spokesman for IT.NRW, the communication, recording, and evaluation of results were not affected, and no one had penetrated the system. The Rheinische Post reported that there were numerous server requests per second, aiming to break down the system entirely, but this attempt was unsuccessful, as it was only a short-term disruption to the presentation.

Title (Company): GoTelemedicina - eMedicoERP - Suiza Lab - Archer Health, Inc. - MedicSolution
Description: Killsec Ransomware Group has been observed targeting the healthcare sector in the Americas by Resecurity Threat Intelligence in a report published on 10 September 2025. In the report, Resecurity describes how, on 8 September 2025, the KillSec Ransomware group claimed responsibility for a compromise of MedicSolution, a software solutions provider for the healthcare industry in Brazil. The attackers compromised an insecure AWS S3 bucket, resulting in data exfiltration, which is believed to have occurred over several months. The stolen data, exceeding 34 GB and comprising over 94,818 files, included sensitive laboratory results reports, medical assessments, X-rays, unredacted patient pictures, and records related to minors. Resecurity reported the incident and identified several affected patients, who were unaware of the breach at the time of disclosure. The KillSec Ransomware group threatened to leak the sensitive data unless negotiations were initiated promptly, with the intention of extorting MedicSolution. Aside from the attack on MedicSolution, days prior, the group had also announced the successful compromise of several other healthcare institutions in the Americas: namely Archer Health (USA), Suiza Lab (Peru), GoTelemedicina (Colombia), and eMedicoERP (Colombia), though the exact tactics used by the group in these compromises, nor the impacts, were not elaborated by Resecurity's report.

Title (Company): FBI - eCheck Background Check System - Google
Description: A loose alignment of members of several criminal networks, referring to themselves as 'Scattered Lapsus$ Hunters', claimed responsibility for gaining access to Google’s Law Enforcement Request System (LERS) portal and the FBI’s eCheck background check system on 11 September 2025. Google confirmed that a fraudulent account was created in its LERS portal, which is used by law enforcement to submit official data requests. However, the company stated that no data was accessed and that no requests were made using the account. At the time of reporting, the FBI had not confirmed the alleged compromise of its eCheck system.

On 19 September 2025, the network equipment vendor Libraesva published a security advisory reporting a previously unknown vulnerability in the company's Email Security Gateway tracked as CVE-2025-59689. According to the advisory, the vulnerability had been exploited in at least one instance that Libraesva with high confidence tracked to an unidentified state entity. Based on the advisory, the bug could be exploited via malicious emails containing specially crafted compressed attachments. Libraesva provided patches to both cloud and on-premise ESG deployments.

Title (Company): Gosuslugi - Central Election Commission (CEC; Russia) - Rostelecom
Description: Ukraine’s military intelligence agency (HUR) carried out a DDoS attack on Russia’s Central Election Commission and other government services in response to voting in occupied Ukrainian regions on 14 September 2025. The operation coincided with Russia’s “unified voting day,” when regional and local elections are held simultaneously across the country. HUR said its DDoS attack targeted the servers of the CEC, Russia’s electronic voting system, the state services portal Gosuslugi and core routers of state-run telecoms provider Rostelecom. Russia confirmed its election-related websites had come under sustained attack. CEC chief Ella Pamfilova told local state media that since the start of the voting on Friday, CEC website was intermittently unavailable but stressed that voting itself had not been affected. Deputy Digital Development Minister Oleg Kachanov confirmed “short-term traffic degradation” on Gosuslugi and the CEC’s digital services but said the remote voting platform functioned as designed.

On 3 October 2025, the town of Fumel in Lot-et-Garonne, France, announced that it was targeted in a ransomware attack claimed by the Malaysian hacking group DragonForce, which encrypted data and demanded payment for access. The attack resulted in the compromise of municipal services, with at least 1,200 intrusion attempts made by the hackers before they eventually gained access via an email. Mayor Jean-Louis Costes confirmed that the town hall refused to pay the demanded ransom and filed a complaint with the gendarmerie as a result of the attack. The restoration process, expected to take at least two weeks, was covered by insurance, estimated to cost around €50,000.

On 13 September 2025, the Uvalde Consolidated Independent School District detected a ransomware attack on its servers, originating from unknown actors, which affected several essential online systems including phones, thermostats, camera monitoring and visitor management systems. The district closed from 15 to 18 September 2025 due to the incident. According to Uvalde CISD's Chief of Communications, Anne Marie Espinoza, the affected systems are "crucial to the safety and security of our schools," hence the closure; meanwhile, incident was reported to the FBI, which initiated a "comprehensive investigation" to uncover the source of the malware and assess whether any sensitive information has been compromised; the investigation was initiated alongside the school district's insurance cybersecurity team and other relevant agencies. On 20 September 2025, Uvalde Consolidated Independent School District announced that the affected systems have been fully restored, and an investigation found no data breach.

Starting on at least 27 August, unknown actors stole data from customers of the South Korean telecommunications company, TK Corp. Following this incident, on 14 September 2025, South Korea's ICT minister, Bae Kyunghoon, urged a cybersecurity overhaul after the breach at KT Corp. exposed major gaps in handling cyber incidents; in the incident, International Mobile Subscriber Identity (IMSI) information was stolen through an illegal "miniature base station," which enabled the hackers to charge unauthorised micropayments to nearly 280 KT subscribers, worth over 170 million won (US$122,400). KT estimated that over 5000 other customers may have had their data compromised, and KT Corp. offered "swift compensation" as a result of the incident.

Starting on 8 July 2025, the Iranian state-sponsored hacker group Handala Hack Team carried out a hack-and-leak operation targeting five journalists with Iran International, including one based in Canada, through accessing their internal communication and server infrastructure. As part of the operation, the group released uncensored photos of government IDs, email address passwords, intimate photos, and videos on their website, which were then amplified via X, Facebook, Instagram, Telegram, and Iranian news websites until early August 2025, according to Canadian officials. The operation was detected by Rapid Response Mechanism Canada (RRM Canada) on 9 July 2025 and was reported in an advisory on 12 September 2025. According to Canadian officials, Handala claimed to have acquired information of thousands of individuals linked to Iran International. The leaked information was further amplified through multiple AI chatbots, including ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Claude, Grok, and DeepSeek, which provided detailed information about the operation, names of affected individuals, and links to released images. The leak increased the risk to the personal safety of the affected staff, and such operations are used as a form of digital transnational repression (DTNR) to coerce, harass, silence, and intimidate those who speak against foreign actors or their interests. Several threat intelligence firms, including Recorded Future and Trellix, assess Handala maintains links with groups, such as Storm-842, with documented connections to Iranian intelligence.

Title (Company): Central Physicians' Appointment System - Not available - Turkish Scholarships Information System (TBBS)
Description: On 11 September 2025, the hacker group Anonymous allegedly launched a cyber attack on official Turkish websites, claiming to have compromised more than 20 sites, including the Central Physicians' Appointment System (MHRS), used to schedule health appointments, as well as the Turkish Scholarships Information System (TBBS), which provides scholarships to international students in Türkiye. Anonymous announced its activities via social media statements.

On 11 September 2025, the Deputy of the Legislative Assembly of Costa Rica, Rodrigo Arias Sanchez, had his WhatsApp account compromised by cybercriminals, as reported by his office and Costa Rican news site La Nacion. The Office of the Deputy warned citizens about possible fraud originating from the compromised account in an attempt to use his identity to scam others.

On 6 September 2025, Banco Triangulo S.A., a Brazilian financial institution, was the victim of a cyber incident which resulted in the theft of financial assets and money from accounts within the bank, as confirmed by Brazil's central bank, which published a security alert the following day. The central bank's alert advised strengthening transaction controls to avoid further incidents, while also advising that all cryptocurrency exchanges related to the incident be blocked.

Title (Company): Panama Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF)
Description: On 5 September 2025, the INC ransomware gang claimed to have breached Panama's Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) stealing over 1.5 TB of data, including emails, financial documents, and budgeting details. The group added Panama's Ministry Of Economy to its victim list on the dark web and provided sample data. On 9 September 2025, the MEF informed the public that an incident of possible malicious software was detected in one of the Ministry's workstations, but note that none of the MEF's central systems and platforms have been compromised and continue to operate as normal.

On 10 September 2025, Bitdefender researchers uncovered that a Chinese APT group, which is not further specified, compromised a Philippine military firm using a new fileless malware framework called EggStreme. The deployed toolset suggests persistent, low-profile espionage by injecting malicious code directly into memory and leveraging DLL sideloading to execute payloads. The EggStreme framework consisted of several components, including a loader named EggStremeFuel and a full-featured backdoor called EggStremeAgent, which could perform reconnaissance, steal data, modify files and delete important files. The malware performed fileless execution and used DLL sideloading to evade detection. Additionally, the attackers deployed a secondary tool named EggStremeWizard and a proxy tool called Stowaway to maintain access and bypass network segmentation and firewall rules.

On 10 September 2025, a breach affecting the London North Eastern Railway (LNER) resulted in unauthorized access to customer contact details and previous journey information managed by a third-party supplier. No bank, payment card or password information was affected. The company urged customers to be cautious of unsolicited communications asking for personal information. LNER informed the public about the incident through a statement on 10 September 2025, and provided further information, including an FAQ, via their website.

ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for an intrusion of Credit Institute of Vietnam, reportedly exfiltrating over 160 million records. The Credit Institute of Vietnam, which operates under the State Bank of Vietnam, maintains credit information on individuals and legal entities nationwide. According to the group, the breach included highly sensitive data such as personally identifiable information, credit payment histories, government and military IDs, tax and income records and debt details of all citizens. The dataset, which ShinyHunters listed for sale on a hacking forum, reportedly also included historical data. The attackers stated they exploited an n-day vulnerability in end-of-life software. ShinyHunters denied involvement from other allied groups such as Scattered Spider or Lapsus$, claiming it to be a sole act.

Unknown threat actors targeted Wayne Memorial Hospital (WMH), a Georgia-based healthcare provider, in a ransomware attack that occurred between 1 May and 30 June 2024. The attackers encrypted portions of the hospital’s data and left a ransom note. The breach potentially exposed the personal information of approximately 163,440 individuals, including names, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, financial account details and medical histories. The incident was reported to the Office of the Maine Attorney General and publicly disclosed by WMH’s legal representatives on 9 September 2025.

Title (Company): Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) - Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC)
Description: The Canadian government confirmed a cyberattack affecting several services - including the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC) and the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) - on 17 August 2024. The breach occurred between 3 and 15 August and exploited a vulnerability introduced during a routine software update to the multifactor authentication (MFA) system provided by 2Keys. The attacker accessed email addresses and phone numbers linked to user accounts protected by the compromised MFA app. Some affected individuals later received fraudulent text messages containing links to a spoofed Government of Canada website. In response, the Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat initiated an investigation supported by external cybersecurity experts and reinstated the MFA service. Authorities stated there was no evidence of further compromise involving personal or sensitive information.

On 5 November 2024, Embargo Ransomware, a cybercriminal group, launched a ransomware attack on Wexford County, Michigan, paralyzing some services and stopping real estate transactions for about half a year at the register of deeds office. The attackers claimed responsibility for the incident, but did not specify a ransom. According to Wexford County Administrator Joe Porterfield, the attack resulted in an estimated financial cost of at least $500,000. The expenses included recovering systems, restoring lost documents, upgrading security, and contracting with a cybersecurity firm. Although no public information was believed to be breached, internal personnel information for 30-35 employees may have been compromised.
