Porterfield informed the public about the attack on 9 September, 2025,.

Title (Company): General Council of Education of Entre Ríos
Description: The Brazilian hacker group Paralord Team breached the website of the General Council of Education of Entre Ríos in Argentina on 18 August 2025 rendering the site inaccessible for one day. The attackers defaced the website by presenting a Brazilian flag, an ironic message, and the signatures of five alleged team members. Hours after the breach, Entre Ríos government confirmed that the website was temporarily out of service while technical teams were recovering the services.

The Peruvian National Police Intelligence Directorate (DIRIN) confirmed publicly that it was infiltrated by the hacktivists Deface Perú, resulting in the leak of thousands of intelligence documents on Telegram on 4 September 2025. The leaked information included data on agent identities, operational plans, electronic equipment and follow-up on members of criminal organizations and armaments. Approximately 1500 officers' names, surnames and personal data were distributed, along with reports on espionage, terrorism, drug trafficking, illegal mining and organized crime. The Ministry of the Interior admitted that the Police Intelligence Directorate was a victim of the attack and announced damage control measures, including activating a contingency plan and suspending services. An investigation was initiated to follow up on the crimes committed and identify all possible perpetrators. The incident was publicly reported on 7 September 2025.

On 9 June 2025, networks of the US City of St. Joseph, Missouri, were breached, resulting in interruptions of its network services for an extended period. The compromise led to the city spending over $1 million on cybersecurity and technology infrastructure upgrades. An investigation, which concluded on 4 September 2025, found that certain files may have been acquired without authorization, and approximately 11,000 people were notified about the potential exposure of their personal information. The City of St. Joseph informed the public about the incident through a notice dated 8 September 2025.

The weekend before 8 September 2025, unknown hackers breached the servers of ARS Hauts-de-France hosting identity data of public hospital patients in the Hauts-de-France region, as well as other parts of France. The attackers impersonated a healthcare professional to gain access to the servers. The Regional Health Agency of Hauts-de-France (ARS) reported that the intrusion was limited to identity data, including names, first names, ages, telephone numbers, and email addresses, but did not affect medical records. The ARS informed the public about the attack on 8 September 2025. The attackers did not claim responsibility for the incident. The incident has no impact on the functioning of hospitals in the region and the region’s digital health services.

Title (Company): School District Five of Lexington and Richland Counties
Description: The School District Five of Lexington and Richland Counties in South Carolina suffered a cyberattack that compromised the personal data of approximately 31,475 individuals on 3 June 2025. Exposed information included names, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, financial account details and state-issued ID numbers. The breach occurred when an external actor gained unauthorized access to the district’s network and exfiltrated files. The incident was disclosed to the Maine Attorney General on 29 August 2025. Local media outlet WISTV reported on 5 June that staff bonuses had been delayed as a result of the disruption. Superintendent Akil E. Ross Sr. notified affected individuals and offered complimentary credit monitoring and identity theft protection. The Interlock ransomware group claimed responsibility for the attack on 24 June.

Canadian online investment platform Wealthsimple suffered a data breach affecting less than 1% of its customers on 30 August. The breach stemmed from a compromised software package provided by a trusted third-party vendor. Threat actors gained access to sensitive customer information, including contact details, government-issued IDs, account numbers, IP addresses, Social Insurance Numbers and dates of birth. No customer funds were stolen and login credentials remained secure. Wealthsimple notified affected users on 5 September.

On 5 September 2025, the personal X account of Italian Defence Minister Guido Crosetto was compromised by unknown threat actors. The Ministry of Defence confirmed the breach via a statement published on Adnkronos, clarifying that the posts made on the account were unrelated to the minister or the ministry.

On 4 September 2025, threat researchers at Lab52 (S2 Grupo) reported that Russian state-sponsored group Fancy Bear (also known as APT28, Forest Blizzard, Sednit and others) deployed a custom backdoor called NotDoor by exploiting Microsoft Outlook. The attackers used a Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) macro that scanned incoming emails for specific trigger phrases such as "Daily Report" to activate hidden functionality. They abused Microsoft's signed OneDrive.exe through a DLL sideloading technique, loading a malicious SSPICLI.dll that disabled Outlook's macro security. The malware copied itself into Outlook’s macro project folder using encoded PowerShell commands, verified successful infection via DNS queries to webhook.site and established persistence through Windows registry changes. It supported remote command execution, file exfiltration, payload delivery and encrypted data exfiltration via Outlook.

The Orleans Parish Sheriff's Office (OPSO) in Louisiana was hit by a ransomware attack on 4 September 2025, that disrupted over a dozen computers but did not compromise the jail’s security systems. The attack was discovered around 8 a.m. when OPSO employees encountered login issues. Sheriff Susan Hutson confirmed the incident in a public statement. OPSO’s IT team, supported by the Louisiana Governor's Office of Homeland Security, Louisiana State Police Cybercrimes Unit, New Orleans Office of Homeland Security and City Hall’s IT department, is working to restore operations, secure systems and investigate the breach. The scope of the intrusion and whether a ransom demand was made have not been disclosed. Qilin ransomware group claimed responsibility for the attack on 13 September 2025 in its darknet site.

Bridgestone Americas, the North American arm of the Japanese multinational tyre manufacturer, was impacted by a cyberattack on 31 August 2025 that disrupted operations at facilities in Aiken County, South Carolina, and Joliette, Quebec. The company stated it contained the incident early, preventing customer data theft or deeper network infiltration. As a result of the disruption, more than 1,000 workers at the Joliette plant were sent home during the shutdown, with some employees experiencing pay delays. Bridgestone confirmed no customer data or interfaces were compromised.

Title (Company): Greenville Electric Utility System (GEUS) - City of Greenville
Description: On 5 August 2025, an unknown ransomware group attacked the city of Greenville's servers, affecting access to police and other records. The city immediately implemented protective measures, isolated affected systems, contacted law enforcement and engaged a third-party cybersecurity firm to mitigate the event and restore services. The attack did not affect the city's emergency 911 service, but some phone lines experienced intermittent outages or busy signals. The Greenville Electric Utility System (GEUS) was impacted and online payments and access to billing information were unavailable. There was no evidence that employee or resident information was affected by the breach. The city filed a catastrophe notice with the Texas Attorney General's office and stated that some systems will not be restored as early as 26 August 2025.

Pittsburgh Gastroenterology Associates was hit by a ransomware attack on 20 August 2025 carried out by the Sinobi group, who claimed responsibility and stated that they had accessed the organization’s internal systems and obtained sensitive patient data, including potentially names, contact details, Social Security numbers, health insurance data, medical records and payment information.

The Safepay ransomware group carried out an attack on Waterford Surgical Center, a physician-owned ambulatory surgery centre in Michigan, around 1 September 2025. The group claimed responsibility, stating that it had accessed internal systems and exfiltrated sensitive data including names, contact details, Social Security numbers, insurance records, medical data and payment information. The centre confirmed the attack but did not comment on whether data had been stolen.

The British automobile manufacturer Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) suffered a major cyberattack that disrupted production at its Halewood and Solihull plants and affected global IT systems on 31 August 2025. Staff were sent home and retail operations were impacted for weeks during a key delivery period. While JLR referred to an “IT security incident,” a Tata Motors filing confirmed global issues. The newly formed hacking group Scatteres Lapsus$ Hunters claimed responsibility for the attack in early September 2025. The production was impacted until October 2025 and the losses due to the weeks-long forced production stoppage are estimated at almost 2.2 billion euros.

Title (Company): Communal Centre for Social Action (CCAS) - Grand Poitiers - Town of Poitiers
Description: The administration for the French greater Poitiers metropolitan area, comprising 40 municipalities, suffered a cyberattack on 29 August 2025, resulting in a computer outage that disrupted several online public services. The incident impacted the City of Poitiers, the Community Social Action Center (CCAS) and the wider Grand Poitiers region. In response, authorities isolated community networks from external communications and mobilized a third-party service provider to investigate the origin and scope of the attack. While the exact nature of the intrusion has not been disclosed, the city confirmed the situation was stabilized by early September. The attack rendered planning applications and library reservations inaccessible online. However, services related to passports, identity cards and civil status were later restored.

In August 2025, Iranian-aligned operators connected to the Homeland Justice persona, associated with the MOIS (Ministry of Intelligence and Security of Iran), compromised a mailbox of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) of Oman. The attackers used this breach to conduct a spear-phishing campaign targeting global governments. The attackers sent emails to multiple government recipients worldwide, disguising legitimate diplomatic communication, with malicious Microsoft Word attachments containing encoded content that was decoded using embedded VBA macro code to deploy malware. The campaign, which was identified by Dream Security's threat intelligence agents, targeted embassies, consulates, and international organizations across multiple regions, including the Middle East, Africa, Europe, Asia, and the Americas. A total of 270 emails were sent, with 104 unique compromised addresses used to mask the true origin of the activity. The attackers exploited the common practice of enabling macros to access content, and the campaign's infrastructure included a compromised Oman MFA mailbox, a NordVPN exit node in Jordan, and C2 infrastructure with the domain screenai.online. The inceident was reported by ClearskySec on X and was analysed by Dream Security, which attributed the campaign to Iranian-aligned operators.

Title (Company): Natural Heritage Expertise and Data Centre (PatriNat) - National Museum of Natural History (MNHN)
Description: On 28 July 2025, the National Museum of Natural History (MNHN) in Paris was victimized in a ransomware attack. The attack resulted in disruptions to the museum's networks, making its cash registers unavailable for the visiting places of the Jardin des Plantes and the Paris Zoological Park. Approximately 100 researchers faced difficulties accessing the institution's databases and its partner, the Natural Heritage Expertise and Data Centre (PatriNat). The attackers reportedly exploited a fault operating on a secondary site of the institution (sonotheque.mnhn.fr) as a gateway to gain access. The National Museum of Natural History filed a complaint with the Paris Public Prosecutors Office, and the investigation was entrusted to the Cybercrime Brigade.

On 29 August 2025, the Interlock ransomware gang claimed responsibility for an attack on Loyola College in Victoria, Australia, compromising the college's information technology system and accessing personal information. The attackers exfiltrated 591 gigabytes of data, consisting of over 430,000 files in more than 35,000 folders, including financial, legal, and private documents, which were published on the darknet. Principal Alison Leutchford informed the college community about the incident on 30 August 2025, stating that cybersecurity experts had been engaged to investigate the extent of the breach. The college reset passwords for all staff, students, and parents, and implemented additional safeguards to protect against future attacks.

WhatsApp patched a zero-click security vulnerability (CVE-2025-55177) in its iOS and macOS messaging clients on 29 August 2025, which was exploited in a targeted zero-day campaign against specific users between May and August 2025. The attackers used this flaw, in combination with an OS-level vulnerability on Apple platforms (CVE-2025-43300), to trigger processing of content from an arbitrary URL on a target's device. Donncha Cearbhaill, the head of the Security Lab at Amnesty International, reported that WhatsApp warned some users they had been targeted in an advanced spyware campaign. WhatsApp advised potentially impacted individuals to perform a device factory reset and keep their devices' operating system and software up to date.

On 30 November 2025, Aras Kargo's servers were breached by an unknown threat actor. The company's cyber security teams intervened, partially bringing the situation under control. Cargo acceptance and delivery operations resumed at branches, although temporary interruptions may occur during the transition period. Aras Kargo informed the public about the attack through a publication on 02 December 2025.

According to a report published on 20 November 2025 by Russian IT company Positive Technologies, the China-linked hacking group APT31 (Violet Typhoon, also known in private industry reporting as ZIRCONIUM/BRONZE VINEWOOD/G0128/Judgment Panda/Red Keres/Altaire/WebFans/Chameleon) has infiltrated Russia's technology sector for years, exfiltrating data from companies involved in government contracting and systems integration. APT31, which is allegedly affiliated with Wuhan Xiaoruizhi Science and Technology Company and the Chinese Ministry of State Security's Hubei State Security Department, has increased its targeting of the Russian tech sector between 2024 and 2025 in a long-term espionage campaign utilising legitimate web services to evade detection by its victims. Despite the increase in attacks since 2024, Positive Technologies states that initial access of the Russian IT sector could date as far back to 2022, where they discovered an unnamed Russian IT company being targeted. According to the report, initial access in at least one incident involved a phishing scam with a cover letter which contained a LNK file that launched a decoy document and CloudyLoader, the CobaltStrike downloader. The group then would deploy decoy files while also launching a malicious library. Once in the victim's systems, Positive Technologies reports that APT31 made an effort to evade detection in their campaign against the Russian tech sector, hence the ability to target the sector for such a long time without detection. For example, the group used a legitimate Tailscale VPN tool to create an encrypted tunnel and establish a peer-to-peer (P2P) network between the compromised host and their infrastructure. The group also utilised legitimate Microsoft dev tunnels tools to disguise traffic as legitimate communication with trusted Microsoft domains, and the group further timed key phases of the operation to coincide with weekends and public holidays to avoid detection, including large-scale intrusions during New Year celebrations of 2023.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Between September and December 2024, Insikt Group observed a threat actor tracked as TAG-144 (aka Blind Eagle, AguilaCiega, APT-C-36, and APT-Q-98) targeting nine Colombian entities in the defence, government, transport, oil, and retail sectors, the unit reported on 26 August 2025. Overall, Insikt Group observed five activity clusters as part of this campaign.  Activities linked to cluster two, utilized legitimate internet services during the staging phase, including the code sharing platforms GitHub, Archive, and Past.ee. C2 IP addresses observed as part of cluster two primarily linked to Colombian ISPs, as well as US hosting providers AS-COLOCROSSING and VULTR. From these nodes, the threat actors sought to control instances of XWorm and primarily ASyncRAT deployed on victim systems. Some government victims were infected multiple times and overlapped with victims of TAG-144 in other activity clusters, indicating lateral movement or broader targeting.  Insikt Group noted possible connections between TAG-144 and a threat group tracked by SCILabs under the heading Red Akodon based on similar targeting patterns and TTPs. While the five activity clusters tracked by Insikt Group differ in certain tools, there also exist significant overlaps between clusters, potentially indicating related and/or evolving campaigns rather than entirely isolated activity.

Unknown threat actors stole $1.5 million from the City of Baltimore by spoofing a city vendor and tricking city employees into changing the contractor's bank account information between December 2024 and March 2025. The attacker submitted a supplier contact form using the name of a legitimate company employee to gain access to the vendor's Workday account. The attacker then submitted multiple requests to change the linked bank account, which were approved by two employees without proper verification. The city's accounts payable department made two payments of over $800,000 and $721,000 to the purported vendor, with the smaller payment being retrieved after the recipient's bank informed them of suspicious activity. The incident was disclosed by the city's inspector general in a detailed report on 27 August 2025.

On 31 August 2025, credit card company Lotte Card detected an intrusion, where malware code was found during a server inspection and an attempt was observed to steal internal data. The company removed the malware and conducted a thorough investigation with outside specialities. Lotte Card reported the incident to the Financial Supervisory Service. The incident was publicly disclosed on 1 September 2025. According to a later analysis, the intrusion already happened between 22 July and 27 August 2025. Lotte Card later confirmed that the compromise exposed the personal data of 2.97 million users with more than 200 gigabytes of data stolen.

Title (Company): Qualys - Elastic - Chanel - Petco - Tenable - Salesforce - Puma - McDonald's - CyberArk - Cato Networks - Proofpoint - Adidas - IKEA - Marriott  - Instacart - BeyondTrust - PagerDuty - TransUnion - Kering (Gucci, Balenciaga, Brioni, Alexander McQueen) - Walgreens - Engie Resources - Disney/Hulu - Rubrik - TripleA - Google - Air France - Fujifilm - Nutanix - Allianz Life Insurance Company of North America - CarMax - Cisco - Salesloft - Instructure.com - Canvas - ASICS - Saks Fifth Avenue - Toyota Motor Corporation - Albertsons - Vietnam Airlines - Home Depot - Stellantis - Republic Services - FedEx - Aeromexico - KFC - UPS - Qantas Airways - Palo Alto Networks - Zscaler - Cloudflare
Description: Between 8 and 18 August in 2025, a previously unidentified threat actor tracked as UNC6395 was linked to a breach campaign that exposed Salesforce customer data through the misuse of OAuth tokens issued via Salesloft Drift integration. It was discovered that all applications with a Salesloft Drift integration are affected. Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant reported on the widespread data theft on 26 August 2025. Moreover, Google is investigating a few Google Workspace accounts that are also impacted. GTIG assesses the primary intent of the threat actor is to harvest credentials. After the data was exfiltrated, the actor searched through the data to look for secrets that could be potentially used to compromise victim environments. GTIG observed UNC6395 targeting sensitive credentials such as Amazon Web Services (AWS) access keys (AKIA), passwords, and Snowflake-related access tokens. UNC6395 demonstrated operational security awareness by deleting query jobs.  On 2 September, the cybersecurity company Palo Alto Networks disclosed a data breach of primarily customer business contact information linked to the Salesloft supply chain attack, but Palo Alto Networks products itself had not been affected. Similar, the cloud security company Zscaler disclosed a breach of customer information linked to the Salesloft compromise. On the same day, Cloudflare announced to be affected by the Salesloft hack and stated that most of stolen information is customer contact information and basic support case data, but some customer support interactions may reveal information about a customer's configuration or may contain other sensitive information. On 21 September 2025, automaker Stellantis confirmed a data breach after a hack on a third-party service provider's platform resulted in the theft of some of its North American customers' contact information. On 22 September, ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for the breach and said to obtained over 18 million Salesforce records, including names and contact details, from the company's Salesforce instance. Later, the company appeared on the leak site of Scattered Lapsus$ Hunters. On 2 October, Scattered Lapsus$ Hunters – a collective of the notorious ShinyHunters, Scattered Spider, and Lapsus$ groups—publicly launched a data leak site threatening to release close to 1 billion records allegedly stolen from the Salesforce environments of dozens of major organizations, including FedEx, Air France and KLM, Marriott, Cisco, and Google Adsense.

The INC Ransom group carried out a ransomware attack against Manesa, a Mexican exporter of auto parts and metal components, on 29 August 2025. The attackers exfiltrated more than 300,000 documents, including contracts, financial information, employee records and customer records, and encrypted internal systems, setting a three-day ransom deadline. Publimetro Mexico reported the incident and verified samples of leaked data such as employee names, corporate minutes and action plans.

Amazon disrupted a watering hole campaign by Russian-linked espionage group APT29 (also known as SVR, Cozy Bear, Nobelium, BlueBravo, Midnight Blizzard and The Dukes) that targeted academics and Russia critics to gather intelligence on 31 August 2025. The attackers used compromised websites to redirect visitors to attacker-controlled infrastructure and trick them into authorizing malicious devices through Microsoft’s device code authentication flow. Amazon’s threat intelligence team detected the activity via custom analytics, identifying domains such as findcloudflare.com that mimicked Cloudflare pages and malicious JavaScript injections redirecting 10% of site visitors. Working with Cloudflare and Microsoft, Amazon isolated affected EC2 instances, blocked malicious domains and tracked attempts to migrate to new infrastructure.

The Austrian Ministry of the Interior (BMI) disclosed on 30 August 2025 that it had been the target of a highly professional and targeted intrusion discovered several weeks earlier. The compromise involved unauthorized access to ministry mail servers, affecting around 100 of approximately 60,000 email accounts. Officials stressed that sensitive citizen data, registers and core police systems were not impacted and that operational capacity remained intact. Interior Minister Gerhard Karner and State Secretary Jörg Leichtfried described the attack as “highly professional” and consistent with patterns typically used by state or state-affiliated actors. In response, affected accounts were isolated, employees notified and external cybersecurity experts engaged. Externally, email communications were restricted as a precaution, temporarily disrupting services such as police press releases.

Title (Company): Lycoming County Department of Public Safety
Description: The Lycoming County Department of Public Safety in Pennsylvania detected ransomware on its network on 12 August 2025, potentially compromising data held by the department. An investigation was launched with support from third-party cybersecurity and forensics consultants, and law enforcement, including the FBI, was notified. The breach may have included drivers’ licence numbers. The incident was publicly disclosed on 28 August after investigators advised against earlier notification.

The Office of the Registrar General (ORG) in Jamaica suffered a cyberattack on 25 August 2025 that primarily targeted the availability of its systems. The technical team activated an incident response plan, contained the threat and launched a forensic investigation, while notifying the relevant authorities. Some services remained temporarily unavailable as of 27 August. The ORG stated that existing security measures helped isolate the attack and limit its impact.

In 2020, an unidentified actor launched a ransomware attack against Tillamook County, Oregon, USA, disrupting its computer systems and website, which were left out of operation as a result of the incident. According to county officials, the incident disrupted the systems of all departments of the county, as well as phone systems. Emergency services remained unaffected. According to County Commissioner Beth Anne Steele, an investigation was initiated with local and state law enforcement, with the Federal Bureau of Investigation offering assistance as well.

The City of Middletown, Ohio (USA) was the victim of a cyber incident by unknown actors on 18 August 2025.  According to the city's administration, which disclosed the incident on its Facebook page, the incident resulted in the disruption of several city services, with many city offices reportedly having no access to computers, email, or phone services. According to media sources, services of the health department were also temporarily disrupted, with access being regained on 20 August. The city meanwhile initiated an investigation alongside local, state, and federal law enforcement.

Healthcare Services Group, Inc. (HCSG), a US-based company providing housekeeping, laundry, dining, and nutritional services to healthcare facilities, suffered a data breach in 2024 that impacted 624,496 people. The breach occurred between 27 September 2024, and 3 October 2024, when hackers accessed company systems and stole files with personal data, including names, Social Security numbers, drivers' licence numbers, state identification numbers, financial account information, and full access credentials. The breach was discovered on 7 October 2024, and the company quickly investigated the incident, notified law enforcement, and implemented new safeguards and staff training. The compromised data was reported to state regulators and major credit bureaus, but details about the attack were not disclosed until later. Impacted individuals received notifications about the breach on 25 August 2025, and were offered 12 months of free credit monitoring and guidance on fraud alerts, credit freezes, and reporting identity theft.

On 26 August 2025, a malicious group of targeted the email server of West Chester Township (Ohio, USA), resulting in unauthorized access to certain systems of the district. The township's public information officer, Brianna Wooten, confirmed the intrusion, stating that the incident was discovered at approximately 6:45 a.m. and a team was assembled to handle the incident, including a forensic investigation seeking to determine the scope and scale of the unauthorized access. The unnamed threat actor, who claimed responsibility for the incident via an email sent to employees, stated that they had stolen two terabytes of information, including personal data of residents and employees.

In mid-November 2023, a ransomware attack was carried out by unknown actors against the city of Huber Heights, Ohio, USA, disrupting city services and prompting the city to declare a state of emergency. According to City Manager Rick Dzik, the ransomware attack resulted in the disruption of the city’s zoning, engineering, tax, finance, utilities, human resources and economic development divisions, and the attack further resulted in the compromising of 6,000 individuals' data and theft of a fraction of those, which was discovered by a data-mining company brought in to investigate the incident. According to Dzik, the city's response to the incident included $800,000 to revamp IT infrastructure and safeguard systems, which was finalized three months after the incident.

China-nexus threat actor UNC6384 aka Mustang Panda carried out a sophisticated espionage campaign aimed at diplomats in South Asia and other organizations around the world. The intrusion method involved using a Captive Portal Hijacking technique, which allowed the user to load up a window that said software or plugin updates were required when accessing the site. When a user clicked on an update check, it connected to a page that appeared to be a legitimate software update site, using an HTTPS connection containing a valid TLS certificate issued by Let's Encrypt. The attacker installed and executed multiple-level malware, including Adobe Plugs.StateCLUGlN, disguised as Exe, signed with a global agent's certificate issued by Cendu Nuuxin Times Technology. The malware implemented the user's custom TForms and disguised them as Microsoft Visual C 2013 redistributable package installations. The ending malware, CanonSTAGER, was launched, providing long-term espionage capabilities through SEC backdoors. Google Threat Intelligence Group made this technical attribution on 25 August 2025.

In June 2025, a threat actor tracked as UNC6040 (later linked to ShinyHunters) executed a sophisticated voice phishing (vishing) attack targeting Google employees. The attackers impersonated IT staff in phone calls to convince a Google employee to authorize a malicious connected application, enabling the exfiltration of business-related information—including contact details, company names, and associated notes—for approximately 2.5 billion Gmail users. Google officially acknowledged the attack on 4 June 2025, but spoke of limited impact noting that user passwords were not stolen. However, the company warned that other information may have been compromised and advised users to take steps to improve account security, such as using the Google Security Checkup and Advanced Protection Program. Following the attack, some users reported being targeted by social engineering scams, with individuals posing as Google employees attempting to defraud them, highlighting the increased risk of identity theft and data leaks. According to an FBI Flash Alert released on 12 September 2025, the threat activity ties in with a broader vshing social engineering campaign by UNC6040 aimed at breaking into victim networks to connect a modified version of Salesforce's Data Loader app to exfiltrate data.

Farmers Insurance, alongside other company affiliates including Farmers Insurance Exchange, was breached by unknown hackers through a Salesforce attack, which impacted 1.1 million customers, on 29 May 2025. The attackers used social engineering and voice phishing (vishing) methods to steal data including names, addresses, dates of birth, driving licence numbers, and the last four digits of Social Security numbers. Farmers Insurance disclosed the breach on 25 August 2025.

Title (Company): Volvo North America - Swedish Municipalities - Miljödata
Description: On 23 August 2025, an extortion attack was carried out by unknown hackers against Miljödata, a data service and system provider for Swedish municipalities. The attackers took over Miljödata's data environment and demanded a ransom of 1.5 bitcoins (approximately €135,000). The attack affected around 200 municipalities and regions, including Skellefte, Kalmar, Karlstad, Mnsters and the Gotland Region. The municipality of Skellefte reported that there was a risk that sensitive personal data belonging to current and former employees, as well as students, may have been exposed in the data breach. CERT-SE, a department within Swedish Civil Contingencies Agency responsible for cybersecurity issues, was informed of the incident and offered advice and support to the affected businesses. The attack was disclosed to the public on 26 August 2025. In September 2025, Volvo North America notified in a data breach notice that they are also affected by the breach, including full names and social security numbers of employees. In mid-September, data of 1.5 million Swedes obtained during the breach was leaked.

On 23 August 2025, Iranian hacktivists known as Promised Revenge infiltrated Internet Rimon, an Israeli 'kosher' internet provider that offers internet filtering services for religious, in particular the strictly Orthodox Haredi, communities. The attack caused disruptions in service, including partial or complete disconnection from the network for many customers. Internet Rimon took immediate action to block it, with the company's technology teams and other leading entities in Israel working to reconnect customers to the service. The incident was reported by Internet Rimon on 26 August 2025.

On 24 August 2025, the State of Nevada identified a breach, which was later confirmed by the state Governor's office. A later investigation revealed that the threat actor had infiltrated the system as early as 14 May 2025. The incident disrupted government websites, phone systems and online platforms, forcing all state offices to close on 25 August 2025. The Governor's Technology Office warned that websites, online services and phone lines could be slow or unavailable as teams worked to restore service. A final report concluded that the incident disrupted state systems for approximately 28 days and The investigation found that 26,408 files were accessed, but only one document contained the personal information of a former employee who has since been notified. According to a report, the incident costed the state $1.5M in total.

In a campaign tracing back to January 2025, an Android spyware app identified as Android.Backdoor.916.origin targeted Russian business executives. Designed to resemble a legitimate antivirus app, the tool poses as software provided or approved by Russian state institutions. The Russia-based IT security company Dr. Web, which reported on the activity on 12 August 2025, described this tactic as a hallmark of cybercriminals looking to trick unsuspecting users into installing malicious programmes.  One version distributed under the name “GuardCB” sought to invoke a link to Russia’s Central Bank, including by using branding reminiscent of the bank’s official emblem. Other discovered modifications disguised the spyware under the names “SECURITY_FSB” and “ФСБ” (FSB). The app, which has no known links to other malware families, was circulated through private messages in instant messengers. While the malicious app does not include any security functions, it purports to conduct malware scans on the device and returns threat detections according to a predetermined pattern. When launched, Android.Backdoor.916.origin requests access to geolocation, text messages, contacts, call lists, media files, the camera and microphone as well as permissions to make calls and work in the background. The malicious app further seeks access to the device accessibility service to deploy key logging capabilities to capture user interactions in instant messengers and browsers, including Telegram, Google Chrome, Gmail, Yandex Start, Yandex Browser, and WhatsApp. Able to connect to a variety of command-and-control servers, the tool allows the operators to exfiltrate information collected through this set of permissions.
Techniques Used: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel, Drive-by Compromise, Phishing

Title (Company): Tokat Mayor Mehmet Kemal Yazolu's official X account
Description: The official X account of the mayor of the Turkish city of Tokat, Mehmet Kemal Yazolu, was compromised on 21 August 2025, with the incident publicly disclosed by the mayor on 24 August. Attackers seized control of the account, which was also used to monitor accounts of a political party leader and members. Mayor Yazolu described the incident as an attempt to undermine the city’s stance and manipulate public opinion, condemning it as vicious and despicable. He confirmed that legal and cybercrime units had been notified and pledged that those responsible would be held accountable.

Elche City Council in Spain suffered a network breach on 25 August 2025, detected when a screen displayed encrypted information, prompting officials to shut down systems to prevent data theft or unauthorized access. The incident affected all municipal departments, including payroll and census, suspending services and preventing around 500 citizens per day from accessing OMAC offices. The City’s Innovation Department and external cybersecurity firms began working with the Centre for ICT Security of the Valencian Community and the National Cryptological Centre to restore operations. A crisis cabinet was convened, and municipal email access was cut off as a precaution. The city council's opposition accused Mayor Pablo Ruz Villanueva of remaining silent and failing to adequately inform the public.

The Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) disclosed on 25 August 2025 that it had suffered an incident affecting systems used to organize transportation for disabled passengers through its Mobility service. The Rhysida Ransomware Group, which later claimed responsibility for the attack, gained unauthorized access to real-time information systems and associated tools, preventing the scheduling or rebooking of trips, though core transportation services were not impacted. All previously scheduled Mobility trips were honoured, with new ride requests temporarily redirected to the Call-A-Ride programme. The threat actors are now reportedly attempting to sell the stolen data for 30 BTC.

US electronics manufacturer Data I/O suffered a ransomware attack on 16 August 2025 that disrupted critical systems for shipping, manufacturing, production and support functions. The company, which supplies components for customers including Tesla, Panasonic, Amazon, Google and Microsoft, reported the incident to federal regulators on 22 August in an SEC 8-K filing. Data I/O took systems offline to contain the breach and is awaiting the outcome of a third-party investigation before notifying potential victims. While no ransomware group has claimed responsibility so far, the company expects the incident to have a material impact on its operations and financial condition. On 4 September 2025, the company's CEO stated that the incident has been completely contained and remediated.

Hacking group Lip-Dochtjan, also known as The Sewn Lips, breached the systems of Iranian satellite communications provider Fannava, gaining access to core Linux operating systems controlling ships’ satellite links. The attackers disabled Falcon, the central programme managing Iran’s maritime communications, disrupting services for 30 oil tankers and 25 cargo ships operated by the National Iranian Oil Tanker Company and Iran Shipping Lines. The incident was reported by Marine Insight on 23 August 2025, with Lip-Dochtjan claiming responsibility in a statement to Iran International.

Title (Company): Nissan's Creative Box Inc. (CBI) - Nissan Motor Corporation
Description: The Qilin ransomware group claimed responsibility for a data breach at Nissan’s Tokyo-based design subsidiary Creative Box Inc. (CBI) in August 2025, exfiltrating 4TB of data. The attackers copied more than 405,000 files, including 3D design data, reports, photos, videos and internal documents linked to Nissan automobile projects. As proof, Qilin published sample files on its dark web leak site, including 3D CAD renderings, financial data, a photorealistic vehicle interior render and images of staff using VR headsets to review designs. The group threatened to release further sensitive material unless its demands were met. The breach targeted CBI’s design workflow, potentially exposing valuable intellectual property to competitors. Hackread.com reported on the incident with screenshots from the leak site.

China-nexus adversary MURKY PANDA, also tracked as Silk Typhoon and Hafnium, has conducted cyberespionage operations since late 2024, targeting government, technology, academic, legal and professional services entities in North America. The group exploits internet-facing appliances for initial access, weaponizing n-day and zero-day vulnerabilities, and frequently deploying web shells such as Neo-reGeorg. MURKY PANDA also employs the low-prevalence malware family CloudedHope, a Golang-based Linux RAT with anti-analysis features. A distinctive tactic is trusted-relationship compromises in the cloud, including intrusions at SaaS and Microsoft cloud solution providers that enabled lateral movement into downstream customer environments. In these cases, the adversary abused Entra ID service principals and delegated administrative privileges to escalate access, exfiltrate emails and establish persistence. CrowdStrike assesses the group’s operations as intelligence-driven and highly sophisticated.

Healthcare provider CPAP Medical Supplies and Services disclosed a data breach affecting more than 90,000 people following unauthorized access to its systems in December 2024. Threat actors maintained access for over a week and may have stolen files containing Social Security numbers and protected health information. CPAP Medical, which supplies sleep apnoea equipment including to US military personnel and families, reported the incident to state authorities and the Department of Health and Human Services. No ransomware group has claimed responsibility, and the company stated it has no evidence that the compromised data has been misused.

French retailer Auchan confirmed a network breach affecting several hundred thousand customer loyalty accounts, exposing personal data including names, contact details and loyalty card numbers. Banking information, passwords, PIN codes and prize balances were not compromised. The breach impacted several hundred thousand customers.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Static Tundra, a Russian state-sponsored group organised under FSB Centre 16 and also known as "Dragonfly," "Energetic Bear," and "Berserk Bear," has been observed by the FBI to be exploiting a 7-year-old vulnerability (CVE-2018-0171) in Cisco routers and switches worldwide, specifically the Cisco Smart Install feature, to execute code or crash devices. According to an FBI Public Service Announcement published on 20 August 2025 discussing Static Tundra's activities, the group has been active since at least 2015. Cisco Talos, which published its own report on the campaign on the same date, assessed that activity related to the campaign had been detected dating back to at least 23 March 2023. The FBI's report states that the campaign was detected "within the past year" prior to its 20 August 2025 disclosure. The FBI reported that the campaign involved the breaching of vulnerable network devices of thousands of US-based critical infrastructure entities. According to Cisco Talos' report, the campaign, which was still active as of August 2025, was observed primarily targeting organizations in the telecommunications, manufacturing, and higher education sectors not only in the US, but also across North America, Asia, Africa, and Europe. Once breached, Static Tundra pulled device configurations containing administrator credentials and details about wider network infrastructure, providing a launchpad for deeper compromises. In some cases, the attackers changed device settings to keep their access to the networks, showing particular interest in systems that help run industrial equipment and operations. The FBI and Cisco Talos both recommended immediately patch devices still running Smart Install or disable the feature if patching is no longer an option.

Orange Belgium, the Belgian branch of the Orange Group, an international telecommunications company, was breached by unknown actors in late July 2025, according to a press release published on 20 August 2025.  According to Orange Belgium's press release, the actors gained unauthorized access to the information of 850,000 customers through breaching one of the company's IT systems; the impacted data included surnames, first names, telephone numbers, SIM card numbers, personal unlocking key (PUK) codes, and tariff plans. Following the detection of the breach, Orange Belgium immediately shut down the affected system, thus blocking access, while the company alerted the relevant authorities and filed a breach notification. Warlock Ransomware Group claimed responsibility for the attack after publishing 4 GB of the stolen data in August 2025.

Pro-Ukrainian hacker group Cyber Anarchy Squad targeted the Russian investment platform Investment Projects, operated by PKR Group, on 17 August 2025. The attackers claimed to have partially destroyed the site’s infrastructure, accessed internal databases and employee documents and published stolen files in an attempt to pressure regulators into imposing fines. The platform reported the incident to state regulators and began restoring its infrastructure. Confirmation of the breach came on 20 August, with the company framing the attack as an effort to undermine Russia’s economy and industry. Investors

On 8 August 2025, US pharmaceutical company Inotiv was breached by a threat actor who gained unauthorized access to and encrypted certain systems and data, impacting business operations. The Qilin ransomware group claimed responsibility for the attack, alleging to have stolen around 162,000 files amounting to 176 GB, and published data samples on their leak site. Inotiv, with the help of external security experts, started an investigation and notified law enforcement authorities. The incident caused disruptions to certain business operations, including databases and internal applications used in business processes, and is expected to persist for some time. Inotiv's IT team worked to restore systems and migrated affected operations to offline alternatives to mitigate outages. The company disclosed the attack in a filing to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on 19 August 2025.

Unidentified attackers breached the order management system of Australian internet provider iiNet using stolen employee credentials, accessing customer information, on 16 August 2025. The breach was detected on the same day and reported by TPG Telecom, iiNet's parent company. Approximately 280,000 active iiNet email addresses, 20,000 landline numbers, 10,000 usernames, street addresses, and phone numbers, as well as around 1,700 modem setup passwords were exposed. TPG Telecom disabled the compromised accounts, brought in external security specialists, and informed the Australian Cyber Security Centre, the National Office of Cyber Security, and the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner about the breach. The incident was publicly reported on 19 August 2025.

The office computer of the leadership of Berlin's Justice Senator Felor Badenberg (CDU) was breached. The attackers stole personal data, including emails and calendar information, which included private appointments and meetings. The hackers, suspected to be the Iranian state-sponsored group “Charming Kitten,” posed as a high-ranking representative of the Central Council of Jews in Germany. They sent a phishing email with a link that was clicked by a Senate administration employee, infecting a computer with malware. The attack was reported publicly on 19 August 2025.

A UK-based contractor for the UK Ministry of Defence, "Inflite The Jet Centre Ltd.," was breached by unknown hackers on or around 10 August 2025, resulting in unauthorized access to the information of roughly 3,700 people, particularly including people resettled from Afghanistan, according to the Ministry of Defence's Afghan resettlement team. Inflite The Jet Centre, Ltd., which provides ground-based services for flights linked to the UK's Ministry of Defence, published a breach notification of the incident, stating that they detected "unauthorised access to a limited number of company emails," which, according to an email sent out by the Ministry of Defence, covered the time period between January and March 2024. While details regarding the scope are yet unclear outside of the particular impact on resettled people from Afghanistan, the BBC reported that the information of military personnel and former government ministers was also impacted in the breach; Inflite, however, reiterated that the information was only limited to email accounts.

According to Cisco Talos, a newly-discovered China-linked APT dubbed UAT-7237, believed to be operating since at least 2022, has been observed infiltrating several Taiwanese web-hosting entities in an ongoing campaign characterized by reconnaissance, credential extraction, and long-term persistent access in victims' systems. Cisco Talos states that the group is likely a subgroup of another China-linked APT, UAT-5918, which itself is connected to other state-linked APTs such as Volt Typhoon; Cisco Talos ties this assessment to the similar TTPs of the groups, as well as similar targeting patterns and dates of activity. According to Talos' reporting on the group's activities, a recent (undated) intrusion of a Taiwanese web-hosting provider indicated that UAT-7237 might be specifically interested in gaining access to VPN and cloud infrastructure. Talos' analysis indicates that UAT-7237 gains initial access by exploiting known vulnerabilities on unpatched servers exposed to the internet; once a target is deemed valuable, UAT-7237 deploys webshells to establish backdoor access and uses a SoftEther VPN client (similar to Flax Typhoon) to maintain this access. From there, UAT-7237 has been observed proliferating within victims' systems, with Cisco Talos hypothesizing that UAT-7237's goal in establishing persistent access is for data theft/espionage.

Title (Company): SPD (Social Democratic Party of Germany) - AfD (Alternative for Germany) - CDU (Christian Democratic Union)
Description: Websites belonging to the CDU, AfD and SPD parliamentary groups in Saxony-Anhalt were temporarily taken offline by coordinated DDoS attacks in August 2025. The Ministry of Infrastructure and Digital Affairs in Magdeburg confirmed the disruptions, citing notification from Germany’s Federal Office for Information Security (BSI). CDU parliamentary leader Guido Heuer said the source of the attacks was suspected to be Russia, though no damage beyond temporary outages was reported. The websites were restored after mitigation measures were applied.

WarLock Ransomware attacked London-based telecommunications provider Colt Technology Services on 12 August 2025, leading to the temporary shutdown of several internal systems, including the customer portal Colt Online and the Voice API platform. As a precaution, Colt took systems offline, causing disruption to support services.  On 15 August, the WarLock ransomware group claimed responsibility, offering a cache of allegedly stolen documents for sale. The group alleged it had exfiltrated around one million files, including financial, employee, and customer data, internal emails, and software development material. Sample data was posted on a hacker forum to support the claim. Colt acknowledged on 21 August that data had been stolen, while WarLock began auctioning files stolen in the incident. Security researcher Kevin Beaumont linked the incident to the exploitation of a remote code execution vulnerability in Microsoft SharePoint (CVE-2025-53770), which had been actively exploited as a zero-day. He reported that Colt’s SharePoint servers had likely been compromised with webshells and taken offline, with several hundred gigabytes of data potentially stolen.

The University of Western Australia (UWA) experienced a cyberattack in early August 2025 that resulted in the unauthorized access of password information for thousands of staff, students and visitors. Upon detecting the breach on 9 August, the university locked all accounts and initiated a system-wide password reset over the weekend. UWA’s chief information officer, Fiona Bishop, stated there was no evidence that data other than passwords had been accessed and the university had received no communication from the attacker. Classes continued without disruption, though students were granted a three-day extension for assessments while login access was restored.

On 14 August 2025, Turkish cryptocurrency exchange BTCTurk reported a security incident in which attackers stole approximately $49 million in digital assets. Over $38.6 million was taken in Ethereum, with the remainder spread across multiple cryptocurrencies. The breach was detected after unusual activity was observed in the exchange’s hot wallets, prompting an immediate investigation and the temporary suspension of deposits and withdrawals. BTCTurk stated that most assets are stored in secure cold wallets and that user funds will not be affected. Law enforcement was notified, and blockchain security firm PeckShield tracked the stolen funds.

A ransomware attack against the Pennsylvania Attorney General’s Office, discovered before 13 August 2025, disrupted its phone and email systems, impairing communication with state residents. While prosecutors continued working on cases, the office’s public website remained inaccessible as of Wednesday morning. Attorney General Dave Sunday announced the incident via social media, noting that Information Technology staff were working around the clock to restore services. The identities of the attackers and the methods used to compromise the networks have not been disclosed. The incident was publicly reported on 13 August 2025. In a statement published on 29 August 2025, the Attorney General's Office disclosed that the attackers demanded a ransom, but no payment was made.  On 21 September 2025, INC Ransom claimed responsibility for the attack by adding Pennsylvania Attorney General's Office to its dark web leak site. On 17 November 2025, the office confirmed in a statement that, in August, they were attacked with ransomware and data has been stolen including Social Security numbers.

Title (Company): Government bodies - Energy distribution company - Unspecified judicial bodies
Description: The Russian-linked hacking group Curly COMrades deployed MucorAgent malware in Eastern Europe, specifically targeting government and judicial bodies in Georgia and an energy distribution company in Moldova. The group’s activity has been tracked since mid-2024. The attackers used advanced techniques, including hijacking a built-in Windows component called NGEN, to stay hidden and maintain long-term access to their victims' computer networks. They also utilized specialized proxy tools like Resocks and Stunnel, as well as methods like Mimikatz and DCSync, to steal passwords and other credentials. The malware was designed to secretly reactivate at random times, making it difficult for security teams to detect and remove the threat. Researchers from Bitdefender informed the public about the attack on 12 August 2025. The attackers' goal was to spy on their targets and steal sensitive information, with their operations appearing to support Russian interests. Bitdefender did not find sufficient evidence for links to any existing threat clusters and decided to track the activity under the new threat actor designation Curly COMrades.

Title (Company): Kimsuky/Velvet Chollima/STOLEN PENCIL/Emerald Sleet fka THALLIUM/Black Banshee/G0094 (Reconnaissance General Bureau)
Description: Individual hackers, operating under the pseudonyms Saber and cyb0rg, leaked 9GB of data from an alleged North Korean stated-sponsored hacker's computer on 11 August 2025. The leak was shared through Phrack, a hacker publication, during its 40th anniversary issue at DEF CON in Las Vegas. The leaked data included tools, logs, sensitive information, and more, which were obtained after the hackers gained access to a virtual workstation and virtual private server used by an individual believed to be linked to Kimsuky/Velvet Chollima/STOLEN PENCIL/Emerald Sleet fka THALLIUM/Black Banshee/G0094 (Reconnaissance General Bureau), a group associated with North Korean state-backed cyber activity. The leak revealed attempts to compromise South Korea's government and its Defense Counterintelligence Command through the VPS, as well as internal documentation, source code, stolen credentials, and command scripts from the operator's workstation. The data was made available for download via DDoSecrets.

Hackers breached the personal data of almost 500,000 women who participated in mass screenings for cervical cancer at Clinical Diagnostics NMDL in Rijswijk in the first week of July 2025. The attackers accessed names and addresses of approximately 485,000 women as well as health professionals, and information concerning referrals. Research agency Bevolkingsonderzoek Nederland informed the public about the attack on 11 August 2025 through their website.

Russia-aligned hackers RomCom (aka Storm-0978 and Tropical Scorpius) exploited a critical WinRAR flaw, CVE-2025-8088, based on a high-confidence assessment by cybesecurity company ESET. The threat actors sought leverage the vulnerability to install various backdoors through specially crafted archive files sent in phishing emails in July 2025. The vulnerability was discovered on 18 July 2025 and disclosed by security researchers from ESET on 11 August 2025, allowing attackers to trick the program into installing malware on users' computers without their knowledge. This allows them to steal sensitive data and install other harmful programs. The flaw was patched by WinRAR in a new update on 30 July 2025.

On 2–3 June 2025, Connex Credit Union in Connecticut experienced a breach by an unidentified attacker, potentially resulting in the unauthorized access or download of files containing names, account numbers, debit card details, Social Security numbers, and government IDs - affecting approximately 172,000 members. The breach was detected on 3 June, prompting an immediate investigation. External counsel for Connex reported the incident to the Maine Attorney General’s Office on 7 August 2025.

On 6 August 2025, Pakistan Petroleum Limited (PPL) detected and contained a ransomware attack attributed to the Blue Locker strain, which targeted parts of its IT infrastructure. PPL activated its internal cybersecurity protocols, isolating affected systems and temporarily suspending some non-critical IT services to prevent further impact. Manual processes were used for financial transactions while a full system scan was conducted. Although the attackers issued a ransom note, PPL made no contact with them and reported no compromise of business-critical or sensitive data. The incident was reported to law enforcement and regulatory authorities, with forensic investigations ongoing to determine the scope of the breach and enhance defences. PPL disclosed the attack in a notice to the Pakistan Stock Exchange on 8 August 2025.

Gers Hospital Centre in France experienced an intrusion, potentially involving ransomware, that disrupted parts of its information system and restricted access to certain professional files on 6 August 2025. To contain the incident, the hospital suspended access to affected files, resulting in limited functionality of some business software, including the Computerized Patient Record. An investigation was initiated, with a dedicated follow-up team meeting daily to monitor the situation. Patient admissions and care services continued without interruption.

North Korean state-backed hacker group ScarCruft aka APT37 launched a cyberattack involving ransomware, labelled VCD, alongside other malicious files. The attackers dropped two versions of their ransom note, one in English and the other in Korean. The incident was reported by analysts at South Korean cybersecurity firm S2W on 8 August 2025.

Title (Company): Unspecified third-party customer support platform - Air France - KLM
Description: Unknown threat actors breached a third-party customer support platform used by Air France and KLM, potentially exposing limited personal information of some customers, including names, contact details, Flying Blue loyalty programme numbers, and the subject lines of service request emails. The airlines stated that their internal systems remained unaffected and that no sensitive data was compromised. The incident, detected and contained with the assistance of external experts, was reported to law enforcement, the Dutch Data Protection Authority and the French CNIL. The breach was disclosed by the airlines in a public statement on 7 August 2025. ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for the attack on the same day. Based on media reports, the underlying compromise was part of a wave of breach attempts by ShinyHunters targeting Salesforce instances with social engineering techniques.

The INC Ransomware Group launched a ransomware attack against the City of Durant (Oklahoma, USA) on 1 June 2025, which resulted in the personal information of private individuals being stolen.  According to the city, the attack was first detected on the same date; it was quickly determined that most of the city's servers were not impacted by the breach. However, the city mentioned that at least one server was found to have been breached, which contained personal information about private individuals who had interacted with the city in the past; this included names and addresses, but also more sensitive information such as social security numbers and financial information. On 17 June 2025, INC Ransomware Group claimed the hack and stated that they had stolen 800+ GB of data from the city, demanding a ransom payment from the city within 48 hours. While the potential leak and its scope is yet unclear, the city sent out a notice on 15 July to citizens who were potentially affected by the breach, informing them of their options to protect their identities. According to the city's notice, the attack resulted in an immediate isolating of the city's servers, thus impacting the functioning of certain card payment systems. Forensic and IT experts were brought in to analyse the scope and depth of the damage. While the city acknowledged the breached database mentioned above, it also mentioned that the city's systems had been successfully isolated, and the damage contained by 9 June 2025.

Title (Company): Administrative Office of the US Courts
Description: An unidentified threat group, widely suspected, according to Politico, to have nation-state ties, breached two systems operated by the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts: the Case Management/Electronic Case Files (CM/ECF) system and PACER, its publicly accessible counterpart. These platforms are used across several federal courts to manage and access case filings, including those in criminal proceedings. The intrusion, which occurred sometime before 4 July 2025, compromised sensitive information such as the identities of informants, sealed indictments, and search warrants. In at least one federal court district, approximately a dozen dockets were altered during the attack. Politico was first to report the breach on 6 August 2025, citing sources familiar with the incident. As reported by The New York Times on 12 August 2025, investigators believe that Russia may have been behind the attack.

On 30 April 2025, a ransomware attack was carried out by unknown threat actors on the internal computer system of the City of Tahlequah (Oklahoma, USA), with the unknown actor(s) targeting an internal server that contained personal information of current and former city employees.  The city's IT department responded immediately, isolating the attack with the help of a forensic specialist. While the city confirmed the unauthorized access to city data, it is unclear to what extent the attackers exfiltrated information stored on the servers. The city notified current and former employees as a precautionary measure. City Administrator Taylor Tannehill informed the public about the incident through a memorandum to city employees in August 2025. The investigation following the intrusion found that no customer information was compromised.

The city of Trier, Germany, reported a suspected DDoS attack that caused partial unavailability of its official website, on 5 August 2025. According to municipal authorities, the attack repeatedly disrupted access to public-facing web services but did not affect internal IT systems, email communications or administrative operations. The city has notified the police and the State Criminal Police Office and countermeasures have been initiated. Residents unable to access online services were advised to contact the city via the 115 hotline during business hours.

Bouygues Telecom, a major telecommunications provider in France, disclosed unauthorized access to personal data from 6.4 million customer accounts, on 6 August 2025. A formal complaint was filed with the judicial authorities and the French data protection regulator (CNIL) was notified. Affected individuals have been or will be informed. Bouygues Telecom did not provide details on the nature of the compromised data or the methods used in the intrusion.

In a recent cyberespionage campaign targeting Ukraine’s government, military and defence sector, threat actor UAC-0099 sent phishing emails impersonating Ukrainian courts to deliver malware-laced archive files via legitimate file-sharing platforms. The campaign was disclosed by CERT-UA and involves a new malware family dubbed Matchboil, used to collect system data and deploy secondary tools including Matchwok (a backdoor for remote command execution) and Dragstare (a stealer that extracts browser data and desktop files). UAC-0099 has been active since at least 2022 and has previously targeted forensic institutions, forestry departments and industrial entities in Ukraine. While CERT-UA did not attribute the attacks to a specific country, the targeting and methods bear resemblance to operations previously linked to Russian state actors.

Title (Company): South Shore Regional Emergency Communications Center (SSRECC)
Description: On 2 August 2025, at 9:30 a.m., the South Shore Regional Emergency Communications Center (SSRECC) in the US state of Massachusetts was breached, leading to a disruption of the centre's computer-aided dispatch software for most of the day. The incident, reportedly involving a common, but fairly new form of malware linked to a group with ties to Russia, was detected when SSRECC staff began experiencing significant issues with its Information Management Corporation computer-aided dispatch software. The disruptions did not affect the ability to manage emergencies, communicate with emergency responders, or receive 911 calls. Executive Director Aaron Smith informed the public about the incident on 2 August 2025. The centre's information technology vendor, Multi Service Provider Global Data Systems (GDS), and the FBI were notified, and an investigation was launched by the Norwell Police Department, the Massachusetts State Police and the FBI. During the attack, dispatchers relied on manual methods of emergency dispatch.

On 5 November 2024, Turkey's Ministry of National Education detected unauthorized access to the driver’s test database, where scores were altered using fake e-signatures. The incident was noticed by the AI-supported warning module 'AlERT' and reported to the General Directorate of MEB Measurement, Evaluation and Test Services. An investigation was launched, and log records and IP addresses were obtained on 7 November 2024. The Ministry of National Education corrected the scores of 91 candidates whose test results had been changed. The incident was reported to the Ankara Chief Public Prosecutor's Office, which led to a follow-on investigation identifying a group specialized in fraudulent e-signings. The gang's leader, Ziya Kadiroglu, also known as 'Ziya Hodja', was arrested on 7 January 2025, and the group dismantled by 23 May 2025. Coordination among the Ministry of Transport and Substructure, the Ministry of National Education, the Ministry of Justice, and the Ministry of Interior led to the indictment of six suspects, including Kadiroglu, who face a combined possible sentence 354 years in prison. The incident was released on 5 August 2025.

In June 2023, during the 12-day war between Iran and Israel, Iranian state-backed hackers and proxy groups, including Imperial Kitten (also known as Tortoiseshell, Cuboid Sandstorm, Yellow Liderc), compromised Israeli targets. Shortly after the beginning of the war on 13 June 2025, Imperial Kitten purchased conflict-themed domain names, such as nowsupportisrael.com and supportisraelfunding.com, from NameCheap, which were used to host phishing campaigns using the Evilginx framework. The attackers targeted Hebrew-speaking victims with petition forms offering support for Israel. The group deployed the RemCosRAT remote access Trojan malware to selected targets. The incident was reported by SecurityScorecard’s STRIKE threat intelligence team on 5 August 2025, who analysed over 250,000 messages exchanged by 178 Iranian proxy and hacktivist groups on Telegram. This revealed that the attackers aimed to intimidate civilians, undermine Israeli morale and amplify Iran's wartime narrative. Imperial Kitten was identified as one of the most active initiators in the attack.

On 24 July 2025, unknown threat actors stole basic profile information of users registered on Cisco.com by targeting a company representative with a voice phishing (vishing) attack. This allowed them to gain access to a third-party cloud-based Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system and steal personal and user information, including names, organization names, addresses, Cisco-assigned user IDs, email addresses, phone numbers, and account metadata such as creation dates. The incident was disclosed by Cisco on 5 August 2025.

Russian State-sponsored Hackers are suspected to have hacked the Dutch public prosecution department's internal systems between June and July 2025. The affected systems contained sensitive information on ongoing police investigations, court cases, and personal data on staff. The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) issued an alert about vulnerabilities in Citrix network devices (CVE-2025-5349, CVE-2025-4365, as well as a critical vulnerability, CVE-2025-5777, dubbed "CitrixBleed 2") used by the department in June. The department applied the relevant security updates seven days later, on 24 June. The prosecution department ultimately took its systems offline on 17 July, until then allowing threat actors potential access to the system for at least three weeks. The attribution to Russian hackers is based on the Dutch newspaper AD claiming to have spoken to well-established sources within justice confirming the Russian origin.

Ukrainian military intelligence, specifically the Ukrainian secret services (DIU), carried out an intelligence collection operation on the Russian nuclear submarine Knyaz Pozharsky, which had officially entered service at the end of July 2025. The operation allegedly stole secret data including crew lists, combat instructions, technical diagrams of weapons systems, operational plans, survival measures, and technical reports. This incident was disclosed to the public by Ukrainian military intelligence, which posted screenshots of the documents. Moscow did not officially confirm a related data breach.

CL-STA-0969 was observed in multiple incidents targeting the telecommunications industry in Southwest Asia between February and November 2024. Palo Alto Networks is currently tracking this activity as CL-STA-0969 and heavily overlaps with activity attributed to China-nexus APT group Liminal Panda tracked by CrowdStrike. This activity includes attacking and leveraging interconnected mobile roaming networks. No clear evidence of data collection or exfiltration from the investigated systems and networks was found, nor any attempts to track or communicate with target devices within mobile networks. However, the threat actor behind CL-STA-0969 maintained high operational security and employed various defence evasion techniques to avoid detection. The actors deployed several tools within the compromised networks and set up communication capabilities that provide resilient remote control for future objectives.

On 29 July 2025, the website of the city of Lützen was disrupted by a coordinated DDoS attack. The incident began at approximately 8:15 a.m., when anomalies were detected on individual customer systems, followed by a severe overload of central proxy servers that rendered multiple websites inaccessible. The website operator confirmed that the disruption was caused by a deliberate and coordinated DDoS campaign, aimed at overwhelming the infrastructure with excessive traffic to force system outages. Countermeasures were promptly implemented and proved effective, with services stabilizing later the same day.

Title (Company): Maccabi Tel Aviv - Israeli Premier League - Hapoel Tel Aviv - Hapoel Jerusalem
Description: On 2 August 2025, hackers based in the Gaza Strip launched a coordinated cyber attack against several prominent Israeli sports websites, including those of the Israeli Premier League, Hapoel Jerusalem, Maccabi Tel Aviv and Hapoel Tel Aviv. The attackers defaced the targeted websites with a message reading “Time is running out” and temporarily took some sites offline, leaving them inaccessible or displaying blank pages. The tone of the defacement suggested a political motive, with indications of alignment to a Palestinian group. As of reporting, normal access to the affected websites had not been fully restored.

Genoa Community Hospital, also known as Genoa Medical Facilities, in Nebraska, disclosed a data breach on 1 August 2025 following the discovery of unusual activity in an employee’s email account in March 2025. The breach potentially exposed sensitive patient data, including names, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, financial account details, medical treatment or diagnosis information, and health insurance data. The hospital stated that it was not aware of any misuse of the compromised information and did not report receiving any extortion demands. Notification letters were sent to affected individuals; however, the total number impacted was not disclosed.

Between 2024 and July 2025, the Russian state-linked threat actor Secret Blizzard conducted a sophisticated espionage campaign targeting foreign embassies in Moscow. Using an adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) position at the ISP level, likely facilitated by Russia’s lawful intercept infrastructure (e.g., SORM), the threat actors deployed a custom malware named ApolloShadow to maintain persistent access and harvest intelligence. Microsoft Threat Intelligence identified that ApolloShadow enabled the installation of malicious root certificates under the guise of Kaspersky antivirus, allowing TLS/SSL stripping and enabling credential theft. The campaign involved redirecting victims to actor-controlled domains through captive portals, triggering the download and execution of ApolloShadow. Once executed, the malware checked for privilege levels, prompted users for elevated access, and installed certificates to facilitate further compromise. It also altered network settings and created a persistent admin account. Microsoft assessed that Secret Blizzard’s AiTM position allows it to intercept and manipulate internet traffic of foreign diplomatic entities in Russia.

Highlands Oncology Group in Arkansas was compromised by the Medusa ransomware gang between 21 January and 2 June 2025, resulting in unauthorized access to files and systems affecting 113,575 individuals. The breach was discovered on 2 June 2025, prompting an investigation and notification to affected parties. On 19 June 2025, Medusa listed Highlands on its data leak site, demanding $700,000 for data deletion or download, with a deadline set for 21 July 2025. Highlands reported the incident to the Maine Attorney General’s Office on 1 August 2025 and disclosed the ransomware attack on its website.

Title (Company): Unspecified Government Agencies  - Curaçao Tax Authority
Description: Between 15 and 19 July 2025, multiple government agencies in the Caribbean part of the Kingdom of the Netherlands experienced significant disruption following a series of cyberattacks. The Curaçao Tax Authority was among the affected institutions, with officials confirming the use of ransomware. Upon detection, one of the agency’s systems was taken offline to contain the attack. Authorities reported that no confidential data was lost and that the online tax portal remained operational, though telephone and in-person services were temporarily suspended.

On 20 January 2025, Northwest Radiologists and Mt. Baker Imaging in Washington State were targeted by a network intrusion attack, which was discovered on 25 January 2025. The attackers compromised the confidentiality of approximately 348,118 individuals' personal and medical information. This includes first and last name, address, telephone number, date of birth, email address, Social Security number, driving licence or state identification card number, treatment or diagnosis information, provider name, medical record number or patient identification number, health insurance information, and treatment cost information. Northwest Radiologists notified the affected individuals six months later, on or after 25 July 2025, and offered complimentary credit monitoring and identity protection services to those affected. The incident was publicly disclosed by Northwest Radiologists on 1 August 2025.

On 14 July 2025, unknown hackers infiltrated Seoul Guarantee Insurance (SGI), Korea's largest comprehensive guarantee insurance firm, and disrupted the systems with ransomware. Key services, including issuing and verifying guarantee insurance policies through its website, were down for at least four days, and it is still unclear whether the attackers stole sensitive data.
