While the Chinese Embassy in Sarajevo firmly denies any allegations regarding their involvement in the incident.

Criminal actors compromised the systems of US-based OnePoint Patient Care, a pharmacy specializing in hospice and palliative care, exposing the personal data of 795,916 individuals between 6 and 8 August 2024. The breach affected names, addresses, medical records, diagnoses, prescriptions, and, for some, Social Security numbers. OnePoint detected suspicious network activity on 8 August, initiating an investigation and containment measures with forensic experts. The incident, while not affecting operations, was later linked to the Inc Ransom ransomware group, which leaked stolen data after the company declined to pay the ransom. Impacted individuals have been advised to monitor credit and financial activity for suspicious transactions. OnePoint notified their customers on 21 October 2024.

In October 2024, Stormous ransomware group compromised the Transak company, which provides an 'onamp' service for many famous blockchain companies, by exploiting a data leak caused by employees using laptops for non-work purposes, affecting some 93,000 unique users, including passports, ID cards, and personal photos, and is now trying to negotiate with the company, demanding $30,000 to remove the stolen data, which includes classified private documents, government identifications, addresses, financial statements, and personal photos of users, with the company classifying the damage as 'low or moderate' due to the lack of sensitive information such as social security numbers and credit card details, and the CEO, Sami Stairt, stating that the company is not interested in negotiating with the ransomware group.

Various sources reported that Hackers have used the vulnerability (CVE-2024-47575) to compromise FortiManager devices since at least 23 September 2024. A possible vulnerability in FortiManager first became public in a Reddit conversation on 19 October 2024, after Fortinet may have privately notified these individuals. On 23 October, cybersecurity researcher Kevin Beaumont published a post on the Medium website naming a vulnerability in the FortiManager protocol. In the same post, Beaumont criticized Fortinet's reluctance to disclose the vulnerability and attributed the exploitation to nation-state actors. The following day, 24 October 2024, Fortinet published the vulnerability notification for the first time. On the same day, Mandiant also published its technical report and wrote that over 50 devices had been compromised since at least 27 June 2024. The vulnerability allowed a compromised FortiManager device to issue arbitrary commands. Mandiant attributed this incident to the group UNC5820, which exfiltrated the configuration data of the FortiGate devices managed by the compromised FortiManager.

Unknown threat actors hacked the Ministry of Education and Science (MEC) data center of Paraguay on 21 October 2024, compromising all its data center, with services and systems dropped, and demanded 16 Bitcoins (approximately 1,076,910 dollars) in exchange for restoring the system. However, the MEC denied the ransom request. According to officials, all information held in the data centre, including data of administrative officials, teachers, the Single Student Registry (RUE) and the entire Educational Information and Management System of the MEC, is at risk due to the lack of backup copies, the situation is under control, and computer technicians are working to replenish the service throughout 22 October 2024 gradually.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: According to a report by IT security firm Cisco Talos Intelligence, on 23 October 2024, the hacking group TA866 (also known as Asylum Ambuscade) gained access to the networks of private and public targets in various countries beginning in 2022. The hacking group gained initial access via malicious spam or advertising in 2022 and 2023. It also used a variety of malware, including WasabiSeed, ScreenShotter and AHK Bot, as well as the persistent backdoors Resident, CSharp- Streamer RAT, Cobalt Strike, and Rhadamanthys in 2023. In early 2024, the hacking group used Cobalt Strike and CSharp-Streamer RAT in WarmCookie/Bad  The targets included manufacturing, government, and financial services, mainly in the United States but also in Canada, Germany, the United Kingdom, Italy, Austria, and the Netherlands.

Unknown hackers defaced the websites of Bold Medya and Turkishminute, displaying the names of those who lost their lives in the coup attempt of 15 July 2016, on 23 October 2024. The two websites are associated with the exiled Turkish cleric Fethullah Gülen and his organization.

Unknown threat actors compromised the Winnebago Public School district in Northeast Nebraska, disrupting their phone and internet services, on Monday, 21 October 2024, forcing the district to cancel classes on Wednesday, 23 October 2024, and send students home early on Tuesday, 22 October 2024, with parent-teacher conferences still scheduled for Thursday, 24 October 2024, from 2 p.m. to 6 p.m., KTIV disclosed in a report on 23 October 2024.

Bloomberg News reported on 22 Oct 2024, citing confidential documents and European government officials involved in the matter, that Russian hackers gained access to the network of the Georgian electricity distribution company Telasi from late 2019 to early 2020. The Russian hackers read emails from Telasi employees and watched them using the company's internal cameras.  This cyber incident was part of a Russian state espionage campaign against Georgia intending to cause sabotage if the Georgian government did not act in Russia's interest.

Unknown threat actors compromised the servers of Japanese auto parts supplier Yorozu in October 2024, encrypting them. The company isolated all affected systems from the internet and internal networks. Ransomware group RansomHub claimed to have stolen 849 GB of data, including customer contracts and documents from HR, accounting, and technical departments, and published screenshots of the documents on their leak site as proof. The data theft has not been officially confirmed by Yorozu. The company's Incident Response Team is working with external cybersecurity specialists to investigate the incident.

Beginning on 10 October 2024, unknown hackers disrupted the Portuguese Agency for Administrative Modernization (AMA) network with ransomware. Parts of the network were still inaccessible five days later.

Unknown perpetrators compromised the computer network of the Clairefontaine-en-Yvelines town hall, France, on 14 October 2024, forcing the IT systems offline to secure data. The town hall's operations were disrupted, leading to the closure of the building and halting all administrative services. While no encryption was detected, data theft from municipal databases was confirmed, prompting concerns about the possible leak of personal information. Citizens have been advised to remain cautious of suspicious communications. The town hall, in partnership with its IT service provider, is working to restore its systems.

Bloomberg News reported on 22 October 2024, citing confidential documents and European government officials involved in the matter, that Russia's state-sponsored hacking group Turla gained access to Georgia's foreign ministry network and stole data from April 2020 to January 2021.  The hacking group stole data from seven Georgian officials, including a current deputy foreign minister and the Georgian ambassadors to the European Union and the United States. The hacking group also collected data from Georgian embassies and consulates in Cyprus, the Baltic states, Russia, South Korea, Azerbaijan and Canada. From November to December 2020 alone, the hacker group stole data 114 times, accumulating 21.1 GB.

Bloomberg News reported on 22 October 2024, citing confidential documents and European government officials involved in the matter, that an unnamed hacking group from the Russian Main Intelligence Directorate (GRU) compromised multiple computer systems at the oil terminal in Batumi in October 2019. Some of the compromised computer systems also included the smart cameras.

Bloomberg News reported on 22 October 2024, citing confidential documents and European government officials involved in the matter, that Russian hackers gained access to a large number of email accounts at the National Bank of Georgia from 2019 to 2020. The hackers were able to read confidential correspondence. This cyber incident was part of a Russian state espionage campaign against Georgia intending to cause sabotage if the Georgian government did not act in Russia's interest.

Unknown threat actors, allegedly IntelBroker, EnergyWeaponUser and zjj, breached the systems of Cisco, a networking hardware and software manufacturer, on 6 October 2024, and exfiltrated data belonging to it and its customers, including Github projects, Gitlab Projects, SonarQube projects, source code, hard-coded credentials, certificates, customer SRCs, Cisco confidential documents, Jira tickets, API tokens, AWS Private buckets, Cisco Technology SRCs, Docker Builds, Azure Storage buckets, Private & Public keys, SSL Certificates, and Cisco Premium Products, as well as the production source code of a large number of organisations, including Vodafone Australia, National Australia Bank (NAB) and Microsoft, according to claims posted by IntelBroker on a popular dark web hacking forum, which Cisco has acknowledged and is currently investigating. The attackers gained access to a DevHub environment, which was publicly accessible and contained software code and scripts, among other things, for customers. The instance has since been taken offline. Cisco has confirmed that data was leaked that was not intended for public download, but states that this does not include any financial data. The investigation is still ongoing, and the network equipment provider states that it is proactively approaching affected customers. On 16 December 2024, IntelBroker leaked 2.9 GB of data belonging to Cisco on the Breach Forums platform. The leaked data included sensitive information from Cisco products and services, such as Cisco ISE (Identity Services Engine), Cisco SASE (Secure Access Service Edge), Cisco Webex, Cisco Umbrella, Cisco IOS XE & XR, and a Wireless LAN Controller software image. IntelBroker claimed this partial leak was intended to prove the legitimacy of the breach to potential buyers. The fate of the remaining 4.5 TB of data remains uncertain.

The BianLian ransomware group claimed on 16 October 2024, that it gained access to Boston Children's Health Physicians (BCHP) and stole certain files starting at least on 10 September 2024. The BCHP incident notification stated that an unnamed BCHP IT provider detected suspicious activity on its network and subsequently informed the BCHP on 6 September 2024. On 10 September 2024, the BCHP also discovered unauthorized activity in limited portions of the network. Working with an IT security firm, the unauthorized access on 10 September 2024, was confirmed, as was the extraction of certain files. The stolen files included current and former employee, patient, and guarantor information such as names, Social Security numbers, addresses, dates of birth, driver's license numbers, medical record numbers, health insurance information, billing information, and/or limited treatment information.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Between 17 and 21 October 2024, LulzSec Black, a hacking group, allegedly carried out six cyberattacks targeting government services and private companies in Cyprus, including the government’s main website, the Electricity Authority of Cyprus, Bank of Cyprus, telecommunication company Cyta, oil company EKO, and Hermes Airports, with the initial attempt on Hermes Airports' website being averted on 17 October, according to communications director Maria Kouroupi. The attacks were reportedly politically motivated, citing Cyprus' relationship with Israel as a factor. The cybersecurity firm Odyssey had warned of the imminent attack earlier in the week, stating that the group 'Moroccan Soldiers' had expressed their support for LulzSec Black in these operations. The targeted systems would have included Cypriot infrastructure, specifically government, financial, and critical services, which may have been at risk of service disruptions, data theft, or system compromises. The attacks caused disruptions at Larnaca airport, with long queues forming, while Paphos airport was less affected. The government’s main website was offline for a few minutes on Sunday, but was restored. Authorities, including police spokesman Christos Andreou and Deputy Minister Research Nicodemos Damianou, reported that the situation has normalised, and upgrades to control systems are being carried out. The Commissioner of Communications and head of the Digital Security Authority George Michaelides did not confirm whether there had been attempts to steal data and said the hackers’ motives and targets were not yet discussed. Cybersecurity experts, including Eleftherios Antoniades, Dinos Pastos, and Yianna Danidou, believe the attacks were a 'show of force' and a possible precursor to more significant attacks in the future, highlighting the need for improved cybersecurity measures in Cyprus.

Title (Company): Cooperative of Exploitation and Distribution of Pharmaceuticals Brittany Atlantic (CEPR)
Description: Unknown threat actors compromised the Cooperative of Exploitation and Distribution of Pharmaceuticals Brittany Atlantic (CEPR) in a cyber attack that began on Saturday, 19 October 2024, targeting the online control system for receiving medicine orders, affecting pharmacies in Brittany, Centre-Val de Loire, Pays de la Loire, and Nouvelle Aquitaine, with Orange Cyber Defense teams working to counter the attack, and the CEPR planning to file a complaint, as disclosed by the Regional Health Agency of Brittany on 21 October 2024.

Title (Company): Fukuoka Airport - Not available - City of Nagoya - Yamanashi Prefecture - Liberal Democratic Party (Japan) - Not available
Description: Pro-Russian hacker group NoName057(16) launched a series of high-impact DDoS attacks against Japanese organizations, transportation, private companies, and government entities from 15-17 October 2024, in response to Japan's increasing militarization and its involvement in US-led military exercises. The attacks, which targeted over 40 Japanese domains, including the website of Japan's ruling political party, the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), caused disruptions to various websites, including a website in Yamanashi prefecture that was difficult to view for about four hours on 16 October 2024. The hackers also claimed to have attacked domestic airports, bus companies, and harbors. The attacks were launched after the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation expressed concern over Japan's rising defense budget and development of pre-emptive strike capabilities. The Minister's Security Security Center is collecting information to prevent further damage, and the country's counter-cyber crime agencies have launched an investigation into the breach.

Russian hacktivists compromised the water system of Stanton, Texas, a small utility serving a population of 2,700, in 2024. According to a CSO Online report, the attackers breached the utility’s network, gaining access to a human-machine interface (HMI) and manipulating its settings. Due to the threat actors' inexperience, they only managed to randomly change settings, leading to the loss of some untreated water.

North Korean IT worker from the state-sponsored fraud group NICKEL TAPESTRY stole proprietary data in mid-2024, the U.S. cybersecurity firm Secureworks reported in a report on 16 October 2024. The report is basically about a campaign by the North Korean state-sponsored group NICKEL TAPESTRY, in which North Korean information technicians are deliberately infiltrated into Western companies in order to generate income for the North Korean state afterwards, for example, by demanding ransom for stolen data.

Unknown threat actors launched a ransomware attack on the Schaffhauser Berufsbildungszentrum (BBZ) in Switzerland on 2 October 2024, exploiting a security vulnerability in the firewall to block access to several IT systems and demand a ransom. The attack was discovered on 3 October, and the school, in collaboration with internal and external experts and the police, took technical measures to protect the IT infrastructure from further attacks. The incident was reported to the Schaffhauser Polizei, the Bundesamt für Cybersicherheit, and the kantonalen Datenschutzbeauftragten. The school's IT systems are currently being restored, and an analysis of the attack is ongoing to determine the extent of the damage and develop measures to prevent future cyber attacks. The incident did not affect the IT systems of the Kanton Schaffhausen. The school informed employees, parents, students, and partner companies about the cyber attack, and the school's operations, including classes, resumed normally on 21 October 2024, after the autumn break.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: The hacker group 'Crypt Ghouls' launched a wave of ransomware attacks targeting the Russian economy, particularly focusing on energy and mining companies, financial services, and large retail chains, as disclosed on 19 October 2024. The group utilized a range of tools in addition to the ransomware of the LockBit 3.0 and Babuk strand, including Mimikatz, XenAllPasswordPro, PingCastle, AnyDesk, and various proxy services, to gain persistent access to compromised systems. The typical attack began with the use of stolen VPN access credentials, often obtained from subcontractors, allowing the attackers to remain undetected in the system for weeks, exfiltrating sensitive data using tools like MiniDump. The attacks culminated in the widespread encryption of all accessible data, including deleted files and virtual machines on ESXi servers. The tactics employed by Crypt Ghouls bear a strong resemblance to those of other ransomware groups, such as MorLock, BlackJack, and Twelve, leading experts to suspect a possible exchange of knowledge and resources among these groups.

Unknown threat actors caused a network outage at the Bartow County School System in Georgia, USA, taking down its websites, online access and email, affecting around 14,000 students, in October 2024. Recovery efforts by the school district remained ongoing as of 18 October 2024, according to Alisha Evans, Bartow communications coordinator.

The ransomware gang Medusa Ransomware Group compromised the Providence Public School District in the US state of Rhode Island during September 2024. The group leaked information about students, including sexual misconduct allegations, special education records, and vaccine histories, after the school district did not pay a $1 million ransom demand. The over 337,000 leaked files, which include details about district investigations into serious complaints, as well as the names and home addresses of students, teachers, and parents, were uploaded to Telegram. The breach was first detected on 11 September 2024.

Title (Company): Uttarakhand IT Development Agency - Disaster recovery centre in Bengaluru
Description: Unknown threat actors breached networks of the disaster recovery (DR) centre in Bengaluru, managed by a private company. Pivoting from this entry point to the Uttarakhand IT Development Agency's (ITDA) data centre in Dehradun, the threat actors deployed ransomware, forcing the shutdown of 192 government websites in the state, as reported by Nitika Khandelwal, director of ITDA, on 18 October 2024. A show-cause notice has been issued to the company managing the DR centre, following chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami's directives. As of 18 October 2024, 160 of the affected websites have been restored, while 32 remained offline due to outdated systems and expired software licences.

Unknown threat actors compromised Sofinco, a subsidiary of the French bank Crédit Agricole specializing in consumer loans, exposing personal data including postal and bank details, as well as copies of identity documents, affecting a small quantity of its 11 million customers. The breach, which was detected on 16 October 2024, targeted one of Sofinco's partners.

The Hunters International ransomware gang compromised Omni Family Health, a nonprofit organization providing healthcare services to communities in California. The group obtained personal information of nearly 470,000 current and former patients and employees in the breach. Omni Family Health discovered the intrusion on 7 August 2024, following claims that information was taken from its systems and leaked on the dark web. The data breach may have exposed varying personal information, including names, addresses, Social Security numbers, dates of birth, health insurance details, and medical information. The Hunters International ransomware gang claimed responsibility for the attack, stating they stole 2.7 terabytes of data, which was released on 23 August. The incident was officially disclosed by Omni Family Health on 19 October 2024.

On October 18, 2024, the official X account of EigenLayer, a restructuring protocol, was hijacked by unknown threat actors, who launched a fake airdrop campaign, directing users to request EIGEN tokens through malicious links. Sector experts, including Blockchain detective ZachXBT and Polygon Labs CISO Mudit Gupta, quickly warned users about the scam through Telegram and other channels. The attackers shared multiple posts, including a 'last call' message, attempting to fool users.

Unknown threat actors compromised systems of the Mexican airport group OMA in October 2024, the company disclosed in a public report on 18 October 2024. The incident had no negative impact on the business, as back-up systems were used, and did not affect the operation of the 13 airports in Mexico operated by OMA, including those of Monterrey, Acapulco, Mazatlan, Culiacán, Durango, Reynosa, San Luis Potosí, Tampico, Torreón, Zacatecas and Zihuatanejo. On 5 November 2024, the hackers leaked 2.2TB out of an alleged 3TB of stolen data, after not receiving a ransom.

On 16 October 2024, the North Korean hacker group Citrine Sleet exploited a series of vulnerabilities in the smart contracts of the Radiant Capital loan protocol, manipulating smart contracts on two blockchains, BNB Smart Chain and Arbitrum, and gaining access to three private keys of signatories to a multi-signing wallet, which controlled the functions of the protocol, resulting in the theft of about $51.5 million from protocol users. The attack was initially reported by De.Fi, another security company, who warned users of the attack through a post on X, clarifying that changes to smart contracts had taken place fraudulently. In response to the attack, security company Ancilia inadvertently posted a link to a wallet drainer, while trying to assist victims, which was promptly removed after the community noticed the error. The incident was widely reported and commented on by security experts, who highlighted the importance of clear and transparent information by security companies, and the need for a strict verification protocol and responsible communications. Radiant Capital claimed to be aware of the problem and took steps to cooperate with several security experts, including Mandiant, SEAL911, Hyperactive, ZeroShadow and Chainalysis, to investigate and resolve the crisis. On 6th December, the Radiant Capital released a summary of the technical report by Mandiant on Medium including an attribution of the attack to the North Korean hacker group Citrine Sleet.

Unknown threat actors compromised the Municipality of Sorso's servers, data, and equipment over the weekend of 12-14 October 2024, paralysing the administration and creating many inconveniences, especially for essential services, such as the Protocol and the Anagraphe, the Carabinieri disclosed on 16 October 2024. The attack was reported by Mayor Fabrizio Demelas, who stated that the administration is taking action to solve the problems. Computer experts estimated that a normalization of the situation is expected within 24-48 hours. Reports suggest that the attackers encrypted municipal data, further complicating recovery efforts. Authorities have not disclosed whether a ransom has been demanded or paid.

Cisco Talos researchers observed Russia-linked threat actor RomCom (aka UAT-5647, Storm-0978, Tropical Scorpius, UAC-0180, UNC2596) targeting Ukrainian government agencies and Polish entities in a new wave of attacks since at least late 2023. In the recent attacks, RomCom deployed an updated variant of the RomCom RAT dubbed ‘SingleCamper. The infection chain consists of a spear-phishing message delivering a downloader consisting of either of two variants: “RustyClaw” – a RUST-based downloader, and a C++ based variant we track as “MeltingClaw”. The downloaders make way for and establish persistence for two distinct backdoors we call “DustyHammock” and “ShadyHammock,” respectively. The group uses multiple tools and malware languages (GoLang, C++, RUST, LUA) to establish long-term access for espionage, possibly followed by ransomware deployment for disruption and profit.

Unknown hackers carried out a massive cyber attack on the Johannesstift Diakonie, the largest confessional health and social enterprise in the region of Berlin and northeast Germany, on 13 October 2024, encrypting the central servers in a ransomware attack. This encryption of the central servers led to disruptions at 80 sites, including eleven clinics, and it further temporarily disrupted the operation of hospitals in Berlin and Wittenberg, with service at all locations returning two days later.

Cybercriminals compromised the University of Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne in a cyberattack on 10 October 2024, resulting in the disclosure of personal data of students and staff, including names, first names, university e-mail addresses, photos, and student status, affecting approximately 73,000 people, according to a hacker who claimed the attack on a hacking forum and published some identity photos, Numerama disclosed the attack on 15 October 2024.

Unknown threat actors, suspected to be Israel, compromised Iran's government institutions, nuclear industry, fuel distribution and transport networks, municipalities and ports, in a massive cyber attack on 12 October 2024, amid escalating Middle East tensions. The attack, which was described as 'unprecedented and enormous' by Abolhassan Firouzabadi, former secretary of the Supreme Council of Iran for cyberspace, resulted in the theft of a large amount of information. The attack was reportedly a surgical strike, involving sophisticated malware engineered to evade detection, and was likely designed to cripple multiple layers of Iran's infrastructure. The attack was attributed to Israel due to the country's history of cyber offensives against Iran and its vested interest in destabilising Iran's infrastructure. The incident was reported by various sources, including Iranian officials and cybersecurity experts, and was described as a 'precision strike' on Iranian systems. The attack has raised concerns about the escalating cyber warfare between Israel and Iran, and the potential for similar attacks on other countries.

An alleged state-nexus actor chained three zero-day vulnerabilities in Ivanti Cloud Service Appliance (CSA) devices, specifically CVE-2024-9380, CVE-2024-8190, and CVE-2024-8963, to gain unauthenticated access to the CSA, enumerate users, and attempt to access their credentials. The actor then used obtained credentials to exploit a command injection flaw and deploy a web shell. The first exploitation was reported on 13 September 2024. Ivanti warned of the vulnerabilities and recommended customers to upgrade to CSA 5.0.2 to fix the issues. The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added the vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, ordering federal agencies to fix the vulnerabilities by 10 October 2024. On 1 July 2025, the French cyber security authority ANSSI released a report detailing the exploitation of the zero-day chain against French entities. First detected in September 2024, ANSSI observed activities associated with the campaign again in November 2024, possible leveraging a second CSA exploitation chain, linking CVE-2024-8963 with a CVE-2024-9379 (an SQL injection vulnerability in the CSA admin web console, disclosed in October 2024). ANSSI attributed the campaign to an intrusion set it tracks as Houken, which overlaps with UNC5174, a potential access broker for China's Ministry of State Security. For the French targets ANSSI identified as part of the September 2024 campaign, UNC5174 sought to deploy a Monero cryptocurrency miner. Confirming a practice previously observed for UNC5174, ANSSI noted efforts by the intrusion set to self-patch the exploited vulnerabilities on compromised devices, in an attempt to avoid cohabitation with other threat actors and obscure its entry vector.

Unknown threat actors launched a cyber attack beginning on 22 September 2024, against Schumag AG, a German precision engineering company, exacerbating the company's financial difficulties and forcing it to file for self-administered restructuring at the Aachen District Court on 11 October 2024. The attack led to production outages, delayed revenues, and unexpected cost burdens, ultimately contributing to the company's insolvency after 194 years. The company's CEO, Stefan Lepers, and the company's official statement disclosed the attack and its impact on the company's restructuring plans.

The systems of Calgary Public Library Systems were compromised by unknown actors on 11 October 2024 forcing the library to close earlier "to mitigate potential effects of the attack". The incident affected the library's website as well as servers and library computers which were shut off out of caution. It was not initially clear whether user or employee data was accessed by the threat actors as the investigation is ongoing.

A Russian state-sponsored hacking group of the Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR) gained access to small businesses' Microsoft Teams accounts in 2023, a joint advisory from the FBI, the National Security Agency (NSA), Cyber National Mission Force (CNMF), and the United Kingdom’s National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC-UK) reported on 10 October 2024. The hacking group used Microsoft Teams accounts to send spear-phishing messages posing as tech support. After successfully gaining access to the Microsoft Teams accounts of unnamed small businesses in this way, the hacking group targeted government agencies, technology and manufacturing companies, and non-governmental organizations.

Unknown threat actors compromised the computer system of Family Medical Center in Mount Airy, a U.S. health care sector, in a ransomware attack discovered on 9 March 2023 and publicly known in September 2024. The attackers accessed the system, but there was no evidence of a breach as all files' records were encrypted and unintelligible to the hackers. The office paid a ransom to the criminals to return the encrypted files with an encryption key to unlock them. The FBI and Maryland Department of Health were informed, and the practice has since increased the security on its computer system to prevent a similar incident in the future.

The Iranian threat actor known as OilRig (also referred to as APT34, Crambus, Cobalt Gypsy, GreenBug, Hazel Sandstorm, and Helix Kitten) exploited a now-patched privilege escalation flaw impacting the Windows Kernel (CVE-2024-30088) as part of a cyber espionage campaign targeting the U.A.E. and the broader Gulf region in 2024. The group utilized sophisticated tactics that included deploying a backdoor that leverages Microsoft Exchange servers for credentials theft, and exploiting vulnerabilities for privilege escalation. Trend Micro researchers Mohamed Fahmy, Bahaa Yamany, Ahmed Kamal, and Nick Dai disclosed the attack in an analysis published on 13 October 2024. The attackers gained initial access to target networks by infiltrating a vulnerable web server to drop a web shell, followed by dropping the ngrok remote management tool to maintain persistence and move to other endpoints in the network. The attackers then used the privilege escalation vulnerability to deliver the backdoor, codenamed STEALHOOK, responsible for transmitting harvested data via the Exchange server to an email address controlled by the attacker. The attackers also used the elevated privileges to drop the password filter policy DLL (psgfilter.dll) in order to extract sensitive credentials from domain users via domain controllers or local accounts on local machines.

The Ukrainian military intelligence agency HUR, in an apparent effort with hacktivist group VO Team disrupted the Russian Digital Court System Pravosudie on 7 October 2024. The attack occurred at the same time as a cyber incident affecting the Russian banking sector and coincides with the birthday of Russian President Vladimir Putin. The disruption of the justice portal affected the filing of lawsuits, but also ongoing hearings and court dates. The HUR also succeeded in stealing data held by the courts.

The Internet Archive, a public service and a digital culture protection mission, faced a series of massive cyber attacks in October 2024, which were claimed by a pro-Palestinian hacktivist group called SN_BLACKMETA. SN_BLACKMETA launched a series of disruptive DDoS attacks between 8 and 10 October. The Internet Archive's founder, Brewster Kahle, confirmed the attack, and stated that the organisation was working to upgrade security and restore services. The DDoS attack disrupted access to the platform, while subsequent attacks on 10 October led to the defacement of the webpage and the downage of further services. The motivations behind the attack are unclear, but the hackers claimed that the Internet Archive was targeted because it belongs to the USA and supports the genocide perpetrated by the State of Israel. The Internet Archive has been working to restore services and has advised users to change their passwords.

Unknown Threat Actors compromised Japanese electronics company Casio's network on 5 October 2024, causing system-wide disruptions and raising concerns about a potential data breach. The company is investigating the incident with cybersecurity experts. This incident comes after a significant data breach in October 2023, caused by human error, which affected users in 148 countries and targeted Casio’s ClassPad education platform. Casio has restricted external access to its systems while the investigation is ongoing and has released a statement acknowledging the breach and its potential impact. No ransomware group has taken responsibility for the attack. Hackread.com reported the incident on 10 October 2024. On 10 October, the Underground ransomware group claimed to have hacked Casio. On 11 October 2024, Casio updated its initial notification of 8 October, in which Casio announced that there had been unauthorized access to its networks, disruption and data theft.

Title (Company): Not available - Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power
Description: Unidentified North Korean hackers gained access to an unnamed company and stole data from the Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power (KHNP) energy company in September 2020 and June 2024, various media reported without referring to a specific source. The data theft included 110,000 technical sources of water technology and nuclear data. The leaked data mainly related to older prototypes, such as the APR 1000 and APR-1400. The hack was attributed to North Korea due to using a password for the management account with system privileges. The incident was reported by the head of the Congress's Science and Information Communications Commission and the Democratic Council for the People's Republic of Korea's CHOI on 9 and 10 October 2024, respectively.

Unknown threat actors compromised the data of 77,099 Fidelity Investments customers in Maine between 17 and 19 August 2024, obtaining personal information, including Social Security numbers and driver’s licenses. They also created two new customer accounts. Fidelity disclosed the breach in a notification letter sent to thousands of customers on 9 October 2024 and offered affected individuals credit monitoring and identity restoration services.

Unknown threat actors compromised the administration of the Verbandsgemeinde Elbe-Heide in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany, on 8 October 2024, causing all systems to be shut down as a precaution, resulting in the limitation of digital processes and partial limitation of office accessibility, with experts working to resolve the issue.

Russian cybersecurity firm Kaspersky reported on 7 October 2024, that the hacking group GoldenJackal gained access and stole data using a variety of modular malware in a European Union government organization from May 2022 to March 2024. The malware used included the file collectors GoldenUsbCopy and GoldenUsbGo; the malware distributor GoldenAce; the email processors GoldenBlacklist and GoldenPyBlacklist and the data exfiltrators GoldenMailer and GoldenDrive.

Russian IT security company Kaspersky reported on 7 October 2024, that the hacker group GoldenJackal gained access using the GoldenHowl backdoor and stole unspecified data using the GoldenRobo exfiltrator on a network of a South Asian embassy in Belarus. The overarching goal of the attack was to penetrate an air-gapped network in August 2019. It can be confirmed that the GoldenDealer downloader, the GoldenHowl backdoor, and the GoldenRobo exfiltrator were running on a computer connected to the Internet. The rest of the process involved infecting a USB drive that would have been connected to the infected computer, which would then have been connected to a computer in the air-gapped network and infected the same.

Title (Company): Hapoel Beersheba FC - Not available - Hapoel Tel Aviv - Maccabi Rishon Lezion - Maccabi Tel Aviv
Description: Following the al-Qassem Brigades' call for widespread cyber attacks on Israel on 7 October, pro-Palestinian hackers allegedly defaced the websites of several Israeli sports clubs and federations, including Maccabi Tel Aviv, Hapoel Tel Aviv, Maccabi Rishon Lezion, and Hapoel Beersheba football clubs, as well as basketball, handball, and swimming federations on 8 October 2024. The hacked websites featured images of al-Qassem spokesman Abu Ubeyde and writings of the Masjid-i Aksa, as well as statements such as "GAZA 4 EVER," and "War has begun, prepare."

Unknown Threat Actors compromised American Water Works Company, a New Jersey-based company responsible for providing water to more than 14 million people in 14 states, in a cyberattack on October 3, 2024, which resulted in the loss of billing systems, according to a Securities and Exchange Commission filing. American Water Works Company disconnected and deactivated certain systems as part of the incident response procedure. The company's water and wastewater facilities and operations remain unaffected by the incident. American Water Works Company notified law enforcement about the attack and is investigating the security breach with the help of cybersecurity experts. The company estimates minimal financial impact from the security incident, though the full impact is still uncertain. No ransomware gang has claimed responsibility for the attack.

In the early morning of 7 October 2024, the pro-Ukrainian hacker group "Sudo rm-RF" launched a disruptive cyber attack against the Russian state media entity, "All-Russia State Television and Radio Broadcasting Company" (VGTRK), which disrupted online broadcasts, internal services, and communications. The attackers also reportedly wiped servers and backups, meant to send a message on the 72nd birthday of Russian President Vladimir Putin.  The attack, which was claimed by the hacking group, affected over 20 channels operated by VGTRK, including Rossiya 1 and Rossiya 24. While the Kremlin condemned the attack, an anonymous Ukrainian government source confirmed that Ukrainian hackers were behind the cyber attack, though the level of coordination between the Ukrainian government and the hackers is not clear.

Unknown threat actors compromised the University of Salerno's website on Sunday, 6 October 2024, blocking access to the site for the entire day, as reported by the daily newspaper 'Le Chroniche' on 7 October 2024. The attackers used a fake certificate, a typical procedure to capture sensitive information, and took control of the university's computer system. This incident follows two previous hacking incidents at the university, which resulted in the theft of thousands of sensitive student data. The university, which has benefited from Pnnr funds and boasts a Serics Cyber foundation, has not yet confirmed the extent of the data breach.

The Chinese-related APT group, CeranaKeeper, targeted state institutions in Thailand in 2023, leaking a large amount of data. The group constantly updates its backdoors to avoid detection and diversify its methods to facilitate the mass data leak. CeranaKeeper used cloud and file sharing services, such as Dropbox, PixelDrain, GitHub, and OneDrive, for infiltration. The group also used services like Pastebin, Dropbox, OneDrive, and Github to conduct commands and release sensitive documents on previously compromised computers. The attacks were attributed to CeranaKeeper, a threat actor believed to be active since at least 2022, primarily targeting state institutions in Thailand, Myanmar, the Philippines, Japan, and Taiwan. The group's tactics, techniques, and procedures, code, and infrastructure were studied by ESET, which presented its findings on CeranaKeeper and the security deficit in Thailand at the 2024 Virus Bulletin conference. CeranaKeeper is probably using a public tool set called 'instruction Stager' (or 'TONESHELL') and has been observed using a sideloading technique to leak files from a network. The group also used a tool to empty its identity information and a legal Avast driver to disable security products in the machine. ESET researchers discovered several targeted campaigns that began in 2023 against state institutions in Thailand, where large amounts of data were leaked. CeranaKeeper's true identity and motivations are unknown, but its activities have been linked to China.

Title (Company): European Organisation of Maritime Ports - Port of Antwerp-Bruges - Municipality of Rhode-Saint-Genese - Municipality of Linkebeek - Chamber of Representatives (Belgium) - Federal Public Service Economy, SMEs, Middle Classes, and Energy - Province of Walloon Brabant - Center for Cyber Security Belgium (CCB) - City of Antwerp - Province of East Flanders - Port of Zeebrugge - Province of Limburg - Febelfin - Province of Flemish Brabant - Hainaut Province - Port of Liege - The City of Herstal - Walloon Region - Municiipality of Kraainem - Province of Liège
Description: The Russian state-sponsored hacker group "NoName057(16)" launched a DDoS attack on several government websites and on several infrastructure targets in Belgium between 7 and 8 October 2024, justifying its attack due to Belgium's planned donation of three Caesar artillery units; while NoName declared the attack on its Telegram channel, it was confirmed by the Belgian Cybersecurity Centre (CBC) and the affected institutions. The attack on municipal websites took place on 7 October and temporarily disrupted the affected servers and impacted the provinces of Liège, Limburg, East Flanders, Flemish Brabant, Walloon Brabant; the municipalities of Rhode-Saint-Genèse, Linkebeek, and Kraainem; the cities of Antwerp and Herstal; and the Belgian Chamber of Representatives. On 8 October, NoName further launched DDoS attacks against several ports in Belgium, including the ports of Antwerp-Bruges, Zeebrugge, Liège, and the European Organisation of Maritime Ports. On October 10, 2024, the NoName hacker group disrupted the organization Febelfin, the Belgian Ministry of the Economy (Federal Public Service Economy, SMEs, Middle Classes, and Energy) and the Belgian Center for Cyber Security (CCB).

An unknown actor disrupted the network of the Wayne County government in Michigan on 2 October 2024, WXYZ reported the next day, citing unspecified sources. The unspecified source said the hackers made a financial demand via ransomware.

The Chinese state-sponsored hacking group APT10, also known as 'Earth Kasha' and 'MirrorFace', compromised Japanese companies in the manufacturing sector in December 2019, as part of a campaign dubbed 'Cuckoo Spear'. The attackers used advanced malware, including 'NOOPLDR' and 'NOOPDOOR', to gain persistent access to the victims' networks for up to three years. The malware was loaded using various techniques, including DLL side-loading and C# code execution with phishing as an initial access vector. The campaign was attributed to APT10 based on similarity in techniques employed by the Threat Actor. The attackers' intention was likely espionage, as they targeted critical infrastructure sectors and academic institutions.

Unknown threat actors infected the Ikaruga City Library's systems with ransomware in September 2024. The incident was reported by Kyocera Systems Corporation as they were responsible for an update of the library's software planned to be launched for all of the library users on 1 October. Due to the encryption of the server infrastructure, the launch had to be postponed to mitigate the issues. Currently, the operations have to be made manually.

The North Korean state-sponsored hacking group 'Stonefly' (also known as the North Korean Surveillance Patrol hack group, Andriel, APT45, Sailant Garima or Orix Slit) attacked at least three US companies in August 2024, according to a report released by the cybersecurity company, Symantec. Stonefly used a custom malformation program called BlackDoor.Preft in this attack. The group has significantly improved its capabilities since 2019, focusing on high-value targets with sensitive information and/or know-how with a primarily financial motivation. The incident is part of Stonefly's continued monetary activities, despite arrest warrants and rewards offered by the US justice department against its members.

Title (Company): Thorax Center Münnerstadt - Not available - I-MED Radiology
Description: Unknown threat actors gained online access to the platform of the Australian radiology system 'I-MED Radiology' and stole physical data carriers with over 100,000 patient data records from medical practices in September 2024, as reported by an unknown source to Australian outlet Crikey. The hacker gained access to I-MED Radiology using credentials from a previous data leak to accounts not protected by multi-factor authentification. Stolen files contain full names, dates of birth, gender and, in some cases, MRI scans. Among the victims, the Thorax Center Münnerstadt in Southern Germany reported that it had been affected and its operations were currently only possible to a limited extent. Moreover, German police confirmed that data carriers were stolen from two medical practices in Hamburg with investigations are reportedly underway.

Unknown threat actors compromised the IT infrastructure of the Uttarakhand government offices in India on 4 October 2024, by using malware, which was detected on systems at the State Data Centre, leaving government offices unable to carry out work. The malware affected critical services like Secure Internet Service and the State Wide Area Network (SWAN), government websites, the Chief Minister’s helpline and land registration services. The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) and the National Informatics Centre (NIC) were informed about the attack. Experts at the Information Technology Development Agency (ITDA) are working to combat the malware. The State Wide Area Network (SWAN) services were restored in the first phase, but other services remained offline as of 4 October 2024.

North Korean state-sponsored hacking group APT37 compromised targets in Cambodia and potentially other Southeast Asian countries in a campaign dubbed SHROUDED#SLEEP, using a previously undocumented backdoor and remote access trojan (RAT) called VeilShell, as reported by Securonix on 3 October 2024. The group delivered the malware via spear-phishing emails, allowing the attacker full access to the compromised machine, including data exfiltration, registry, and scheduled task creation or manipulation. The attack chain featured a lesser-known technique called AppDomainManager injection and used a PowerShell-based malware to contact a command-and-control (C2) server to await further instructions. Securonix researchers Den Iuzvyk and Tim Peck disclosed the ongoing operation in a technical report on 3 October 2024.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: A 24-year-old hacker from Gela, currently residing in Rome, was arrested by the Postal Police on 1 October 2024 after a lengthy investigation into unauthorised access to the computer systems of the Ministry of Justice, Guardia di Finanza, Tim, and Telespazio. Between 2020 and 2024, the hacker acquired sensitive investigation files, including those related to organised crime, as disclosed by the National Anti-Mafia Directorate and the cybercrime pool of the Public Prosecutor's Office of Naples in a press conference on 2 October 2024. The arrest was facilitated by investigators who monitored the hacker's access to the servers, allowing them to seize a substantial amount of decrypted data. The hacker, who employed at least five fictitious identities, had the capability to control the information systems of justice, posing a serious threat to national security. The investigation involved multiple prosecutors and was coordinated by the National Anti-Mafia Directorate and the cybercrime unit of Naples.

Unknown Threat Actors launched a ransomware attack against the Agència de Residus de Catalunya, a municipal waste management point in Catalonia, over the weekend of 2024-09-28 to 2024-09-29, with the intention of hijacking data and demanding a ransom. The attack, which was detected by the Agència de Ciberseguretat de Catalunya, primarily affected the documentary waste system and some internal systems, but did not impact the operability of the ACR. The Agència de Ciberseguretat de Catalunya initiated containment measures and launched an investigation to determine the origin of the virus and its impact. The incident was disclosed by the Department of Presidència of the Generalitat on 2024-09-30.

Title (Company): Charter Communications - Lumen Technologies - Consolidated Communications - Not available - Verizon Communications - AT&T - Windstream Communications
Description: The threat actor Salt Typhoon, aka FamousSparrow and GhostEmporor, and linked to the Chinese government, allegedly infiltrated networks of various US broadband communications companies, including AT&T, Verizon, and Lumen Technologies, to access information about the system used by the US federal government to access telecommunication networks for court-authorized wiretapping requests. The incident was disclosed in an exclusive report by the Wall Street Journal on 26 September 2024 and is believed to have been conducted for reconnaissance purposes. However, the full extent of the operation is still unclear and under investigation by the US government. The incident shares similarities to one conducted by the same threat actor that became publicly known two weeks earlier. On 25 October 2024, the Wall Street Journal further reported that "people familiar with the matter" said that the hackers targeted the phones of former President Donald Trump, his running mate, JD Vance, and persons who are affiliated with the campaign by democratic candidate Kamala Harris. However, at the time of reporting, the actual success of the infiltration attempts could not be verified. On November 13, the Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) published a joint press release reporting on PRC-affiliated actors compromising U.S. telecommunications operators. On November 15, the Wall Street Journal further reported that T-Mobile had also been affected by the cyber incident; however, on 27 November 2024, T-Mobile issued a statement denying that the cyberattack had affected it. T-Mobile wrote that a T-Mobile wireline provider had been compromised, from where the hackers also unsuccessfully attempted to infiltrate T-Mobile's network. On 3 December 2024, senior officials from the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and FBI briefed reporters on the ongoing investigation, describing it as a broad and significant campaign; officials also reported that they were still in the process of removing the hackers from affected networks. The hackers, according to authorities, accessed call metadata, targeted communications content from political and government figures, and data from law enforcement wiretap portals, though the latter was not the primary focus of the campaign. The investigation began earlier this year and has involved collaboration with numerous telecom providers. On 4 December 2024, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), NSA, FBI, and their counterparts in Australia, Canada, and New Zealand issued a joint warning about this cyber espionage campaign by the People's Republic of China (PRC)-affiliated threat actors targeting global telecommunications networks. The agencies emphasize that these compromises exploit known vulnerabilities, and they urge telecommunications providers, critical infrastructure organizations, and enterprises with on-premises equipment to adopt best practices outlined in their guide to enhance visibility, secure network devices, and mitigate further intrusions through timely patching and robust security measures. On the same day, on 4 December 2024, the White House provided an update on China's "Salt Typhoon" hacking campaign, confirming that at least eight U.S. telecommunications companies were breached over the past one to two years, with similar attacks reported in "a couple of dozen" countries. The hackers accessed a significant amount of Americans' metadata, focusing on the communications of government officials and politicians, though no classified communications are believed to have been compromised. On 27 December 2024, Deputy National Security Advisor for Cyber and Emerging Technologies Anne Neuberger provided an update on the cyber incident at a press briefing. She announced that the assistance provided by the government agencies after the cyber incident was first discovered in the summer of 2023 led to the identification of a ninth case involving an unnamed telecommunications company, while it is believed that the attackers were in telecoms' networks for at least a year prior (i.e., by 2022). Neuberger also reported that in one of the nine cases, the hackers gained access to an administrator account and thereby gained access to over 100,000 routers. On 29 December 2024, the victim, Verizon Communications, reported in a statement emailed to TechCrunch that the cyber incident targeted a small number of high-profile customers in the government. On the following day, 30 December 2024, the victim AT&T also announced via TechCrunch that in their case, too, a small number of individuals of interest to foreign intelligence services were targeted and, in relatively few cases, information was compromised. Both telecommunications companies reported at the time of their statements that the cyber incident had been contained. On 31 December 2024, the telecommunications company Lumen Technologies reported that they had removed the hackers from their networks and that there was no evidence that access to data had been gained. On 4 January 2024, the Wall Street Journal reported that Charter Communications, Consolidated Communications, and Windstream, in addition to the already known telecommunications companies, had also fallen victim to this cyber incident. The Wall Street Journal also wrote that the hackers exploited unfixed network devices from Fortinet and compromised large network routers. Reuters reported on 22 January 2025, that the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) terminated all members of its advisory committees, according to a letter signed by Acting Secretary Benjamine C. Huffman and seen by Reuters. Among the affected committees is the Cyber Safety Review Board, which examines this cyberespionage operation by Salt Typhoon. Democratic Senator Ron Wyden criticized the decision, calling it a "gift to Chinese spies" and accusing DHS of undermining a critical investigation into a major security breach.

On 30 September 2024, Unknown Threat Actors compromised the Catholic University of Valencia's servers, encrypting identifying, financial, academic, professional, employment, and health data using ransomware. The university reported the incident to the National Police and the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD), and is collaborating with cybersecurity experts and authorities to address the situation. While key data remains encrypted, it is currently unknown whether unauthorized access or misuse has occurred. The university has bolstered security measures and will restore affected services once safety is assured. Notably, teaching activities have remained unaffected.

Unknown threat actors compromised the computer systems of Chilean Compañía de Cervecerías Unidas (CCU) in its sales and distribution areas, resulting in an information leak in 2024, Chile's biggest brewery group CCU disclosed in a statement to the Commission for the Financial Market (CMF) on 27 September 2024. The company's internal team managed to contain the attack, limiting its impact on services and operations, and is currently in the process of recovery and evaluation of the scope and content of the leaked information.

Unknown hackers launched a ransomware attack on Lubbock, Texas-based UMC Health System, a level 1 trauma centre from the US, on September 26, 2024, causing the system to disconnect its systems due to unusual activity and resulting in the diversion of emergency and non-emergency patients to other local healthcare facilities. Furthermore, it caused the interruption of the organization's phones and patient portal, with the health system enlisting third-party help in its response and investigation, and no timeline for restoration, as reported on the health system's website on September 27, 2024.

Ukraine's Main Directorate of Intelligence (HUR) cyber specialists conducted attacks on over 800 servers across various regions of Russia between September 23 and 26, 2024, resulting in the complete destruction of documents and data stored on the affected servers, which belonged to military, administrative, and financial institutions that support Russia's aggression against Ukraine, according to a source in the intelligence community, Ukrinform and other Ukrainian news outlets reported the same day.

The Israeli cyber army hacked into the communication network of the Beirut Airport control tower on Saturday, 28 September 2024, breaching the communication network and threatening an Iranian civilian plane attempting to land, forcing it to return to Tehran. The hack was reported by MiddleEastMonitor website. The Lebanese Ministry of Transport instructed airport authorities to block the Iranian aircraft from entering Lebanese airspace in response to the hack. The Israeli army claimed that Beirut International Airport was being used as an entry point for weapons to Hezbollah, however Lebanese authorities denied the accusation, stating that the airport is strictly civilian.

On 25 September 2024, an unknown threat actor breached the public Wi-Fi networks at major railway stations in the UK, impacting 19 stations, including Manchester Piccadilly, Birmingham New Street, and 10 stations in London. Passengers attempting to connect were met with alarming messages about terror attacks in Europe, including a webpage titled "We love you, Europe." Network Rail, British Transport Police, and Telent, the third-party firm providing Wi-Fi, reported the incident, which was logged with authorities at approximately 5:03 p.m. Following the breach, the Wi-Fi services were taken offline nationwide, with restoration expected by the weekend. Network Rail assured that no personal data appeared to have been compromised.

Laundry Bear, a Russian-backed state actor, compromised a police account and stole data on all Dutch police officers, including names, email addresses, and positions of the entire organisation, capturing also the names, official contact details, e-mail addresses, positions, and ranks of all Dutch police officers, including those working undercover. The perpetrators hacked a police account, which gave access to the main file of the entire police organisation, as disclosed by the Minister of Justice and Security, David van Weel, to the parliament in The Hague on 27 September 2024, with the exact number of people affected and the extent of the data leak still unknown. The security breach has been reported to the Data Protection Authority. The incident has raised concerns among police officers, with the main Dutch police union expressing worry about its members' safety and the potential consequences of the data leak. The criminal investigation is ongoing, with the police and national security partners trying to identify the attackers and prevent further harm. On 27 May 2025, the Dutch intelligence and security services AIVD and MIVD issued a technical report in which they identified a new Russian state-backed cyber actor “Laundry Bear” as responsible for the cyber attack on the Dutch police in September 2024. The attribution was also shared by the Dutch Ministry of Defense and the Ministry of Interior and Kingdom Relations (Ministerie van Binnenlandse Zaken en Koninkrijsrelaties) on the same day. In addition, Microsoft released a similar attribution but named the threat actor “Void Blizzard."

Lancaster Royal Grammar School in the United Kingdom was the target of a serious ransomware cyberattack on July 16, 2024, but the school did not interact with any demands. Fortunately, none of the most sensitive systems, such as pupil databases, safeguarding, or finance, were affected. The school's IT department noticed something unusual and shut the system down, then rebuilt it from scratch over the summer holidays with added security, resulting in no lasting damage. The incident was reported by the school's head, Dr. Christopher Pyle, and cybersecurity expert Mohammed Patel from Check Point. The attack is part of a series of similar ransomware attacks that affected other schools in the Fylde area, including the Fylde Coast Academy Trust, which was hit by a ransomware attack in September 2024, affecting 10 schools and forcing them to revert to manual processes.

The hacktivist group Ex-Presidents breached the National Party website in Uruguay on 23 September 2024, leaving a public threat, after having already violated the system in August 2024 with a similar message, including a specific date, '13/08/2024', anticipating potential actions. The attack was carried out using a Cross-Site-Scripting technique, according to Birmingham Cyber Arms, and was reported by El Observador. The National Party has responded by taking preventive measures to mitigate future incidents and is actively working to strengthen their cyber security measures.

On September 23, 2024, Mutua Madrileña suffered a cyberattack targeting its home insurance customer database through one of its external providers. Although the insurer swiftly rectified the incident, the data of thousands of clients may have been compromised. In response to the breach, Mutua Madrileña acted promptly and transparently, informing affected customers via email and reporting the incident to the Spanish Data Protection Agency.

Unknown Threat Actors attempted to breach the confidentiality, integrity or availability of the Kuwait Ministry of Health's systems and devices in Kuwait from 22 to 25 September 2024, impacting several health facilities and administrative systems. The Ministry of Health took immediate action to ensure the continuity of essential health services and implemented measures to work with pre-prepared printed documents while safeguarding data integrity. The ministry coordinated with relevant government security agencies, which assisted in containing the problem and preventing its escalation. Infected systems were promptly disconnected from the network, while protection measures were enhanced through software updates and strict access control procedures. The attack did not compromise or encrypt the main databases. The Ministry of Health successfully restored its main systems and hospital operations from the first day of the incident and managed to decode the attack and recover its systems using secure backups. The Ministry of Health is collaborating with government security agencies to restore the remaining systems, which are expected to be fully operational soon.

Between September 6 and 25, 2024, unknown actors compromised over 80 percent of China's IP cams, widely used as CCTVs in the country, also in hospitals, and shared the hacked videos on a Chinese pornographic site, according to South Korean news outlet Chosun. The videos, which contained specific locations, dates, areas, and personal information, were based on places in Korea and China that the hackers could access and expose. The hackers edited the videos to focus on stimulating parts and added voiceovers in some cases. The IP cams, which were mostly Chinese products, had backdoors that allowed the hackers to access the devices and steal information. The hacking group shared information about the hacking of Korean IP cameras on online forums, and the IP cam hack program was easily accessible on online sites.

Unknown Threat Actors launched a ransomware attack on the Arkansas City water treatment facility in Kansas, USA, on Sunday, 22 September 2024, forcing the facility to switch to manual operations. The attackers, believed to be a ransomware group, successfully encrypted at least some computer systems and likely stole information from the water facility, with an apparent ransom note appearing on a water treatment facility computer demanding the employee contact the attackers via email. The city has notified relevant authorities, including Homeland Security and FBI agents, who are investigating the incident. Cybersecurity experts and government authorities are working to resolve the situation and return the facility to normal operations. Enhanced security measures are currently in place to protect the water supply, and no changes to water quality or service are expected for residents. The water supply remains completely safe, and there has been no disruption to service, according to city officials.

Unknown threat actors attacked MoneyGram in September 2024 affecting several systems. After several customers complaints about the lack of services since Friday 20 September, the company itself confirmed a cybersecurity incident. Due to the attack they shut their systems down, impacting network connectivity. Several services like the MoneyGram App or sending and receiving payments are currently unavailable. MoneyGram released a statement on October 8, 2024, saying that an unknown party gained unauthorized access and stole personal information from September 20 to 22, 2024. This included names, contact information (such as phone numbers, email and postal addresses), dates of birth, a limited number of Social Security numbers, copies of government-issued identification documents (such as driver’s licenses), other identification documents (such as utility bills), bank account numbers, MoneyGram Plus Rewards numbers, transaction information (such as dates and amounts of transactions) and, for a limited number of consumers, criminal investigation information (such as fraud). A source familiar with the attack shared further information, telling BleepingComputer that MoneyGram was initially breached through a social engineering attack on the company's internal help desk. This attack allowed the threat actors to access MoneyGram's network using an employee's credentials and target employee information in the company's Windows Active Directory Services.

On 10 September, the Spanish energy company Repsol detected partial access to electricity and gas customer data as a result of an incident suffered by one of its technology providers. The oil company, which stresses that it has ‘immediately implemented measures to rectify the incident’, has avoided specifying the total number of people affected by the unauthorised access. The affected customers were informed about the data breach on Thursday 19 September 2024. The compromised information, according to Repsol, does not include sensitive data, financial data (bank accounts, credit cards), passwords or electricity consumption data. The data affected are name and surname, ID number, address, contact details and CUPS.

Unknown threat actors attacked the German VBG insurance Hamburg with Ransomware in September 2024. This attack only affects the server of the online campus which offers training courses on occupational health and safety. They cannot confirm that no data has been compromised even though they took their server down immediately after they recognised the attack. This data could include names, addresses, e-mail addresses and telephone numbers. The VBG's ability to work is not restricted; in particular, no data on insurance claims is affected.

Iran's security service, via the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), carried out a cyberattack against targets in Sweden on August 1, 2023, compromising a Swedish company that runs a major SMS service in Sweden and sending 15,000 text messages urging Swedes to take revenge against individuals who had burned the Quran, in an attempt to create divisions in Swedish society and portray Sweden as an Islamophobic country. The attack was attributed to Iran by the Swedish Public Prosecutor's Office and the Swedish Security Service, who identified the Iranian hackers responsible for the breach. However, the investigation was closed due to the lack of conditions for prosecution abroad or extradition to Sweden. The incident occurred in the wake of several Quran burnings in public places in Sweden, which sparked widespread anger in the Muslim world and generated diplomatic protests, riots, and threats of economic boycott. The Swedish government had condemned the actions, but the country's courts allowed the protests to proceed under Sweden's freedom of expression laws.

Unknown threat actors hijacked the YouTube channel of the Indian Supreme Court on 20 September 2024. The hackers exploited the channel to showcase a blank video titled Brad Garlinghouse: Ripple Responds To The SEC's $2 Billion Fine! XRP PRICE PREDICTION. The video promoted XRP, a cryptocurrency developed by the United States-based company Ripple Labs. A few hours later, the channel has been taken down.

The Russian state-sponsored hacking group NoName057(16) disrupted several official websites of Austrian political parties and institutions beginning on 23 September 2024, the chief executive officer of the detective agency Foreus, Stefan Embacher, attributed in an article by the television station OE24 on 24 September. On Monday, 23 September 2024, the websites of the Austrian People's Party (ÖVP) and the Social Democratic Party of Austria (SPÖ) were disrupted. On 24 September 2024, the website of the Communist Party of Austria (KPÖ) was also disrupted. On 25 September 2024, the Ministry of Defense, the Austrian Court of Auditors, and other unnamed websites were disrupted. Embacher said that NoName057(16) is a hacker group with "close ties to the Kremlin" and that they are "financed by Putin's regime." In an immediate exchange with the hacker group, they confirmed they had targeted Austrian political parties in the upcoming elections on Sunday, 29 September 2024.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Earth Baxia, a threat actor linked to China, has initiated a sophisticated cyber campaign targeting entities across the Asia-Pacific (APAC) region. In July 2024, the group leveraged spear-phishing techniques to deliver malicious payloads and subsequently exploited the critical Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability CVE-2024-36401 in GeoServer, an open-source Java-based server that manages and disseminates geospatial data. This exploit allowed for deep infiltration into targeted networks, enabling data exfiltration and persistent access while deploying customised Cobalt Strike payloads. Trend Micro reported the use of a new backdoor called EAGLEDOOR, which enhances the threat actor's information gathering and payload delivery capabilities.
Techniques Used: Automated Exfiltration, Exploit Public-Facing Application, Phishing

Description: In September 2024, unknown threat actors launched a ransomware attack targeting the Fylde Coast Academy Trust (FCAT) in Blackpool, disrupting the operations of all 10 schools under its management. The attack compromised the Trust's IT infrastructure, rendering critical systems inaccessible, including those used for teaching, maintaining records, and communication. All 10 institutions within the FCAT umbrella have been impacted. Among them are four key academies in Blackpool: Armfield Academy, Aspire Academy, Montgomery Academy, and Unity Academy. Additionally, Mereside, Gateway, Westcliff, and Westminster primary schools, along with Garstang Community Academy and Hambleton Primary Academy, are also managing the repercussions. As a result, the schools were forced to revert to non-digital processes, significantly impacting daily operations. The attackers demanded a substantial ransom, threatening to permanently block access to the compromised systems if their demands were not met.

On 20 September 2024, the city of Graz experienced a significant cyber disruption when its official website was targeted by a DDoS attack. The assault, which began early in the morning, flooded the site with an overwhelming number of server requests, causing it to crash and become inaccessible to users. Despite the ongoing nature of the attack, city officials assured the public that the security of their data and the integrity of the city’s systems were not compromised. Throughout the day, IT teams worked intensively to counter the attack and restore normal website operations. However, by the afternoon, the website continued to experience intermittent outages, and the timeline for full recovery remained unclear. Sarah Tatschl, a spokesperson from the city's Public Relations office, emphasized that although the service disruption was inconvenient, it did not pose any risk to the data security of Graz's citizens.

On 20 September 2024, unknown threat actors attacked the Singaporean crypto exchange BingX, stealing approximately 52 million US dollars in cryptocurrency from its cold wallet. In response, withdrawals were immediately paused, and asset transfers were initiated to secure remaining funds. Fortunately, most assets remain safe in cold wallets. According to Cyvers, a cybersecurity firm, the attack is suspected to involve the North Korean state-affiliated hacking group Lazarus.

Unknown threat actors attacked the Telegram trading bot Banana Gun and stole cryptocurrency which is about 1.4 million dollars worth in September 2024. Due to this attack, the wallets of about 36 users got drained. According to Cyvers, the attack does not point to a wider smart contract vulnerability. The number of victims suggests that the hacker didn’t successfully infiltrate the entire trading bot, but an isolated number of accounts. According to Banana Gun itself, the back-end is not compromised, and they believe the issue may stem from a front-end vulnerability. The bot got switched off immediately.

The Australian Federal Police (AFP), alone and in cooperation with other law enforcement agencies in Operation Task Force (OTF) NEXT, gained access to devices using the messaging service Ghost from March 2022 to 18 September 2024, as Europol and the AFP reported on 18 September 2024. As part of a separate law enforcement operation, Operation Kraken, under the OTF NEXT, the Australian Federal Police modified the updates from the Ghost messaging service operator to gain access to devices in Australia that used this messaging service. The Ghost messaging service was a communication platform used for illegal activities. However, OTF NEXT also spoke of technical interventions that allowed participating law enforcement agencies to access messages shared via Ghost. In addition to many law enforcement actions in many countries between 17 and 18 September 2024, including arrests and seizures, AFP charged the operator of the messaging service, 32-year-old Jay Je Yoon Jung of New South Wales, with five counts.

Title (Company): Flax Typhoon fka Storm-0919/Ethereal Panda/Red Juliett
Description: On September 18, 2024, the U.S. Department of Justice announced the successful disruption of a botnet that had infected more than 200,000 consumer devices across the United States and globally. The botnet was operated by state-sponsored hackers from the People’s Republic of China (PRC), specifically working for Integrity Technology Group, a Beijing-based company known in the cybersecurity community as “Flax Typhoon.” The botnet compromised a wide range of consumer devices, including small-office/home-office (SOHO) routers, IP cameras, DVRs, and network-attached storage (NAS) devices. These infected devices were linked together into a network controlled by Integrity Technology Group, which used them to conduct covert cyber activities under the guise of normal internet traffic. In a court-authorized operation, the FBI took control of the hackers’ infrastructure and issued disabling commands to the malware across the infected devices. During the operation, the hackers attempted to disrupt the FBI’s efforts with a DDoS attack, but the FBI successfully neutralized this threat, ensuring the botnet's dismantlement.

The North Korean state-sponsored hacking group UNC2970 gained access to a multinational energy company in June 2024, Google reported in a technical report on 17 September 2024. The hacking group posed as a recruiter for well-known companies and lured an unspecified victim via WhatsApp with a job offer. The job offer was in an encrypted PDF file that the victim could only open with the help of a trojanised version of the SumatraPDF software, which downloaded the MISTPEN backdoor via the BURNBOOK uploader. The specific victim downloaded such a ZIP archive, and the connection to the backdoor was then made via a SharePoint server at an unnamed university.

The website of the Turkish National Smart Meter Systems (MASS) was the victim of a disruption by unknown actors in mid-September 2024.
