The threat actors exploited CVE-2026-21509 and CVE-2026-21513 as zero-days via spearphishing emails themed around military training, weather alerts and weapon smuggling. The attack chain triggered exploitation of CVE-2026-21509, forcing systems to connect to attacker-controlled WebDAV servers and execute malicious LNK files. The PRISMEX malware suite included PrismexSheet, PrismexDrop, PrismexLoader and PrismexStager, employing steganography, COM hijacking and abuse of cloud service Filen.io for command and control. Decoy documents included Ukrainian drone inventories, supplier price lists and military logistics forms. Trend Micro attributed the activity to APT28 with high confidence, noting the campaign reflects a shift toward tactical disruption of Ukraine's supply chain and NATO-linked logistics rather than pure espionage, publishing its findings on 26 March 2026.
Techniques Used: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol, Drive-by Compromise, Phishing

Title (Company): Ministry of Education - Central Bank of the Republic of Argentina (BCRA) - Ministry of Health - Police of Santiago del Estero - Cabinet of Ministers - Provincial security forces of Tucuman - Provincial security forces of Misiones - Provincial security forces of Cordoba - Provincial security forces of Entre Rios - National Agency for Disability (ANDIS) - Provincial security forces of Santiago del Estero
Description: Hacktivist group Chronus Team breached over 30 public and private organisations in Argentina in March 2026. Affected institutions included the National Agency for Disability, the Central Bank of the Republic of Argentina, the Chief of the Cabinet of Ministers, the Ministry of Health, the Ministry of Education, the Federal System for Security Measures and the Institute for Medical Assistance Work. The attack also affected provincial police forces in Córdoba, Entre Ríos, Misiones, Tucumán and Santiago del Estero. Users identified as "adrxx", "L0stex" and "Lizard", alleged members of Chronus Team, claimed responsibility for the attack which resulted in the exfiltration of significant amounts of sensitive data. El Liberal reported the attack on 8 April 2026.

Unknown perpetrators breached Instituto Costarricense de Electricidad (ICE), a state-owned electricity and telecommunications provider in Costa Rica, on 12 March 2026. The attackers sought to extract information related to contracts made by the institution. Preliminary analysis indicated that the malware used was of Asian origin. The Costa Rican government stated that the extent of the damage and the amount of data stolen remain unknown. The incident is under investigation. Teletica reported additional information on 7 April 2026.

Unknown threat actors deployed ransomware against ChipSoft, a Dutch healthcare software provider that manages patient files for approximately 70 percent of Dutch hospitals, on 7 April 2026. Z-CERT, the Dutch centre of expertise for digital security in healthcare, informed affected institutions in a confidential message on the same day. Various hospitals, including Rijnstate Hospital in Arnhem, Antoni van Leeuwenhoek Hospital in Amsterdam and Franciscus Hospital in Rotterdam, reported no disruption to operations and no compromise of patient data. ChipSoft confirmed the incident and took measures to limit the adverse consequences. NOS and NL Times reported the attack on 8 April 2026.

Title (Company): Unspecified Private Households - Not available - Unspecified Businesses - Not available
Description: Russia-linked group APT28 compromised internet routers of private homes and businesses in the United Kingdom and United States between 2024 and 2026. The threat actors rerouted internet traffic through servers under their control, intercepting sensitive data including passwords and access tokens from email and web services. The attackers employed DNS hijacking to redirect users to fraudulent websites designed to harvest login credentials. The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) described the campaign as opportunistic, with the attackers initially targeting large numbers of devices before narrowing their focus to individuals or organisations of intelligence interest. The NCSC disclosed the campaign in a technical report on 7 April 2026. The US Department of Justice announced on the same day that they neutralized the U.S. portion of a network in a court-authorized technical operation.

On 6 April 2026, unknown threat actors breached Winona County, Minnesota, disrupting county systems and impairing emergency and municipal services. The Governor signed an executive order authorizing the Minnesota National Guard to assist with the response. The incident was reported to the public on 7 April 2026 through the executive order.

Title (Company): Not available - Not available - Not available
Description: Since 2023, the China-based group Storm-1175 has exploited zero-day and n-day vulnerabilities in high-velocity attacks to deploy Medusa ransomware payloads, targeting the healthcare, education, professional services, and finance sectors in Australia, the United Kingdom, and the United States. The group exploited at least 17 vulnerabilities (CVE-202510035, CVE-202623760, CVE-2026-1731, CVE-2023-21529, CVE-2023-27351, CVE-2023-27350, CVE-2023-46805, CVE-2024-21887, CVE-2024-1709, CVE-2024-1708, CVE-2024-27198, CVE-2024-27199, CVE-2024-57726, CVE-2024-57727, CVE-2024-57728, CVE 2025 31161, CVE-2025-52691) to gain access to victims' networks. Microsoft reported the attacks on 6 April 2026.

Unknown hackers breached the Hospital Authority of Hong Kong and leaked sensitive information affecting approximately 200,000 patient records on 3 April 2026. The compromised data included Hong Kong Identity Card numbers, full names, genders, dates of birth and patient identifiers. The unattributed threat actor claimed responsibility and shared sample content on a dark web forum. The Hospital Authority confirmed a suspected case of patient data theft and leakage on 4 April 2026.

Unidentified perpetrators targeted Signature Healthcare, a hospital provider in Brockton, Massachusetts, US, on 6 April 2026. Signature Healthcare detected the incident, shut down its systems and issued a public notice outlining the service disruptions on the same day.

North Korean threat actor UNC4736 likely stole approximately $285 million in cryptocurrency from Drift, a US-based cryptocurrency trading platform, on 1 April 2026. According to the company, the threat actors targeted Drift employees at an in-person crypto conference in autumn 2025, posing as a potential business partner with a verifiable background. After onboarding on Drift's ecosystem and depositing over $1 million, the threat actor built an operating presence in the system and sent links infected with malware. Drift engaged Mandiant to investigate the incident. Mandiant attributed the attack to North Korean state-affiliated UNC4736 (also tracked as AppleJeus and Citrine Sleet) on 5 April 2026.

Unknown threat actors compromised Gritman Medical Center, a health system in Moscow, Idaho, US, on or around 1 April 2026, resulting in the closure of several primary and specialty clinics. The hospital and emergency department remained open throughout. Gritman Medical Center publicly disclosed the incident on 2 April 2026 via Facebook. Electronic systems were coming back online by 5 April 2026. Preliminary findings indicated no successful access to electronic systems and no compromise of patient or secure data.

Iran-linked Handala claimed responsibility for a breach of PSK Wind Technologies, an Israeli defence contractor specialising in integrated systems for defence and critical communications, on 2 April 2026. Handala claimed to have stolen sensitive data including documents on command and control systems and allegedly sent it to Axis of Resistance missile units. The group released confidential files including communications systems documentation, internal documents and location photos. The attack was announced on 2 April 2026, coinciding with the Jewish holiday of Passover.

Unidentified perpetrators deployed ransomware against the water treatment plant of Minot, North Dakota, US on 14 March 2026, forcing staff to switch to manual operations for approximately 16 hours after a server was compromised. The compromised server was unplugged after a ransomware message was discovered, while operations continued. The attack was disclosed in a letter from the City Manager to the City Council on 31 March 2026.

North Korean threat actor UNC1069 compromised the widely used open-source software Axios by inserting malicious code into a software update on 31 March 2026. The attackers likely attempted to exfiltrate data from downstream entities. Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) reported the incident and attributed it to UNC1069, a North Korean threat actor with financial motives. The malicious software was removed on the same day.

Title (Company): Pepperell Fire Department - Groton Police Department - Pepperell Police Department - Patriot Regional Emergency Communications Center
Description: Unknown threat actors breached systems of the police, fire department and Patriots Regional Emergency Communications Center in Pepperell, Massachusetts on 31 March 2026, affecting nearby communities including Ashby and Townsend. Reports suggest that data was compromised and that non-emergency phone lines were disrupted. The incident was disclosed by Pepperell officials.

Unknown threat actors deployed ransomware against Fernheizwerk Neukölln AG, a district heating provider in Berlin, Germany, on 20 March 2026. The attackers reportedly exfiltrated data and issued a ransom demand with a payment deadline of 29 March 2026. The operators declined to meet the attackers' demands. Despite the compromise, heating operations continued without disruption. The full extent of the data breach remains unclear. German authorities have been informed and investigations are ongoing.

Iran-linked Handala claimed responsibility for a breach of the exile media outlet IranWire on 31 March 2026. According to the Iranian judiciary, large amounts of data were obtained, including correspondence, lists of employees and informants, as well as highly confidential information. Handala published selected materials as proof of the breach. The FBI assesses Handala is operated by Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS).

Qilin ransomware group launched ransomware attack on Maine mental health agency AMHC, the largest behavioural healthcare provider in rural Maine with over 350 employees and 5,500 clients, in March 2026. Qilin added AMHC to its list of victims on its dark web data leak site on or around 24 March 2026. The attack was confirmed in a statement to Bangor Daily News on 25 March 2026, stating that it had recently experienced a network disruption and was investigating the incident with cyber incident specialists. The investigative report, published on 7 April 2026, stated that sensitive data was stolen and found that Qilin had obtained unauthorised access between 11 and 12 March 2026.

On or before 10 March 2026, Iran-linked Homeland Justice group carried out a cyberattack on the digital infrastructure of Albania's parliament. The attackers claimed to have gained access to the correspondences the whole Parliament and later leaked emails belonging to four MPs and also deleted materials from the servers, while the breach caused the parliament's IT team to suspend access to internal email services. Local media reports that the attackers claimed responsibility on 10 March 2026, though they likely gained access much earlier.

Unknown threat actor compromised France's National Agency for Secure Documents (ANTS) website on 15 April, and possibly exposed personal data from users applying for IDs, passports, and drivers licences. The Interior Ministry confirmed the breach in a statement on their website on 20 April 2026, and was investigating the scope and impact on affected users. The security breach may have exposed user details such as login ID, name, email, date of birth, and account ID, as well as address, place of birth or phone number in some cases. Authorities notified impacted users and reported the incident to the French Data Protection Authority, notified prosecutors, and alerted the national cybersecurity agency. On 16 April, the threat actor claimed to be selling a large dataset stolen from ANTS, which included around 18-19 million records with names, emails, phone numbers, birth details, addresses and account metadata in a breach forum.

Unknown threat actors breached the City of Tallahassee, Florida, on 17 April 2026, affecting parts of the city's technology environment and knocking the city website offline. Officials immediately disconnected impacted systems and isolated the threat. The city reported no operational impacts at the time, although periodic downtime was possible during maintenance. The city confirmed the cyberattack on 17 April 2026 but did not disclose whether ransomware was involved or if any data was taken.

Title (Company): Unspecified Hosting Providers - Unspecified Internet Service Providers
Description: China-linked group Salt Typhoon (aka Ghost Emperor / RedMike) targeted smaller internet service and hosting providers in the Netherlands, gaining access to routers but not penetrating further into internal networks. The Dutch Military Intelligence and Security Service (MIVD) and General Intelligence and Security Service (AIVD) conducted an investigation, corroborating some findings of a US investigation with independent intelligence. The Dutch agencies endorsed warnings issued by the NSA, CISA and FBI, along with European intelligence agencies BND (Germany), SUPO (Finland), NCSC (UK) and AISE (Italy). The MIVD and AIVD warned that Chinese cyber activities had become increasingly sophisticated, posing a major challenge to Dutch resilience. The attack was publicly disclosed on 28 August 2025.

The Russian ransomware group REvil disrupted the servers of Brazilian meat processing company JBS S. A. in North America and Australia on 30 May 2021, JBS USA announced in a statement the day after. Media reports noted that the cyber incident disrupted JBS's meat processing facilities in the United States, Canada, and Australia.  On 2 June 2021, the FBI attributed the ransomware attack to the REvil ransomware group (also known as Sodinokibi). White House Deputy Press Secretary Karine Jean-Pierre had announced one day earlier that the White House believed the perpetrators were a criminal organization in Russia. On 3 June, JBS released a statement declaring that in the US the impact of the disruption had been limited to one day's equivalent of meat production. The company expected to return to regular production levels at the end of the following week. On 9 June, JBS USA issued a follow-on press release admitting to paying $11 million in ransom to the ransomware group. JBS USA CEO Andre Nogueira explained this step with efforts to prevent potential risks to customers..  In response, the chairwoman of the House Oversight and Reform Committee, Carolyn Maloney (D-N.Y.), sent a letter to Andre Nogueira one day later demanding all documents related to the decision to pay the ransom. In the letter, Maloney also expressed her disapproval of JBS USA's decision to pay the ransom.  On 9 July 2021, US President Joe Biden reported to have demanded in a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin that he "take action" against cybercriminals in his country and that the United States reserved its right to "defend its own people and it's critical infrastructure".  Soon after, on 13 July 2021, the websites and other infrastructure of REvil went offline and group's spokesperson, going by the monicker 'unknown', disappeared. Media reports later revealed that a foreign partner of the US government had compromised REvil infrastructure. Following a brief period in hiding, the group sought to relaunch in September, apparently relying on backups that had previously been infiltrated by the foreign partner. REvil became aware of this compromise when US Cyber Command blocked its website and redirected traffic in October, following to which the group disbanded.
Techniques Used: Content Injection, Drive-by Compromise, Valid Accounts

Title (Company): Unspecified Turkish Private Organisations - Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey (TÜBİTAK) - Unspecified Turkish Government Entities
Description: Iran-linked group MuddyWater (MERCURY, Static Kitten), attributed to Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS) by US Cyber Command, targeted Turkish private organisations and governmental institutions including the Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey (TÜBİTAK) in a campaign operating as recently as November 2021. The threat actors distributed malicious PDFs and Microsoft Office documents masquerading as legitimate documents from the Turkish Health and Interior Ministries, delivering PowerShell-based downloaders as initial footholds.  Cisco Talos attributed the campaign with high confidence to MuddyWater based on technical indicators and TTPs

Title (Company): Unspecified Transportation Sector Organisations - Unspecfied Financial Sector Organisations - Unspecified High-Tech Sector Organisations - Unspecified Global Government Agencies - Unspecified US Defence Industrial Base Companies
Description: China-nexus groups UNC2630 and UNC2717 exploited vulnerabilities in Pulse Secure VPN appliances to compromise dozens of US and EU organisations between August 2020 and March 2021. The threat actors deployed custom malware to maintain long-term access, collect credentials and steal proprietary data.  UNC2630 targeted US defence industrial base companies with malware families including SLOWPULSE, RADIALPULSE, THINBLOOD, ATRIUM, PACEMAKER, SLIGHTPULSE and PULSECHECK. UNC2717 targeted global government agencies using HARDPULSE, QUIETPULSE and PULSEJUMP. FireEye later identified four additional malware strains deployed by UNC2630: BLOODMINE, BLOODBANK, CLEANPULSE and RAPIDPULSE.  Targeted organisations operated in defence, government, high-tech, transportation and financial sectors, aligning with Beijing's strategic objectives outlined in China's 14th Five Year Plan. The threat actors exploited CVE-2021-22893 along with previously disclosed vulnerabilities CVE-2019-11510, CVE-2020-8260 and CVE-2020-8243.  FireEye observed UNC2630 removing webshells from compromised devices between 17 and 20 April 2021, displaying sensitivity to publicity following FireEye's initial reporting. FireEye published the findings on 27 May 2021, and CISA updated its alert with the new TTPs and indicators of compromise.

Sie beanstandete jedoch auch das Fehlen einer Datenschutz-Folgeabschätzung, unzureichende Information der Betroffenen, die als mangelhaft eingestuften technischen und organisatorischen Maßnahmen der Apps. Darüber hinaus stellte die GPDP Unregelmäßigkeiten im Bezug auf die Benennung der Datenverantwortlichen fest. Gegen Postepay wurde ein Bußgeld von 5.877.000 EUR verhängt.
LINDDUN categories: Linkability, Identifiability, Non-repudiation, Detectability, Disclosure of information, Unawareness, Non-compliance

Description: Die italienische Datenschutzbehörde die Poste Italiane und Postepay, Betreiber der Apps BancoPosta und Postepay, nachdem sie 140 Meldungen und 12 Beschwerden erreichten. Die beiden Apps hatten beim Download von den Usern weitgreifende Berechtigungen zum Zugriff auf gespeicherte Daten und andere installierte Anwendungen. Dies wertete die Behörde als überzogenen Eingriff in die Privatsphäre der User. Sie beanstandete auch das Fehlen einer Datenschutz-Folgeabschätzung, unzureichende Information der Betroffenen, die als mangelhaft eingestuften technischen und organisatorischen Maßnahmen der Apps. Darüber hinaus stellte die GPDP Unregelmäßigkeiten im Bezug auf die Benennung der Datenverantwortlichen fest.
LINDDUN categories: Linkability, Identifiability, Non-repudiation, Detectability, Disclosure of information, Unawareness, Non-compliance

Description: Die spanische Datenschutzbehörde reagierte auf eine Meldung eines Sicherheitsvorfalls. MEDIOS DE PREVENCIÓN EXTERNOS SUR war Opfer eines Ransomware-Angriffs geworden, bei dem die Täter Daten stahlen. Die Datenverarbeitung erfolgte ohne angemessene Sicherheitsgarantien, mit denen solche Vorfälle verhindert werden sollten. Nach freiwilliger Zahlung und Haftungsanerkennung wurde das ursprüngliche Bußgeld von 60.000 EUR auf 36.000 EUR heruntergesetzt.

Die spanische Datenschutzbehörde untersuchte eine Beschwerde. Das Kind der Beschwerdeführerin hatte die Webseite des Bußgeldempfängers besucht, woraufhin sie feststellte, dass der Internetauftritt keine Informationen darüber enthielt, ob und inwiefern dieser Cookies speicherte - während jedoch genau das geschah.
Die rumänisch Datenschutzbehörde beantwortete eine Beschwerde. CROWD ENTERTAINMENT LIMITED hatte Werbe-SMS versendet, ohne dass die Empfänger dem Erhalt dieser zugestimmt hätten.

In April 2026, the ultra-luxury hotel brand Aman was named by ShinyHunters as the target of a "pay or leak" extortion campaign, with the data allegedly obtained from their Salesforce CRM. The data was subsequently leaked publicly and contained over 200k unique email addresses. Whilst not present on all records, the data also included genders, physical addresses, phone numbers, nationalities, dates of birth, spouse names and VIP status codes.

In April 2026, the commercial real estate brokerage firm Marcus & Millichap was named as one of multiple alleged victims of the ShinyHunters hacking and extortion group. Data alleged to have been obtained from the company was subsequently released publicly and included 1.8M unique email addresses, along with names, phone numbers and employment-related information including employer, job title and physical company address. In their disclosure notice, Marcus & Millichap advised that data which may have been accessed appeared limited to "company forms, templates, marketing materials, and general contact information".

In April 2026, the gaming community Reborn Gaming suffered a data breach due to a vulnerability in cPanel and WebHost Manager (WHM). The breach exposed 126 unique email addresses along with IP addresses and Steam IDs. Reborn Gaming self-submitted the data to Have I Been Pwned.

In April 2026, the ShinyHunters extortion group listed Vimeo on their extortion portal as part of their "pay or leak" campaign. They subsequently published hundreds of gigabytes of data, predominantly consisting of video titles, technical data and metadata. The data also included 119k unique email addresses, sometimes accompanied by names. Vimeo attributed the exposure to a breach of Anodot, a third-party analytics vendor, and advised the incident does not include "Vimeo video content, valid user login credentials, or payment card information".

In March 2026, the hacker and extortion group "ShinyHunters" claimed to have obtained a substantial corpus of data from ZenBusiness, a business formation and compliance platform. The group claimed the data had been exfiltrated from platforms including Snowflake, Mixpanel and Salesforce, and threatened to publish it if a ransom was not paid. The following month, after claiming payment had not been made, ShinyHunters publicly released the data. The collection amounted to many terabytes across thousands of files that appeared to originate from multiple systems and business functions, including leads, support records and other CRM-related data. The data contained approximately 5M unique email addresses, often accompanied by name and phone number depending on the source file.

Description: An unknown threat actor exploited a critical zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-41940) in the web hosting software cPanel and WebHost Manager (WHM) to target government and military organizations in Southeast Asia, as well as Managed Service Providers (MSPs) and hosting providers in countries including the Philippines, Laos, Canada, South Africa, and the U.S. since Mai 2026. The attackers used the flaw to bypass authentication checks, granting access to the control panel without valid credentials, and potentially allowing them to manage hosting settings, access sensitive data, or take control of the server. The vulnerability was first disclosed by researchers at watchTowr on 29 April 2026. On 2 May, researchers at Ctrl-Alt-Intel detected attacks exploiting CVE-2026-41940 in Southeast Asia and other regions. Among other things, the researchers found stolen map, technical, organisational, and personal information from a railway electrification ecosystem that is closely linked to China’s state rail infrastructure on an exposed attacker server.

The ransomware group Payload carried out a cyberattack on the B3 school cluster in Bruck an der Mur, Styria, Austria, on 23 April 2026, affecting hundreds of pupils and teachers. The group claimed to have obtained 21 GB of data and threatened to publish sensitive information on the darknet. The Styrian Education Directorate refused to negotiate with the attackers and took swift action to resolve the IT outage, with systems rapidly restored and no lasting damage reported. A report was filed with the data protection authority.

A group of hackers linked to China breached the systems of the Cuban Embassy in Washington in January 2026, accessing internal communications of dozens of officials, including Ambassador Lianys Torres Rivera and Deputy Chief of Mission Alejandro Pila, as reported by cybersecurity firm Gambit Security on 30 April 2026. The intruders bypassed embassy security by exploiting two old vulnerabilities in Microsoft Exchange email servers and compromised the emails of 68 officials.

Unknown threat actors hit Columbia Surgical Partners, a surgery center in Maury County with a ransomware attack in April 2026. The attackers compromised patient medical records and made it difficult to access them. The clinic informed it's patients about the attack on 29 April and stated that the clinic was unable to access electronic medical records.
In April 2026, the commercial residential and ISP proxy network LegionProxy suffered a data breach. The incident exposed 10k email addresses, bcrypt password hashes, names and purchases.

In March 2026, the AI-driven merchant data platform Woflow was named as a victim by the ShinyHunters data extortion group. The group subsequently published tens of thousands of files allegedly obtained from the company, comprising more than 2TB of data. The trove included hundreds of thousands of email addresses, names, phone numbers and physical addresses, with the data indicating it related to Woflow customers and, in turn, the customers of merchants using their platform.

Iranian state-sponsored hacking group Handala (aka Handala Hack Team, Hatef) stole 430.000 documents from Fujairah Port in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) on 4 May 2026. The group stole documents concerning contracts, marine traffic, financial information and maps of the port's oil infrastructure and subsequently leaked them on its website. It also released a statement threatening further attacks if the UAE did not cease its support for the United States and Israel. Handala stated it had shared the stolen maps of oil infrastructure with missile units of what it called the “Resistance Axis”. Shortly after the incident, the port was subject of an air attack, which Handala attributed to the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). According to Al Jazeera, the UAE’s Ministry of Defence stated it had engaged ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as drones launched from Iran on 4 May 2026. The cyber incident was reported by News.Az on 5 May 2026.

An unknown threat actor breached US cybersecurity software vendor Trellix giving them unauthorized access to its source code. The actor exploited software development and security infrastructure to place trojans in updates and extensions, which allowed it to steal access credentials and Trellix’ source code. The company said it had notified law enforcement and was working with forensic experts to investigate the incident in a statement on 4 May 2026.

An unknown threat actor targeted San Diego Miramar College on 4 May 2026. The college's IT team identified and stopped the attack, but users faced intermittent disruptions as systems and websites were restored. The attack affected students, employees, and applicants who relied on campus websites and district portals for email, Canvas, class schedules, registration, and other services.

An unknown threat actor breached the servers of the police of City of Ardmore, Oklahoma, deploying ransomware on 7 April 2026. The actor gained unauthorized access via a phishing email. The city did not pay the $300,000 that the threat actor demanded for not leaking the data. The city informed the public about the attack in a social media post on 29 April 2026. In a media statement,  Chief Information Officer Robert Newell stated that the breach was contained within hours, but personal information including names, addresses, and phone numbers may have been exposed for anyone in the police department's database tracing back five years. The city has since upgraded its security and is continuing its investigation.
